\title{Proof-Gap Protocol for Source-Faithful Formalization}
\author{}
\date{2026-05-11}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section{Purpose}

This note fixes terminology for a recurring failure mode in the formalization
of the low individual degree test paper, \path{arXiv:2009.12982}.  It
complements the note-writing policy in \path{docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex} and
the source-statement audit tracked historically in \ghissue{1458}.  The current
source-boundary proof holes are tracked in \ghissue{1507} and \ghissue{422}.
A proof may be blocked at
an intermediate mathematical assertion.  If that assertion is added as a new
hypothesis to a theorem labelled as a paper theorem, the resulting \Lean{}
theorem
may be correct as a conditional statement, but it is no longer the theorem in
the cited source.  The apparent proof has not closed the paper theorem; it has
moved a proof obligation into the theorem statement.

The protocol below distinguishes such proof debt from legitimate formal
boundary conditions and from genuine mathematical corrections.  It is meant for
contributors and reviewers who must decide whether a bridge, residual, repair,
input, or obligation structure is a proved local construction, a tracked proof
gap, or statement drift which must be repaired before a theorem may be
advertised as a source theorem.  The default rule is restrictive: such data
must not be added to a paper-facing theorem unless it is part of the cited
source statement or a documented faithful encoding of its ambient hypotheses.

\section{Basic objects}

\paragraph{Source theorem.}
A source theorem is a theorem, lemma, proposition, or corollary in the paper
source under \path{references/ldt-paper/}.  Its hypotheses and conclusion are
the mathematical ground truth, subject only to faithful formal encoding and to
documented paper-gap corrections.

\paragraph{Paper-facing declaration.}
A \Lean{} declaration is paper-facing when it is named or cited as the
formalization of a source theorem, for instance through a blueprint
\verb|\lean{}| link on a theorem environment carrying a paper label.  Such a
declaration must match the source theorem in its public statement.  In
particular, it may not add an unproved bridge, residual, repair, input,
obligation structure, or other proof-obligation hypothesis which the paper does
not assume.

\paragraph{Proof obligation.}
A proof obligation is an intermediate assertion needed by the proof of a source
theorem.  It may be a construction, an estimate, a transport lemma, or a
comparison between two formal representations.  If the paper proves or invokes
this assertion, then the formalization should state it as a separate lemma or
theorem and prove it from the upstream hypotheses.

\paragraph{Obligation discharger.}
An obligation discharger is a theorem or definition which constructs a proof
obligation from the paper hypotheses already available at that point in the
argument.  This is the preferred representation of missing work.  If the proof
is not yet complete, the discharger may temporarily contain a tracked
\verb|sorry|, but the paper-facing theorem should call it rather than assume
its output as an additional theorem hypothesis.

\paragraph{Conditional helper.}
A conditional helper is a separately named theorem whose statement explicitly
assumes a proof obligation.  Names such as
\leanid{mainFormal\_ofInternalObligations},
\leanid{orthonormalization\_ofInput}, or names whose suffix advertises the
assumed obligation are permitted only when the declaration is not presented as
the source theorem.  A conditional helper is a quarantine for downstream proof
content; it does not close the source theorem.

\section{Bridge, residual, repair, input, and obligation structures}

The words \emph{bridge}, \emph{residual}, \emph{repair}, \emph{input}, and
\emph{obligation structure} name possible formal shapes.  They become dangerous
when their mathematical status is unclear or when their names make unproved
data look like acceptable hypotheses of a source theorem.

\paragraph{Bridge.}
A bridge should be a transport theorem between two already defined
mathematical forms: for example, a tensor-placement identity, a conversion
between two equivalent consistency relations, or a statement translating a
source object into a formal representation.  A bridge is harmless only after it
is proved from previously available assumptions.  It becomes proof debt when it
is assumed because the transport has not yet been proved.  It becomes theorem
drift when the assumed bridge is added to a paper-facing theorem.

\paragraph{Residual.}
A residual is a named remainder after part of an argument has been performed.
It is often a useful way to record the exact missing target after a completed
construction.  A residual may appear as the conclusion of a helper theorem or
as the input of a quarantined conditional helper.  It is not a permissible new
assumption on a paper theorem unless the paper itself assumes that residual.

\paragraph{Input.}
An input is a named bundle of data or hypotheses consumed by a construction or
conditional helper.  It is harmless only when each load-bearing field is either
part of the source hypotheses or is produced by an earlier theorem.  It becomes
proof debt when the bundle is merely assumed because the construction of its
fields is missing.  It becomes theorem drift when such a bundle is added to the
public statement of a source theorem.

\paragraph{Repair.}
A repair is a mathematical construction which replaces an approximate or
partial object by a better object, usually with a quantitative estimate.  In
the low individual degree test formalization, projectivization and
orthonormalization repairs are genuine mathematical operations.  A repair
should therefore appear as a construction or as a theorem discharging the
corresponding obligation.  If a theorem assumes the output of the repair instead
of constructing it, that theorem is conditional on the repair.

\paragraph{Obligation structure.}
An obligation structure is a record whose fields are the data and estimates
needed by a later construction.  This is acceptable only as an internal target
or as a hypothesis of a conditional helper.  Such a structure becomes statement
drift if it is added to a paper-facing theorem instead of being constructed
inside the proof.  The review question is whether every load-bearing field is
proved from the source hypotheses or is explicitly tracked as a missing
obligation.

\section{The main failure mode}

Suppose the paper proves
\[
  H \Longrightarrow C.
\]
During formalization, the proof may need an intermediate assertion \(B\).  The
paper theorem should be represented as
\[
  H \Longrightarrow B \Longrightarrow C
  \quad\text{inside the proof,}
\]
where \(B\) is obtained by a lemma or theorem from \(H\).  The following
public statement is a different theorem:
\[
  H \land B \Longrightarrow C.
\]
It is not unsound in \Lean{}, but it is not the paper theorem.  It says that the
conclusion follows if the missing bridge data is supplied.  Such a theorem is a
conditional helper, even if its conclusion looks exactly like the paper's
conclusion.

This is the situation colloquially described as ``adding a bridge
hypothesis''.  More precisely, an unproved intermediate step has been promoted
from the proof body to the theorem's assumptions.  The correction is not to hide
the hypothesis under a different structure name.  The correction is to keep a
paper-facing theorem with the source statement and move the missing step to a
named internal proof obligation.

\section{Faithful boundary hypotheses}

Not every extra formal hypothesis is a theorem drift.  Some hypotheses are
faithful boundary conditions introduced by formal encoding.  Examples include
nonnegativity needed for a real power, positivity needed to divide by a
quantity, finiteness and nonemptiness of an index type, a field-model instance,
or decidability instances required by \Lean{}.  Such hypotheses are acceptable
when they express part of the mathematical ambient setting or make explicit a
condition used implicitly in the paper.

The distinction is load-bearing.  A faithful boundary hypothesis describes the
domain in which the paper's objects live.  A proof-debt hypothesis supplies a
mathematical step that the proof should derive.  If removing the hypothesis
leaves an unproved construction or estimate from the paper proof, then the
hypothesis is proof debt, not a boundary condition.

\section{Definition drift and subtree repair}

Definition drift is especially dangerous because it propagates.  If a
definition is changed so that it no longer denotes the object in the paper,
then every downstream theorem using that definition may continue to compile
while proving statements about the wrong object.  Downstream theorem statements
can then be repaired piecemeal, but the development remains unstable because
the wrong definition is still upstream.

When a definition mismatch is found, the repair should proceed by a subtree
protocol.

\begin{enumerate}
  \item Identify the source object and the formal object precisely.
  \item Freeze a source-faithful definition or state an adapter theorem
  relating the existing definition to the source object.
  \item Recheck the downstream theorem chain against that definition or adapter.
  \item Re-formalize the affected subtree from the corrected interface, rather
  than adding local hypotheses to each downstream theorem.
  \item If a downstream proof cannot be completed, record the missing obligation
  at the lowest point where the paper proof needs it.
\end{enumerate}

This is slower than editing a final theorem signature, but it prevents a local
definition error from becoming a global theorem-statement error.

\section{Allowed shapes}

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{p{0.24\linewidth}p{0.31\linewidth}p{0.32\linewidth}}
\textbf{Shape} & \textbf{Allowed use} & \textbf{Forbidden use} \\
\hline
Paper-facing theorem & Matches the source statement up to faithful encoding &
Carries non-paper bridge, residual, repair, input, obligation-structure, or
proof-obligation hypotheses \\
Source-shaped theorem with a tracked \verb|sorry| & Default repair when the
source proof is blocked but the statement is known & Replaced by a strengthened
theorem statement merely to keep the file compiling \\
Conditional helper & Temporary quarantine for substantial proof content whose
remaining named obligation has not yet been discharged & Introduced merely to
avoid a \verb|sorry|, or linked as the source theorem or marked as
proof-complete for that theorem \\
Obligation discharger theorem & Constructs the obligation from paper hypotheses &
Merely restates the obligation as an assumption \\
Input bundle & Collects produced data for a local construction & Is assumed by a
source theorem instead of being produced \\
Obligation structure & Bundles constructed data and estimates & Hides unproved
fields that are then assumed by a source theorem \\
Paper-gap note & Documents a real mathematical or formal-statement divergence &
Justifies silent statement drift without a repair plan
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\section{Protocol for a blocked proof}

When a source-labelled proof is blocked, use the following order.

\begin{enumerate}
  \item Read the cited source statement and the proof passage in
  \path{references/ldt-paper/}.
  \item Write the paper theorem form, the current \Lean{} theorem form, and the
  first missing intermediate assertion.
  \item Decide whether the missing assertion is a faithful boundary condition,
  a representation adapter, an ordinary lemma from the paper proof, or a real
  paper-gap discrepancy.
  \item If it is an ordinary lemma or adapter, create a named theorem which
  discharges that obligation.  Do not add it to the source theorem as a new
  hypothesis.
  \item Keep the source-labelled theorem itself in the source form, even if its
  proof must contain a tracked \verb|sorry|.  This is the default repair when
  the missing assertion has not yet been proved.
  \item Create a conditional helper only to quarantine substantial proof content
  that already exists and would otherwise be lost.  Do not create such a helper
  merely to avoid a \verb|sorry| or to keep making progress.  If a conditional
  helper remains, give it a conditional name, keep it separate from the
  paper-facing theorem, and record the obligation discharger that must eliminate
  it.
  \item If the source and formal statements genuinely differ, write or update a
  note under \path{docs/paper-gaps/} before marking the statement as aligned.
  \item Update the blueprint so that paper labels point only to paper-facing
  declarations.  Conditional helpers belong in remarks or implementation
  notes, not in the source theorem block.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Retirement criterion}

An auxiliary declaration should be removed from the main blueprint route, or
renamed and documented as a purely internal lemma, when all three of the
following conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item it is not a statement in the cited paper and is not an explicitly cited
        outside result;
  \item no current proof of a paper-level target needs it as stated;
  \item it assumes stronger proof data, finite-length data, completion data,
        repair data, synchronization data, or package fields than the paper
        proof requires.
\end{enumerate}
If such a declaration is still useful as a formal intermediate result, it
should remain a lemma or a visibly conditional helper with a planned discharge.
It should not be a headline replacement for the paper theorem, and it should
not support a source-labelled blueprint \verb|\leanok| claim.

   397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]
   398	  \label{def:ld-meas}
   399	  Define $\polymeas{m}{d}{q}$ to be the set of POVM measurements whose outcomes
   400	  correspond to (individual) degree-$d$ polynomials of $m$ variables over
   401	  $\F_q$.
   402	  More generally, for an integer $\ldc$ and tuples $m=(m_1, m_2, \ldots,
   403	  m_\ldc)$, $d=(d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_\ldc)$ and $q=(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_\ldc)$,
   404	  we let $\simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}$ be the set of measurements $G =
   405	  \{G_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_\ldc}\}$ such that for $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots,
   406	  \ldc\}$, $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i:\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \rightarrow
   407	  \F_{q_i}$ with individual degree $d_i$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-encoding} for a definition of individual degree).

  1375	\begin{proposition}\label{prop:same-on-point-same-on-subspace}
  1376	Let $d > 0$ be an integer.
  1377	Consider a distribution $\calD$ on pairs $(\bs, \bu)$, where~$\bs$ is a subspace in $\F_q^m$ and~$\bu$ is a uniformly random point in~$\bs$.
  1378	Let $\{M^s_f\}$ be a measurement whose outcomes are degree-$d$ polynomials $f:s \rightarrow \F_q$,
  1379	and let $G \in \polymeas{m}{d}{q}$.
  1380	Suppose that
  1381	\begin{equation*}
  1382	M^s_{[f(u) = b]} \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}} \consistency_\delta I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes G_{[g(u) = b]}
  1383	\end{equation*}
  1384	with respect to~$\calD$. Then
  1385	\begin{equation*}
  1386	M^s_{f} \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}} \consistency_{\delta+d/q} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes G_{[g|_s = f]}
  1387	\end{equation*}
  1388	with respect to~$\calD$.
  1389	\end{proposition}
  1390	\begin{proof}
  1391	Suppose the verifier (i)  samples $(\bs, \bu) \sim \calD$,
  1392	(ii) gives Alice~$\bs$, who measures with $M^{\bs}$ and returns her outcome~$\boldf : \bs \rightarrow \F_q$,
  1393	(iii) receives~$\bg : \F_q^m \rightarrow \F_q$ from Bob, sampled via~$G$,
  1394	and (iv) accepts if $\boldf(\bu) = \bg(\bu)$.
  1395	Then by assumption, the verifier accepts with probability at least $1-O(\delta)$.
  1396	
  1397	We can use this to bound the probability that $\boldf$ and $\bg$ disagree on the subspace~$\bs$.
  1398	By Schwartz-Zippel (\Cref{lem:schwartz-zippel}), conditioned on $\boldf$ and $\bg$ disagreeing,
  1399	the probability they disagree on a random point $\bu \sim \bs$  is at least $1-d/q$.
  1400	This gives us the inequality $\Pr[\boldf \neq \bg|_{\bs}] \cdot (1-d/q) \leq O(\delta)$.
  1401	Now, assume first that $q \geq 2d$. Then this bound implies, via \Cref{fact:agreement}, that
  1402	\begin{equation}\label{eq:almost-there-almost-there}
  1403	M^s_f \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}} \approx_{\delta + d/q} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes G_{[g|_{s} = f]}.
  1404	\end{equation}
  1405	On the other hand, when $q \geq 2d$, then this bound is also true for trivial reasons.
  1406	This is because we can pick $\delta(\cdot)$ such that $\delta(\eps) \geq 1$ in this case.
  1407	\end{proof}

  1416	\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical
  1417	  low-degree test]
  1418	  \label{thm:simultaneous-ldt}
  1419	There exists a constant $c > 0$ and a function $\delta(\eps) = \mathrm{poly}(\epsilon, d (m + \ell)/q^c)$ such that the following holds.
  1420	Suppose Alice and Bob are entangled provers who pass $\game_{\mathrm{Surface}}^\ell(m,d,q,2)$ with probability at least $1-\eps$
  1421	using the strategy $(\psi, M)$, where~$M$ consists of projective measurements.
  1422	Then there exists a measurement $G \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ell}$ such that
  1423	\begin{equation*}
  1424	M^w_{b_1, \ldots, b_\ell} \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}} \consistency_{\delta(\eps)} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes G_{[g_1(w), \ldots, g_\ell(w) = b_1, \ldots, b_\ell]},
  1425	\qquad
  1426	G_{g_1, \ldots, g_\ell} \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}}
  1427	\consistency_{\delta(\eps)}
  1428	I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes G_{g_1, \ldots, g_\ell},
  1429	\end{equation*}
  1430	where the first is on the uniform distribution over $\F_q^m$.
  1431	\end{theorem}
  1432	
  1433	\begin{proof}
  1434	Suppose Alice and Bob pass $\game_{\mathrm{Surface}}^\ell(m, d, q,2)$ with probability at least $1-\eps$.
  1435	We will use them to simulate two provers, ``Combined Alice" and ``Combined Bob", who pass
  1436	the single-function low-degree test $\game_{\mathrm{Surface}}(\ell + m, d+1, q,2)$ with probability at least $1-\eps$.
  1437	They are specified as follows:
  1438	\begin{itemize}
  1439	\item[$\circ$] \textbf{Combined Alice:} Given $\bs \subseteq \F_q^{\ell + m}$, draw $\bs' \sim_2 \bs_{\mathrm{proj}}$.  Give it to Alice, who responds with $\boldf_1, \ldots, \boldf_{\ell}: \bs' \rightarrow \F_q$.  Output the function $\mathrm{combine}_{\boldf}|_{\bs}$.
  1440	\item[$\circ$] \textbf{Combined Bob:} Given $(\bx, \by) \in \F_q^{\ell + m}$, compute $\by \in \F_q^m$. Give it to Bob, who responds with $\bb_1, \ldots, \bb_\ell \in \F_q$.
  1441				Return $\mathrm{combine}_{\bb}(\bx) \in \F_q$.
  1442	\end{itemize}
  1443	By \Cref{prop:really-the-same-dist}, $\bs'$ and $\by$ are distributed as the questions in $\game_{\mathrm{Surface}}^\ell(m, d, q,2)$.
  1444	Using our assumption on Alice and Bob, this means that $\boldf_1(\by) = \bb_1$, \ldots, $\boldf_\ell(\by) = \bb_\ell$ with probability at least $1-\eps$.
  1445	As a result, $(\mathrm{combine}_{\boldf}|_{\bs})(\bx, \by) = \mathrm{combine}_{\bb}(\by)$ with probability at least~$1-\eps$.
  1446	By \Cref{prop:sub-subspace}, $\mathrm{combine}_{\boldf}|_{\bs}$ is a degree-$(d+1)$ function on~$\bs$,
  1447	and so it is a valid response to subspace queries.
  1448	This means Combined Alice and Bob pass~$\game_{\mathrm{Surface}}(\ell + m, d+1, q, 2)$ with probability at least~$1-\eps$.
  1449	
  1450	Thus, we can apply \Cref{thm:anand-thomas-classical-low-degree}.
  1451	It gives a measurement $G \in \polymeas{\ell+m}{d+1}{q}$ such that
  1452	\begin{equation}\label{eq:g-meas-equals-combine-meas}
  1453	M^y_{[\mathrm{combine}_b(x)=\nu]} \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}}
  1454	\consistency_{\delta(\eps)} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes G_{[g(x, y) = \nu]},
  1455	\qquad
  1456	G_g \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}} \consistency_{\delta(\eps)} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes G_g,
  1457	\end{equation}
  1458	where $\delta(\eps) = \poly(\eps, (d+1)(\ell+m)/q^c)$.

  1462	We would like to show that~$\bg$ is exactly linear in~$x$ with high probability, over the randomness in the measurement~$G$.

  1508	\subsection{Self-testing}
  1509	
  1510	The games presented in \Cref{sec:classical-q-low-deg,sec:q-simultaneous} might be referred to as ``measurement testers":
  1511	if a strategy passes them with high probability, then we can extract some property on its measurements.
  1512	In this section, we will introduce a significantly stronger notion of testing called \emph{self-testing}.
  1513	A self-tester is a game in which if a prover passes with high probability,
  1514	then not only do we do exactly which measurements the prover must be performing,
  1515	we also know which exactly state it must be performing them on (up to local isometry).
  1516	(We note that some works use ``self-testing" to refer both to ``measurement testing" and what we refer to as ``self-testing"~\cite{NV18a}.
  1517	In this work, we will reserve the term exclusively for the latter.) We begin with a definition.
  1518	
  1519	\begin{definition}
  1520	We say that $\mathcal{S} = (\psi, M)$ is a \emph{partial strategy} for $\game$
  1521	if $M$ contains the POVM $M^x$ for only a subset of the questions in~$\game$.
  1522	We call this set of questions $\mathcal{S}$'s \emph{question set}.
  1523	A strategy $\mathcal{S}' = (\psi, M')$ \emph{extends} $\mathcal{S}$ if $(M')^x = M^x$ for every~$x$ in $\mathcal{S}$'s question set.
  1524	\end{definition}
  1525	
  1526	Next, we define self-testing.
  1527	
  1528	\begin{definition}[Self-testing]
  1529	Let $\mathcal{S} = (\psi, G)$ be a partial strategy and $\mathcal{D}$ be a distribution over its question set.
  1530	A game $\game$ is a \emph{self-test for $\mathcal{S}$ over $\mathcal{D}$ with robustness $\delta(\epsilon)$}
  1531	if it satisfies the following two conditions.

    50	\section{Key theorem forms}
    51	
    52	The source theorem (\texttt{lem:ld-soundness}) states that for every
    53	projective strategy passing the low individual degree game with parameters
    54	$(q,m,d,k)$ with probability at least $1 - \eps$ there are polynomial-tuple
    55	measurements $G^{\mathrm A}$ and $G^{\mathrm B}$, with outcomes
    56	$(g_1,\dots,g_k)$ of individual degree at most $d$, such that on average over
    57	a uniform point $u \in \F_q^m$
    58	\[
    59	  A^{\mathsf{Point},u}_{a} \ot I \simeq_{\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}}
    60	    I \ot G^{\mathrm B}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = a]},
    61	  \qquad
    62	  G^{\mathrm A}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = a]} \ot I \simeq_{\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}}
    63	    I \ot B^{\mathsf{Point},u}_{a},
    64	  \qquad
    65	  G^{\mathrm A}_{g} \ot I \simeq_{\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}} I \ot G^{\mathrm B}_{g},
    66	  \tag{source form}
    67	\]
    68	where $a = (a_1,\dots,a_k)$ and
    69	$\mathrm{eval}_u(g_1,\dots,g_k) = (g_1(u),\dots,g_k(u))$.
    70	
    71	The formalization planned to derive this from the case $k = 1$ as follows.
    72	Reading the $i$-th coordinate of every answer yields $k$ strategies for the
    73	game with $k = 1$, each passing with probability at least $1 - 3\eps$; the
    74	single-polynomial theorem gives projective measurements $G^{w,i}$ with
    75	\[
    76	  A^{\mathsf{Point},u}_{[a_i]} \ot I \simeq_{\delta}
    77	    I \ot G^{\mathrm B,i}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = a_i]},
    78	  \qquad
    79	  G^{\mathrm A,i}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = a_i]} \ot I \simeq_{\delta}
    80	    I \ot B^{\mathsf{Point},u}_{[a_i]},
    81	  \qquad
    82	  G^{\mathrm A,i}_{g} \ot I \simeq_{\delta} I \ot G^{\mathrm B,i}_{g},
    83	  \tag{coordinate form}
    84	\]
    85	where $A^{\mathsf{Point},u}_{[a_i]}$ is the $i$-th marginal of the joint
    86	point measurement; and the planned combination was the sandwich
    87	\[
    88	  C^{w}_{g_1,\dots,g_k}
    89	    = G^{w,k}_{g_k} \cdots G^{w,2}_{g_2}\, G^{w,1}_{g_1}\,
    90	      G^{w,2}_{g_2} \cdots G^{w,k}_{g_k},
    91	  \qquad
    92	  A^{\mathsf{Point},u}_{a} \ot I \simeq_{C k (\delta + md/q)^{1/2}}
    93	    I \ot C^{\mathrm B}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = a]},
    94	  \tag{planned form}
    95	\]
    96	with a universal constant $C$, and likewise on the other side and for the
    97	global relation.  We show that no statement of the planned form holds: the
    98	coordinate form, even with $\delta = 0$ and even with both point
    99	measurements and all $2k$ polynomial measurements available, does not
   100	determine any polynomial-tuple measurement consistent with the joint point
   101	measurement.
   102	
   103	The formalization proves the source form for every $k$, for the directly
   104	indexed low-degree game of \cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility} and by the
   105	source reduction rather than by the refuted route.  From a projective strategy for the
   106	directly indexed low-degree game with parameters $(q,m,d,k)$ succeeding with
   107	probability at least $1 - \eps$ it produces polynomial-tuple measurements
   108	satisfying the three relations of the source form with the error of the low
   109	individual degree theorem at the combined parameters $(q, m+k, d, 1)$, at the
   110	auxiliary parameter $2560000\,(m+k)^{3}d$ and pass bound $30\eps$, increased by
   111	the recovery loss $(m+k)d/q$ on the two point/polynomial relations;%
   112	\footnote{The declaration is
   113	\leanid{exists\_directSimultaneousPolynomialMeasurements\_combinedError} in
   114	\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/Combining/SimultaneousGeneral.lean}.}
   115	and, absorbing that error, the same three relations with the error function
   116	$\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}(\eps,q,m,d,k)$ of the source statement at the universal
   117	constants $a = 10^{23}$ and $b = 1/80000$.%
   118	\footnote{The declaration is \leanid{exists\_direct\_ld\_soundness} in
   119	\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Soundness.lean}.  The case
   120	$k = 1$, the only one instantiated by the Pauli basis test analysis, remains
   121	available separately as
   122	\leanid{exists\_directSimultaneousPolynomialMeasurements\_of\_k\_eq\_one}
   123	in \doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/Simultaneous.lean};
   124	the instantiation with $k = 1$ at dimension $2m+2$ is in the proof of
   125	\texttt{lem:qld-4-7}, \path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex}.}
   126	
   127	The route is the source's: the combined strategy answers each question of the
   128	game at the combined parameters by measuring one question of the original
   129	strategy and relabeling its outcome, its success probability is at least
   130	$1 - 10\eps$, the case $k = 1$ is applied once to it, and the $k$ polynomials
   131	are recovered from the single outcome polynomial by exact linearity in the
   132	fresh coordinates.  Two quantitative points differ from the account of the
   133	source assertion below, and both are forced by the individual-degree
   134	formulation of the game.  The degree does not rise to $d + 1$: the combined
   135	polynomial $(u,\alpha) \mapsto \sum_r \alpha_r g_r(u)$ has individual degree
   136	at most $d$ in each of the $m + k$ variables, so the theorem is applied at
   137	degree $d$ and its error function is evaluated there.  Correspondingly the
   138	recovery cost is not $(d+1)/q$ taken twice but $(m+k)d/q$: the exact-linearity
   139	test on the point space contributes $md/q$, and the collision of two distinct
   140	tuples at the sampled point contributes $kd/q$.  A reader comparing the two
   141	accounts should read the displayed recovery term of the source assertion as
   142	$(m+k)d/q$ throughout.

   144	\section{The source assertion}
   145	
   146	The proof of \texttt{lem:ld-soundness} in
   147	\cite[lines~413--458]{Ji2020MIPStar} treats $k = 1$ by an identification
   148	with the tensor-code test of \cite{Ji2021Quantum} (the identification is
   149	examined in \path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex}) and
   150	then extends to general $k$ by reference to the derivation of Theorem~4.43
   151	from Theorem~4.40 in \cite[lines~1409--1503]{Natarajan2018NEEXP}.  That
   152	derivation is not coordinatewise.  It builds two combined provers who play
   153	the single-polynomial test in $m + k$ variables at degree $d + 1$: on a
   154	point $(\alpha, u)$ the combined prover asks the original prover for the $k$
   155	values $(b_1,\dots,b_k)$ at $u$ and returns $\sum_i \alpha_i b_i$, and on a
   156	line it returns the corresponding combination of the $k$ answer polynomials.
   157	The degree rises by one because the combination
   158	$(\alpha, u) \mapsto \sum_i \alpha_i g_i(u)$ is linear in $\alpha$ and of
   159	degree $d$ in $u$, so its restriction to a queried subspace has degree
   160	$d + 1$; the single-polynomial theorem is therefore applied at degree $d + 1$
   161	and its error function is evaluated there.  That theorem then yields one
   162	measurement with outcomes $g(\alpha,u)$, and the $k$ polynomials are
   163	recovered from $g$ because $g$ is exactly linear in $\alpha$ with high
   164	probability, by the Schwartz--Zippel lemma; applied at degree $d + 1$, that
   165	lemma contributes the term $(d+1)/q$ twice in the recovery.  The
   166	simultaneity of the $k$ outputs is thus inherited from the joint answers of
   167	the original provers through a single application of the $k = 1$ theorem.

   169	\section{The counterexample}
   170	
   171	Let $q = 2^s$, let $d = 1$, and let $\Gamma$ be the set of univariate
   172	polynomials $g = g_0 + g_1 x$ over $\F_q$, so $|\Gamma| = N = q^2$.  Two
   173	distinct elements of $\Gamma$ agree at a uniformly random point of $\F_q$
   174	with probability at most $1/q$.  Bob's Hilbert space is $\C^{\Gamma}$ with
   175	standard basis $\{\ket{g}\}$; Alice's is a second copy, and the state is
   176	the maximally entangled state
   177	$\ket{\psi} = N^{-1/2} \sum_{g \in \Gamma} \ket{g}\ket{g}$, for which
   178	$(X \ot I)\ket{\psi} = (I \ot X^{\mathsf T})\ket{\psi}$ and
   179	$\bra{\psi} X \ot Y \ket{\psi} = N^{-1}\tr(X Y^{\mathsf T})$.
   180	
   181	Equip $\Gamma \cong \F_q^2$ with the symmetric pairing
   182	$\langle h, g\rangle = h_0 g_1 + h_1 g_0$ and the additive character
   183	$\chi(t) = (-1)^{\mathrm{tr}(t)}$, where $\mathrm{tr}$ is the absolute
   184	trace of $\F_q$; the pairing is nondegenerate, so
   185	$\phi_h = N^{-1/2} \sum_{g} \chi(\langle h, g\rangle)\ket{g}$, $h \in \Gamma$,
   186	is an orthonormal basis.  Evaluation at $u \in \F_q$ is represented by the
   187	vector $v_u = u + x$, since $\langle h, v_u\rangle = h_0 + h_1 u = h(u)$, and
   188	$\langle v_u, v_u\rangle = 2u = 0$ in characteristic two.  Bob's two
   189	coordinate measurements are
   190	\[
   191	  G^{1}_h = \ket{\phi_h}\bra{\phi_h},
   192	  \qquad
   193	  G^{2}_g = \ket{g}\bra{g},
   194	  \qquad
   195	  Q^{1,u}_{[a]} = \sum_{h(u) = a} G^1_h,
   196	  \qquad
   197	  Q^{2,u}_{[b]} = \sum_{g(u) = b} G^2_g .
   198	\]
   199	Writing $H_u = \{h : h(u) = 0\} = \F_q v_u$ and summing the character over
   200	the coset $\{h : h(u) = a\}$ gives the matrix elements
   201	\[
   202	  \bra{g'} Q^{1,u}_{[a]} \ket{g}
   203	    = \frac1N \sum_{h(u) = a} \chi(\langle h, g - g'\rangle)
   204	    = \frac{1}{q}\, \chi(\langle h_a, g - g'\rangle)\,
   205	      \mathbf 1[\,g(u) = g'(u)\,],
   206	\]
   207	where $h_a$ is any polynomial with $h_a(u) = a$: the sum over
   208	$H_u = \F_q v_u$ vanishes unless $\langle v_u, g - g'\rangle = 0$, that is,
   209	unless $g(u) = g'(u)$, because $v_u$ is isotropic.  Hence $Q^{1,u}_{[a]}$
   210	is block diagonal for the partition of $\Gamma$ by the value at $u$, it
   211	commutes with every $Q^{2,u}_{[b]}$, its diagonal entries all equal $1/q$,
   212	and each product $\Pi^u_{a,b} = Q^{1,u}_{[a]} Q^{2,u}_{[b]}$ is the rank-one
   213	projector onto the unit vector
   214	$\xi^u_{a,b} = q^{-1/2} \sum_{g(u) = b} \chi(\langle h_a, g\rangle)\ket{g}$.
   215	
   216	Let both players answer the point question $u$ with the joint projective
   217	measurement $\{\Pi^u_{a,b}\}_{a,b}$, which is real symmetric, and let Alice's
   218	coordinate polynomial measurements be the transposes $(G^{i})^{\mathsf T}$.
   219	On $\ket{\psi}$ every relation of the coordinate form holds with error
   220	$0$: the marginals of the joint point measurement are $Q^{1,u}_{[a]}$ and
   221	$Q^{2,u}_{[b]}$, which are exactly the evaluated coordinate measurements, and
   222	$(G^i)^{\mathsf T} \ot I$ agrees with $I \ot G^i$ on $\ket{\psi}$.  The
   223	collision probability is $1/q$.  The sandwich on Bob's side, evaluated at
   224	$u$, is
   225	\[
   226	  C^{\mathrm B}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = (a,b)]}
   227	    = \sum_{g(u) = b} \ket{g}\bra{g}\, Q^{1,u}_{[a]}\, \ket{g}\bra{g}
   228	    = \frac1q\, Q^{2,u}_{[b]},
   229	\]
   230	and its consistency with the joint point measurement is
   231	\[
   232	  \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} \Pi^u_{a,b} \ot C^{\mathrm B}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = (a,b)]}

   234	    = \frac{1}{qN} \sum_{a,b} \tr\bigl(Q^{1,u}_{[a]} Q^{2,u}_{[b]}\bigr)

1390	\begin{proof}
  1391	Suppose the verifier (i)  samples $(\bs, \bu) \sim \calD$,
  1392	(ii) gives Alice~$\bs$, who measures with $M^{\bs}$ and returns her outcome~$\boldf : \bs \rightarrow \F_q$,
  1393	(iii) receives~$\bg : \F_q^m \rightarrow \F_q$ from Bob, sampled via~$G$,
  1394	and (iv) accepts if $\boldf(\bu) = \bg(\bu)$.
  1395	Then by assumption, the verifier accepts with probability at least $1-O(\delta)$.
  1396	
  1397	We can use this to bound the probability that $\boldf$ and $\bg$ disagree on the subspace~$\bs$.
  1398	By Schwartz-Zippel (\Cref{lem:schwartz-zippel}), conditioned on $\boldf$ and $\bg$ disagreeing,
  1399	the probability they disagree on a random point $\bu \sim \bs$  is at least $1-d/q$.
  1400	This gives us the inequality $\Pr[\boldf \neq \bg|_{\bs}] \cdot (1-d/q) \leq O(\delta)$.
  1401	Now, assume first that $q \geq 2d$. Then this bound implies, via \Cref{fact:agreement}, that
  1402	\begin{equation}\label{eq:almost-there-almost-there}
  1403	M^s_f \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}} \approx_{\delta + d/q} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes G_{[g|_{s} = f]}.
  1404	\end{equation}
  1405	On the other hand, when $q \geq 2d$, then this bound is also true for trivial reasons.
  1406	This is because we can pick $\delta(\cdot)$ such that $\delta(\eps) \geq 1$ in this case.
  1407	\end{proof}

  1409	\subsection{Quantum soundness of the classical simultaneous low-degree test}\label{sec:q-simultaneous}
  1410	
  1411	We would now like to use \Cref{thm:anand-thomas-classical-low-degree}
  1412	to show quantum soundness for the simultaneous classical low-degree test.
  1413	This will be done using the same reduction presented in~\Cref{sec:simultaneous-classical}.
  1414	The main result is the following.
  1415	
  1416	\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical
  1417	  low-degree test]
  1418	  \label{thm:simultaneous-ldt}
  1419	There exists a constant $c > 0$ and a function $\delta(\eps) = \mathrm{poly}(\epsilon, d (m + \ell)/q^c)$ such that the following holds.
  1420	Suppose Alice and Bob are entangled provers who pass $\game_{\mathrm{Surface}}^\ell(m,d,q,2)$ with probability at least $1-\eps$
  1421	using the strategy $(\psi, M)$, where~$M$ consists of projective measurements.
  1422	Then there exists a measurement $G \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ell}$ such that
  1423	\begin{equation*}
  1424	M^w_{b_1, \ldots, b_\ell} \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}} \consistency_{\delta(\eps)} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes G_{[g_1(w), \ldots, g_\ell(w) = b_1, \ldots, b_\ell]},
  1425	\qquad
  1426	G_{g_1, \ldots, g_\ell} \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}}
  1427	\consistency_{\delta(\eps)}
  1428	I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes G_{g_1, \ldots, g_\ell},
  1429	\end{equation*}
  1430	where the first is on the uniform distribution over $\F_q^m$.
  1431	\end{theorem}
  1432	
  1433	\begin{proof}
  1434	Suppose Alice and Bob pass $\game_{\mathrm{Surface}}^\ell(m, d, q,2)$ with probability at least $1-\eps$.
  1435	We will use them to simulate two provers, ``Combined Alice" and ``Combined Bob", who pass
  1436	the single-function low-degree test $\game_{\mathrm{Surface}}(\ell + m, d+1, q,2)$ with probability at least $1-\eps$.
  1437	They are specified as follows:
  1438	\begin{itemize}
  1439	\item[$\circ$] \textbf{Combined Alice:} Given $\bs \subseteq \F_q^{\ell + m}$, draw $\bs' \sim_2 \bs_{\mathrm{proj}}$.  Give it to Alice, who responds with $\boldf_1, \ldots, \boldf_{\ell}: \bs' \rightarrow \F_q$.  Output the function $\mathrm{combine}_{\boldf}|_{\bs}$.
  1440	\item[$\circ$] \textbf{Combined Bob:} Given $(\bx, \by) \in \F_q^{\ell + m}$, compute $\by \in \F_q^m$. Give it to Bob, who responds with $\bb_1, \ldots, \bb_\ell \in \F_q$.
  1441				Return $\mathrm{combine}_{\bb}(\bx) \in \F_q$.
  1442	\end{itemize}
  1443	By \Cref{prop:really-the-same-dist}, $\bs'$ and $\by$ are distributed as the questions in $\game_{\mathrm{Surface}}^\ell(m, d, q,2)$.
  1444	Using our assumption on Alice and Bob, this means that $\boldf_1(\by) = \bb_1$, \ldots, $\boldf_\ell(\by) = \bb_\ell$ with probability at least $1-\eps$.
  1445	As a result, $(\mathrm{combine}_{\boldf}|_{\bs})(\bx, \by) = \mathrm{combine}_{\bb}(\by)$ with probability at least~$1-\eps$.
  1446	By \Cref{prop:sub-subspace}, $\mathrm{combine}_{\boldf}|_{\bs}$ is a degree-$(d+1)$ function on~$\bs$,
  1447	and so it is a valid response to subspace queries.
  1448	This means Combined Alice and Bob pass~$\game_{\mathrm{Surface}}(\ell + m, d+1, q, 2)$ with probability at least~$1-\eps$.
  1449	
  1450	Thus, we can apply \Cref{thm:anand-thomas-classical-low-degree}.
  1451	It gives a measurement $G \in \polymeas{\ell+m}{d+1}{q}$ such that
  1452	\begin{equation}\label{eq:g-meas-equals-combine-meas}
  1453	M^y_{[\mathrm{combine}_b(x)=\nu]} \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}}
  1454	\consistency_{\delta(\eps)} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes G_{[g(x, y) = \nu]},
  1455	\qquad
  1456	G_g \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}} \consistency_{\delta(\eps)} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes G_g,
  1457	\end{equation}
  1458	where $\delta(\eps) = \poly(\eps, (d+1)(\ell+m)/q^c)$.
  1459	This means that if we give Alice~$\by$ and she returns~$\bb$, and Bob simply returns~$\bg$,
  1460	then $\mathrm{combine}_{\bb}(\bx) = g(\bx, \by)$ with probability at least~$1-\delta(\eps)$.
  1461	
  1462	We would like to show that~$\bg$ is exactly linear in~$x$ with high probability, over the randomness in the measurement~$G$.
  1463	Let us condition on a $\bg$ which is not exactly linear.
  1464	By \Cref{prop:exactly-linear-prop}, the probability that $\bg|_{\by}$ is not exactly linear is at least $1-(d+1)/q$.
  1465	On the other hand, because $\mathrm{combine}_{\bb}(\bx)$ is always exactly linear by construction,
  1466	the probability that $\bg|_{\by}(\bx) = \mathrm{combine}_{\bb}(\bx)$ is at most $(d+1)/q$ by Schwartz-Zippel (\Cref{lem:schwartz-zippel}).
  1467	As a result, the probability that $\bg(\bx, \by) = \mathrm{combine}_{\bb}(\bx)$ is at most $(d+1)/q + (d+1)/q$.
  1468	Thus, if we write $\mu_{\mathrm{linear}}$ for the probability that $\bg$ is exactly linear, we have equality at most $\mu_{\mathrm{linear}} + 2(d+1)/q$ fraction of the time.
  1469	Rearranging, $\bg$ is exactly linear with probability
  1470	\begin{equation*}
  1471	\mu_{\mathrm{linear}} \geq 1 - 2\delta(\eps) - 2(d+1)/q.
  1472	\end{equation*}
  1473	Define a new measurement $\{H_{g_1, \ldots, g_\ell}\} \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ell}$ operationally as follows: first, measure~$G$ and receive~$\bg$.
  1474	If it is exactly linear, it can be written as $\sum_i x_i \cdot \bg_i(y)$, and so output $\bg_1, \ldots, \bg_\ell$.
  1475	If~$\bg$ is \emph{not} exactly linear, output any arbitrary degree-$d$ polynomials instead.
  1476	When~$\bg$ is exactly linear, we have $\mathrm{combine}_{\bg_1, \ldots, \bg_\ell}(x, y) = \bg(x, y)$.
  1477	Since this happens with probability at least $1-\delta(\eps)$,
  1478	we can replace~$G$ with~$H$ in \Cref{eq:g-meas-equals-combine-meas}, yielding
  1479	\begin{equation}\label{eq:no-name-is-a-bad-name}
  1480	M^y_{[\mathrm{combine}_b(x)=\nu]} \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}}
  1481	\consistency_{\delta(\eps)} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes H_{[\mathrm{combine}_g(x, y) = \nu]},
  1482	\end{equation}
  1483	On the other hand, because~$H$ is just~$G$ with data processing applied to its output,
  1484	we can apply \Cref{fact:specialize-the-simeq} to \Cref{eq:g-meas-equals-combine-meas}. This produces the equation
  1485	\begin{equation*}
  1486	H_{g_1, \ldots, g_\ell} \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}} \consistency_{\delta(\eps)} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes H_{g_1, \ldots, g_\ell}.
  1487	\end{equation*}
  1488	
  1489	Consider $\bg_1, \ldots, \bg_\ell$ drawn by Bob using~$H$.
  1490	For any fixed~$b$ and~$y$, if it is not the case that $g_1(y) = b_1$, \ldots, $g_\ell(y) = b_\ell$,
  1491	then the probability that $\mathrm{combine}_{\bg}(\bx, y) = \mathrm{combine}_{b}(\bx)$
  1492	over a random~$\bx$ is at most $1/q$ by Schwartz-Zippel, since both are exactly linear functions.
  1493	Thus, if Alice draws~$\bb_1, \ldots, \bb_\ell$ given~$\by$,
  1494	and we write~$\eta$ for the probability that $\bg_1(\by) = \bb_1$, \ldots, $\bg_\ell(\by) = \bb_\ell$,
  1495	then the probability that $\mathrm{combine}_{\bg}(\bx, \by) = \mathrm{combine}_{\bb}(\bx)$ is at most
  1496	$\eta +  (1-\eta) \cdot 1/q$.
  1497	Combined with \Cref{eq:no-name-is-a-bad-name}, this implies that
  1498	\begin{equation*}
  1499	\Pr[\bg_1(\by) = \bb_1, \ldots, \bg_\ell(\by) = \bb_\ell] \geq 1- \delta(\eps) - 1/q.
  1500	\end{equation*}
  1501	Or, equivalently,
  1502	\begin{equation*}
  1503	M^y_{b_1, \ldots, b_\ell} \otimes I_{\reg{Bob}}
  1504	\consistency_{\delta(\eps)} I_{\reg{Alice}} \otimes G_{[g_1(y), \ldots, g_\ell(y) = b_1, \ldots, b_\ell]}.\qedhere
  1505	\end{equation*}
  1506	\end{proof}

  1508	\subsection{Self-testing}
  1509	
  1510	The games presented in \Cref{sec:classical-q-low-deg,sec:q-simultaneous} might be referred to as ``measurement testers":
  1511	if a strategy passes them with high probability, then we can extract some property on its measurements.
  1512	In this section, we will introduce a significantly stronger notion of testing called \emph{self-testing}.
  1513	A self-tester is a game in which if a prover passes with high probability,
  1514	then not only do we do exactly which measurements the prover must be performing,

   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test.    421	  \[G^w \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}\] on $\mH_w$, for

   425	      A^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}

   443	Let $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$
   444	where $m, d, \ldc \in \N$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size,
   445	and $m$ divides $q$. Let $\Sigma=\F_q$. Let $\code \subseteq \Sigma^q$ be the Reed-Solomon code with degree $d$. Explicitly, $\code$ is the set of all $(p(x_1),\ldots,p(x_n))$ where $p:\F_q\to\F_q$ is a univariate polynomial of degree at most $d$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ are an enumeration of $\F_q$.    448	\begin{enumerate}
   449	\item The \emph{axis-parallel line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{axis-parallel lines test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with the only difference that in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} the roles of A and B are chosen uniformly at random.    450	\item The \emph{diagonal line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{subcube commutation test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with again the added symmetrization between players. 
   451	\item The \emph{consistency test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{synchronicity test} from~\cite[Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}.
   452	\end{enumerate}

   454	As a result,~\cite[Theorem 4.7]{ji2021quantum}, in which we choose the parameter $k$ as $k=m^3d$,  immediately yields \Cref{lem:ld-soundness}.

   457	via a standard reduction, following exactly the same steps as the derivation of Theorem 4.43 from Theorem 4.40 in~\cite{NW19}.
   458	\end{proof}

  1508	\subsection{Self-testing}
  1509	
  1510	The games presented in \Cref{sec:classical-q-low-deg,sec:q-simultaneous} might be referred to as ``measurement testers":
  1511	if a strategy passes them with high probability, then we can extract some property on its measurements.
  1512	In this section, we will introduce a significantly stronger notion of testing called \emph{self-testing}.
  1513	A self-tester is a game in which if a prover passes with high probability,
  1514	then not only do we do exactly which measurements the prover must be performing,
  1515	we also know which exactly state it must be performing them on (up to local isometry).
  1516	(We note that some works use ``self-testing" to refer both to ``measurement testing" and what we refer to as ``self-testing"~\cite{NV18a}.
  1517	In this work, we will reserve the term exclusively for the latter.) We begin with a definition.

    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    24	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    25	open MIPStarRE.Quantum

    27	noncomputable section
    28	
    29	/-- Parameters for the directly indexed low-degree game.  Unlike `LdParams`,
    30	this directly indexed line-space construction has no divisibility field: its coordinate index is
    31	sampled from `Fin m` rather than encoded by fibers of `chiIndex`.
    32	
    33	This is the direct-index repair described in
    34	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`; it is not a second
    35	definition of the source verifier game. -/
    36	structure DirectLdParams where
    37	  q : ℕ
    38	  m : ℕ
    39	  d : ℕ
    40	  k : ℕ
    41	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    42	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    43	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    44	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    45	
    46	/-- The canonical scalar model for directly indexed parameters. -/
    47	noncomputable def DirectLdParams.model (D : DirectLdParams) : FixedFieldModel D.q :=
    48	  fixedFieldModel D.q D.hq
    49	
    50	/-- The scalar field of a directly indexed low-degree game. -/
    51	abbrev DirectScalarQ (D : DirectLdParams) := D.model.K
    52	
    53	/-- The first coordinate, available because directly indexed dimensions are
    54	positive. -/
    55	def DirectLdParams.firstIndex (D : DirectLdParams) : Fin D.m :=
    56	  ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one D.hm⟩
    57	
    58	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Nonempty (Fin D.m) := ⟨D.firstIndex⟩
    59	
    60	/-- The direct game used at the extended dimension of the combining map.  Its
    61	field, degree, and simultaneity parameters are inherited from `P`, while its
    62	dimension is `2 * P.m + 2`; no divisibility assertion is introduced.
    63	
    64	The construction has dimension `2 * P.m + 2` without requiring
    65	`2 * P.m + 2 ∣ P.q`; it supplies the directly indexed line and coordinate
    66	spaces used in the dimension-extension argument of
    67	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1257-1293`.
    68	-/
    69	def AdmissibleParams.extendedDirectLd (P : AdmissibleParams) : DirectLdParams where
    70	  q := P.q
    71	  m := 2 * P.m + 2
    72	  d := P.d
    73	  k := 1
    74	  hm := by omega
    75	  hd := P.hd
    76	  hk := by decide
    77	  hq := P.hq
    78	
    79	/-- A common random sample for the directly indexed question distribution.
    80	The point, coordinate index, and unrestricted direction are mutually uniform. -/
    81	structure DirectLdSpace (D : DirectLdParams) where
    82	  point : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
    83	  index : Fin D.m
    84	  direction : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
    85	  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype
    86	
    87	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Nonempty (DirectLdSpace D) :=
    88	  ⟨⟨0, D.firstIndex, 0⟩⟩
    89	
    90	/-- Decompose a direct sample into its point and the remaining independent
    91	coordinates. -/
    92	private def directLdSpacePointEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
    93	    DirectLdSpace D ≃
    94	      (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ×
    95	        (Fin D.m × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) where
    96	  toFun sample := (sample.point, sample.index, sample.direction)
    97	  invFun sample := ⟨sample.1, sample.2.1, sample.2.2⟩
    98	  left_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
    99	  right_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
   100	
   101	/-- Decompose a direct sample into its stored index and the remaining
   102	independent coordinates. -/
   103	def directLdSpaceIndexEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   104	    DirectLdSpace D ≃
   105	      Fin D.m ×
   106	        ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ×
   107	          (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) where
   108	  toFun sample := (sample.index, sample.point, sample.direction)
   109	  invFun sample := ⟨sample.2.1, sample.1, sample.2.2⟩
   110	  left_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
   111	  right_inv sample := by cases sample; rfl
   112	
   113	/-- Compatibility name for the index-first direct-sample decomposition. -/
   114	abbrev directLdSpaceIndexSplitEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   115	    DirectLdSpace D ≃
   116	      Fin D.m × ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) :=
   117	  directLdSpaceIndexEquiv D
   118	
   119	/-- Zero the coordinates preceding the directly sampled prefix index. -/
   120	def directPrefixProjection {D : DirectLdParams} (i : Fin D.m)
   121	    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D :=
   122	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   123	
   124	/-- Zeroing the coordinates preceding a prefix index is idempotent: the
   125	coordinates it leaves unchanged are exactly those it does not zero. -/
   126	theorem directPrefixProjection_idem (D : DirectLdParams) (i : Fin D.m)
   127	    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
   128	    directPrefixProjection i (directPrefixProjection i v) =
   129	      directPrefixProjection i v := by
   130	  funext j
   131	  unfold directPrefixProjection
   132	  split_ifs <;> rfl
   133	
   134	/-- Canonical line descriptions whose coordinate index is stored directly.
   135	Coordinates are numbered from zero, so `index = i` represents coordinate
   136	`i + 1` in the paper. -/
   137	inductive DirectLineDesc (D : DirectLdParams) where
   138	  | axis (base : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (index : Fin D.m)
   139	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap (coordinateDirection index) base = base)
   140	  | diagonal (base : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (index : Fin D.m)
   141	      (direction : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
   142	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap direction base = base)
   143	      (prefixZero : ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < index.val → direction j = 0)
   144	  deriving DecidableEq
   145	
   146	/-- The kind of a directly indexed line. -/
   147	def DirectLineDesc.kind {D : DirectLdParams} : DirectLineDesc D → LineKind
   148	  | .axis _ _ _ => .axis
   149	  | .diagonal _ _ _ _ _ => .diagonal
   150	
   151	/-- The coordinate index stored in a directly indexed line. -/
   152	def DirectLineDesc.index {D : DirectLdParams} : DirectLineDesc D → Fin D.m
   153	  | .axis _ index _ => index
   154	  | .diagonal _ index _ _ _ => index
   155	
   156	/-- The canonical base point of a directly indexed line. -/
   157	def DirectLineDesc.base {D : DirectLdParams} :
   158	    DirectLineDesc D → Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
   159	  | .axis base _ _ => base
   160	  | .diagonal base _ _ _ _ => base
   161	
   162	/-- The geometric direction of a directly indexed line. -/
   163	def DirectLineDesc.direction {D : DirectLdParams} (line : DirectLineDesc D) :
   164	    Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D :=
   165	  match line with
   166	  | .axis _ index _ => coordinateDirection index
   167	  | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction
   168	
   169	/-- The base of a directly indexed description is fixed by its geometric
   170	direction. -/
   171	theorem DirectLineDesc.base_fixed {D : DirectLdParams} (line : DirectLineDesc D) :
   172	    lineRepMap line.direction line.base = line.base := by
   173	  cases line with
   174	  | axis base index baseFixed => exact baseFixed
   175	  | diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact baseFixed
   176	
   177	/-- Every directly indexed diagonal description retains its prefix-zero
   178	invariant. -/
   179	theorem DirectLineDesc.diagonal_prefix_zero {D : DirectLdParams}
   180	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) (hline : line.kind = .diagonal) :
   181	    ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < line.index.val → line.direction j = 0 := by
   182	  cases line with
   183	  | axis base index baseFixed => simp [DirectLineDesc.kind] at hline
   184	  | diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact prefixZero
   185	
   186	/-- The point set represented by a directly indexed line. -/
   187	noncomputable def DirectLineDesc.pointSet {D : DirectLdParams}
   188	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) : Set (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :=
   189	  linePoints line.base line.direction
   190	
   191	/-- Turn a direct sample into its canonical axis-line description. -/
   192	noncomputable def directALineDescOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   193	    (sample : DirectLdSpace D) : DirectLineDesc D :=
   194	  let direction := coordinateDirection sample.index
   195	  let base := lineRepMap direction sample.point
   196	  .axis base sample.index (lineRepMap_apply_self direction sample.point)
   197	
   198	/-- Turn a direct sample into its canonical diagonal-line description. -/
   199	noncomputable def directDLineDescOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   200	    (sample : DirectLdSpace D) : DirectLineDesc D :=
   201	  let direction := directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction
   202	  let base := lineRepMap direction sample.point
   203	  .diagonal base sample.index direction
   204	    (lineRepMap_apply_self direction sample.point) (by
   205	      intro j hj
   206	      change directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction j = 0
   207	      rw [directPrefixProjection, if_pos hj])
   208	
   209	/-- The axis-line/point law with a directly sampled coordinate index. -/
   210	noncomputable def directALinePointDist (D : DirectLdParams) :
   211	    Distribution (DirectLineDesc D × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) :=
   212	  (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>
   213	    (directALineDescOf D sample, sample.point)
   214	
   215	/-- The diagonal-line/point law with a directly sampled prefix index. -/
   216	noncomputable def directDLinePointDist (D : DirectLdParams) :
   217	    Distribution (DirectLineDesc D × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) :=
   218	  (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>
   219	    (directDLineDescOf D sample, sample.point)
   220	
   221	/-- The equal mixture of the directly indexed axis and diagonal line-point
   222	laws.  This is the replacement for the otherwise undefined extended-dimension
   223	instance used at paper
   224	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1020-1116`. -/
   225	noncomputable def directLinePointDist (D : DirectLdParams) :
   226	    Distribution (DirectLineDesc D × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) :=
   227	  Distribution.mix (1 / 2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   228	    (directALinePointDist D) (directDLinePointDist D)
   229	
   230	/-- The directly indexed axis-line/point law is probabilistic. -/
   231	theorem directALinePointDist_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :
   232	    (directALinePointDist D).IsProbability := by
   233	  exact (uniformDistribution_isProbability (DirectLdSpace D)).map _
   234	
   235	/-- The directly indexed diagonal-line/point law is probabilistic. -/
   236	theorem directDLinePointDist_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :
   237	    (directDLinePointDist D).IsProbability := by
   238	  exact (uniformDistribution_isProbability (DirectLdSpace D)).map _
   239	
   240	/-- The directly indexed line-point mixture is probabilistic. -/
   241	theorem directLinePointDist_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :
   242	    (directLinePointDist D).IsProbability := by
   243	  exact Distribution.mix_isProbability _ _ _
   244	    (directALinePointDist_isProbability D) (directDLinePointDist_isProbability D)
   245	    (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   246	
   247	/-- The point and stored-index marginals of the direct axis-line law are
   248	uniform.  This is a direct-index analogue of `lem:alnf`, required by
   249	the repair described in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`;
   250	the source distribution is at
   251	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257`.
   252	-/
   253	theorem directALinePointDist_point_index_marginal_uniform (D : DirectLdParams) :
   254	    (directALinePointDist D).map Prod.snd =
   255	        uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ∧
   256	      (directALinePointDist D).map (fun sample => sample.1.index) =
   257	        uniformDistribution (Fin D.m) := by
   258	  constructor
   259	  · unfold directALinePointDist
   260	    rw [Distribution.map_map]
   261	    simpa [Function.comp_def] using
   262	      (uniformDistribution_map_fst_of_equiv
   263	        (e := directLdSpacePointEquiv D)
   264	        (f := fun sample : DirectLdSpace D => sample.point) (by intro; rfl))
   265	  · unfold directALinePointDist
   266	    rw [Distribution.map_map]
   267	    simpa [Function.comp_def, directALineDescOf, DirectLineDesc.index] using
   268	      (uniformDistribution_map_fst_of_equiv
   269	        (e := directLdSpaceIndexEquiv D)
   270	        (f := fun sample : DirectLdSpace D => sample.index) (by intro; rfl))
   271	
   272	/-- Every sampled direct axis line contains its paired point.  This is the
   273	Direct-index incidence obligation corresponding to `lem:alnf` and
   274	the repair in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`. -/
   275	theorem directALinePointDist_mem_line (D : DirectLdParams) :
   276	    ∀ sample ∈ (directALinePointDist D).support,
   277	      sample.2 ∈ sample.1.pointSet := by
   278	  intro sample hsample
   279	  rw [directALinePointDist, Distribution.map_support,
   280	    uniformDistribution_support] at hsample
   281	  rcases Finset.mem_image.mp hsample with ⟨source, _, rfl⟩
   282	  simpa [directALineDescOf, DirectLineDesc.pointSet,
   283	    DirectLineDesc.base, DirectLineDesc.direction] using
   284	    (mem_linePoints_lineRepMap
   285	      (coordinateDirection source.index) source.point)
   286	
   287	/-- The point and stored-index marginals of the direct diagonal-line law are
   288	uniform.  This is the direct-index analogue of `lem:dlnf`, paper
   289	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-272`,
   290	and is a named obligation in the dimension-divisibility repair. -/
   291	theorem directDLinePointDist_point_index_marginal_uniform (D : DirectLdParams) :
   292	    (directDLinePointDist D).map Prod.snd =
   293	        uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ∧
   294	      (directDLinePointDist D).map (fun sample => sample.1.index) =
   295	        uniformDistribution (Fin D.m) := by
   296	  constructor
   297	  · unfold directDLinePointDist
   298	    rw [Distribution.map_map]
   299	    simpa [Function.comp_def] using
   300	      (uniformDistribution_map_fst_of_equiv
   301	        (e := directLdSpacePointEquiv D)
   302	        (f := fun sample : DirectLdSpace D => sample.point) (by intro; rfl))
   303	  · unfold directDLinePointDist
   304	    rw [Distribution.map_map]
   305	    simpa [Function.comp_def, directDLineDescOf, DirectLineDesc.index] using
   306	      (uniformDistribution_map_fst_of_equiv
   307	        (e := directLdSpaceIndexEquiv D)
   308	        (f := fun sample : DirectLdSpace D => sample.index) (by intro; rfl))
   309	
   310	/-- Every sampled direct diagonal line contains its paired point.  This is the
   311	Direct-index incidence obligation corresponding to `lem:dlnf`. -/
   312	theorem directDLinePointDist_mem_line (D : DirectLdParams) :
   313	    ∀ sample ∈ (directDLinePointDist D).support,
   314	      sample.2 ∈ sample.1.pointSet := by
   315	  intro sample hsample
   316	  rw [directDLinePointDist, Distribution.map_support,
   317	    uniformDistribution_support] at hsample
   318	  rcases Finset.mem_image.mp hsample with ⟨source, _, rfl⟩
   319	  simpa [directDLineDescOf, DirectLineDesc.pointSet,
   320	    DirectLineDesc.base, DirectLineDesc.direction] using
   321	    (mem_linePoints_lineRepMap
   322	      (directPrefixProjection source.index source.direction) source.point)
   323	
   324	/-- A sampled direct diagonal direction vanishes below its stored prefix
   325	index.  This is the direct counterpart of the third conclusion of
   326	`lem:dlnf`, paper
   327	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-272`.
   328	-/
   329	theorem directDLinePointDist_prefix_zero (D : DirectLdParams) :
   330	    ∀ sample ∈ (directDLinePointDist D).support,
   331	      ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < sample.1.index.val →
   332	        sample.1.direction j = 0 := by
   333	  intro sample hsample j hj
   334	  rw [directDLinePointDist, Distribution.map_support,
   335	    uniformDistribution_support] at hsample
   336	  rcases Finset.mem_image.mp hsample with ⟨source, _, rfl⟩
   337	  exact DirectLineDesc.diagonal_prefix_zero
   338	    (directDLineDescOf D source) (by
   339	      simp [directDLineDescOf, DirectLineDesc.kind]) j hj
   340	
   341	end

     4	/-!
     5	# The directly indexed low-degree game
     6	
     7	This module defines polynomial evaluation, questions, answers, and the game
     8	for the directly indexed low-degree interface.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The underlying game is `def:ld-game` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with source origin
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	open scoped BigOperators
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    23	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    24	
    25	noncomputable section
    26	
    27	/-- Coefficient lists for a univariate polynomial of degree at most `c` in the
    28	direct scalar field. -/
    29	abbrev DirectDegPoly (D : DirectLdParams) (c : ℕ) :=
    30	  Fin (c + 1) → DirectScalarQ D
    31	
    32	/-- A direct line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` lies on the line
    33	and every parameter presenting `u` gives value `a`.  The universal clause
    34	keeps the zero-direction case explicit. -/
    35	def DirectEvaluatesTo {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : DirectLineDesc D)
    36	    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    37	    (a : DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
    38	  (∃ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
    39	    ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction →
    40	      evalCoefficient f t = a
    41	
    42	/-- Option-completed evaluation of a direct line polynomial.  `none` is an
    43	explicit outcome when the point does not determine an evaluation; no field
    44	value is used as a fallback. -/
    45	noncomputable def directEvalOpt {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ}
    46	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    47	    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) : Option (DirectScalarQ D) := by
    48	  classical
    49	  exact if h : ∃ a : DirectScalarQ D, DirectEvaluatesTo line f u a then
    50	    some (Classical.choose h)
    51	  else none
    52	
    53	/-- The typed question alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/
    54	abbrev DirectLdQuestion (D : DirectLdParams) := LdType × DirectLdSpace D
    55	
    56	/-- Canonicalize a common direct sample for one question type.  Irrelevant
    57	coordinates are fixed, so point questions reveal no sampled line index and
    58	axis-line questions reveal no diagonal direction. -/
    59	noncomputable def directLdMap (D : DirectLdParams) :
    60	    LdType → DirectLdSpace D → DirectLdSpace D
    61	  | .point, sample => ⟨sample.point, D.firstIndex, 0⟩
    62	  | .aline, sample =>
    63	      let direction := coordinateDirection sample.index
    64	      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, 0⟩
    65	  | .dline, sample =>
    66	      let direction := directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction
    67	      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, direction⟩
    68	
    69	/-- The directly indexed question distribution.  It has the same uniform
    70	ordered type-pair branches as `ldQuestionDistribution`, but its common sample
    71	contains an actual coordinate index rather than a field seed. -/
    72	noncomputable def directLdQuestionDistribution (D : DirectLdParams) :
    73	    Distribution (DirectLdQuestion D × DirectLdQuestion D) :=
    74	  (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>
    75	    ((sample.1.1, directLdMap D sample.1.1 sample.2),
    76	      (sample.1.2, directLdMap D sample.1.2 sample.2))
    77	
    78	/-- The directly indexed question law is probabilistic. -/
    79	theorem directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :
    80	    (directLdQuestionDistribution D).IsProbability := by
    81	  exact (uniformDistribution_isProbability
    82	    ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map _
    83	
    84	/-- The answer alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/
    85	inductive DirectLdAnswer (D : DirectLdParams) where
    86	  | pointVals (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D)
    87	  | alinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
    88	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
    89	  deriving DecidableEq
    90	
    91	/-- A finite code for the directly indexed answer alphabet. -/
    92	abbrev DirectLdAnswerCode (D : DirectLdParams) :=
    93	  (Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
    94	    ((Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
    95	      (Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D))
    96	
    97	/-- The canonical code equivalence for `DirectLdAnswer`, sending point,
    98	axis-line, and diagonal-line answers to the three summands. -/
    99	noncomputable def directLdAnswerEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   100	    DirectLdAnswer D ≃ DirectLdAnswerCode D where
   101	  toFun
   102	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   103	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   104	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   105	  invFun
   106	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   107	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   108	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   109	  left_inv := by intro answer; cases answer <;> rfl
   110	  right_inv := by
   111	    intro answer
   112	    rcases answer with a | a
   113	    · rfl
   114	    · rcases a with a | a <;> rfl
   115	
   116	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Inhabited (DirectLdAnswer D) :=
   117	  ⟨.pointVals 0⟩
   118	
   119	noncomputable instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Fintype (DirectLdAnswer D) :=
   120	  Fintype.ofEquiv (DirectLdAnswerCode D) (directLdAnswerEquiv D).symm
   121	
   122	/-- Check that a direct-game answer has the constructor required by its
   123	question type. -/
   124	def validDirectLdAnswer {D : DirectLdParams} (t : LdType)
   125	    (answer : DirectLdAnswer D) : Bool :=
   126	  match t, answer with
   127	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   128	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   129	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   130	  | _, _ => false
   131	
   132	/-- The directly indexed axis-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
   133	def directAlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)
   134	    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)
   135	    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
   136	    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
   137	  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,
   138	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection line.index →
   139	      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   140	
   141	/-- The directly indexed diagonal-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
   142	def directDlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)
   143	    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)
   144	    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
   145	    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
   146	  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,
   147	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   148	      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   149	
   150	/-- The directly indexed low-degree win predicate.  It differs from
   151	`ldWinPredicate` only by reading the coordinate index directly from each line
   152	question. -/
   153	noncomputable def directLdWinPredicate (D : DirectLdParams) :
   154	    DirectLdQuestion D → DirectLdQuestion D →
   155	      DirectLdAnswer D → DirectLdAnswer D → Bool :=
   156	  open Classical in
   157	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   158	    if validDirectLdAnswer tA a && validDirectLdAnswer tB b then
   159	      match tA, tB, a, b with
   160	      | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   161	      | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   162	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   163	      | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   164	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   165	      | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   166	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   167	      | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   168	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   169	      | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   170	      | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   171	      | _, _, _, _ => true
   172	    else false
   173	
   174	/-- The directly indexed low-degree game at an arbitrary positive dimension.
   175	It is an internal analysis game, not the conditionally linear verifier game
   176	`ldGame`. -/
   177	noncomputable def directLdGame (D : DirectLdParams) : Game where
   178	  QuestionA := DirectLdQuestion D
   179	  QuestionB := DirectLdQuestion D
   180	  AnswerA := DirectLdAnswer D
   181	  AnswerB := DirectLdAnswer D
   182	  μ := directLdQuestionDistribution D
   183	  μ_prob := directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability D
   184	  decide := directLdWinPredicate D
   185	
   186	/-- The canonical point question associated with a geometric point. -/
   187	def directLdPointQuestionOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   188	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) : DirectLdQuestion D :=
   189	  (.point, ⟨u, D.firstIndex, 0⟩)
   190	
   191	/-- Total point-answer relabeling used in the direct soundness conclusion.
   192	Wrong-form answers are folded into the zero tuple, exactly as for
   193	`ldPointValuesOrZero`. -/
   194	def directLdPointValuesOrZero (D : DirectLdParams) :
   195	    DirectLdAnswer D → Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D
   196	  | .pointVals values => values
   197	  | .alinePolys _ => 0
   198	  | .dlinePolys _ => 0
   199	
   200	/-- A simultaneous tuple of bounded polynomials for the directly indexed
   201	game. -/
   202	noncomputable abbrev DirectPolyTuple (D : DirectLdParams) :=
   203	  Fin D.k → PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d
   204	
   205	/-- A polynomial-tuple POVM for the directly indexed game. -/
   206	noncomputable abbrev DirectPolyMeasTuple (D : DirectLdParams) (ι : Type*)
   207	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   208	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectPolyTuple D) ι
   209	
   210	/-- Evaluate every component of a direct polynomial tuple at a point. -/
   211	def evalDirectPolyTupleAt {D : DirectLdParams}
   212	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (g : DirectPolyTuple D) :
   213	    Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D :=
   214	  fun j => MvPolynomial.eval u (g j).1
   215	
   216	end

     7	/-!
     8	# Simultaneous polynomial measurements for the direct low-degree game
     9	
    10	This module applies the quantum soundness theorem of the low individual
    11	degree test to each coordinate of a projective strategy for the directly
    12	indexed low-degree game, transports the Schwartz--Zippel collision estimate
    13	to the direct polynomial representatives, and, for simultaneity parameter
    14	`1`, obtains the polynomial-tuple conclusion of `lem:ld-soundness` from the
    15	coordinate conclusions.
    16	
    17	## The simultaneity obstruction
    18	
    19	For simultaneity parameter `k ≥ 2` the coordinate conclusions alone do not
    20	determine simultaneous polynomial measurements, so no palindromic combination
    21	of the coordinate measurements can be consistent with a joint point
    22	measurement in general.  Let `q = 2^s`, let the degree be `1`, and let Bob
    23	measure the univariate polynomials `g = g₀ + g₁ x` once in the standard basis
    24	`|g⟩` and once in the Fourier basis attached to the symmetric pairing
    25	`⟨h, g⟩ = h₀ g₁ + h₁ g₀`.  In characteristic two every evaluation functional
    26	`h ↦ h(u)` is represented by an isotropic vector of this pairing, so at every
    27	point `u` the value-level coarse-grainings `Q^{1,u}_{[a]}` (Fourier basis) and
    28	`Q^{2,u}_{[b]}` (standard basis) commute, and on the maximally entangled state
    29	Alice may answer point questions with the joint projective measurement
    30	`P^u_{a,b} = (Q^{1,u}_{[a]} Q^{2,u}_{[b]})ᵀ`.  All coordinate consistencies of
    31	`lem:ld-soundness` then hold with defect `0` and distinct polynomials collide
    32	at a uniform point with probability `1 / q`, but the sandwiched POVM has
    33	`∑_{g₂(u) = b} |g₂⟩⟨g₂| Q^{1,u}_{[a]} |g₂⟩⟨g₂| = q⁻¹ Q^{2,u}_{[b]}`, whose
    34	consistency defect against `P^u` is `1 - 1/q`; more strongly, every
    35	polynomial-pair POVM on Bob's side has defect at least `1 - 2/q` against
    36	`P^u`.  No bound of the form `C k √(δ + m d / q)` holds for a universal `C`.
    37	The source obtains the general case not coordinatewise but by the combining
    38	reduction of Theorem 4.43 in the NEEXP paper, which applies the `k = 1`
    39	theorem once, in dimension `m + k`, to a combined strategy; that reduction is
    40	not formalized here.  The two-measurement pasting estimate (Fact 4.35 there)
    41	does not apply either, since it evaluates the two coordinates at
    42	independently sampled points while the low-degree game evaluates all
    43	coordinates at one point.  The counterexample and the resulting formal
    44	status are recorded in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-simultaneous-sandwich.tex`.
    45	
    46	## References
    47	
    48	* `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`
    49	* `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:465-501`
    50	* `references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex:912-1060` and `:1409-1503`
    51	* `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:180-202`
    52	* `lem:ld-soundness` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex`
    53	* `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`
    54	* `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-simultaneous-sandwich.tex`
    55	-/

    67	/-! ## Direct polynomial collision estimate -/
    68	
    69	/-- Two distinct direct polynomial representatives agree at a uniformly
    70	sampled direct point with probability at most `m d / q`.
    71	
    72	This is the Schwartz--Zippel estimate `polynomialAgreement_avg_le_mdq` of the
    73	low individual degree test, read through the polynomial and point
    74	identifications of the direct low-degree game; it is the collision
    75	hypothesis of `lem:ld-sandwich` (blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:454-480`,
    76	paper `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:465-501`). -/
    77	theorem directPolynomialAgreement_avg_le_mdq (D : DirectLdParams)
    78	    (g g' : PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d) (hneq : g ≠ g') :
    79	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
    80	        (fun u => if MvPolynomial.eval u g.1 = MvPolynomial.eval u g'.1 then
    81	          (1 : Error) else 0) ≤
    82	      (D.m * D.d : Error) / D.q := by
    83	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    84	  let gLdt := directPolyEquivPolynomial D g
    85	  let g'Ldt := directPolyEquivPolynomial D g'
    86	  have hneqLdt : gLdt ≠ g'Ldt := by
    87	    intro heq
    88	    exact hneq ((directPolyEquivPolynomial D).injective heq)
    89	  calc
    90	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
    91	        (fun u => if MvPolynomial.eval u g.1 = MvPolynomial.eval u g'.1 then
    92	          (1 : Error) else 0) =
    93	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
    94	        (fun u => if gLdt (directPointEquiv D u) =
    95	          g'Ldt (directPointEquiv D u) then (1 : Error) else 0) := by
    96	            apply avgOver_congr
    97	            intro u
    98	            simp only [gLdt, g'Ldt, directPolyEquivPolynomial_apply]
    99	            exact if_congr
   100	              ((directScalarEquiv D).injective.eq_iff.symm) rfl rfl
   101	    _ = avgOver (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
   102	        (fun u : Point D.toLDTParameters =>
   103	          if gLdt u = g'Ldt u then (1 : Error) else 0) := by
   104	      simpa using
   105	        (avgOver_uniform_equiv (directPointEquiv D)
   106	          (fun u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D =>
   107	            if gLdt (directPointEquiv D u) =
   108	              g'Ldt (directPointEquiv D u) then (1 : Error) else 0))
   109	    _ ≤ (D.m * D.d : Error) / D.q :=
   110	      polynomialAgreement_avg_le_mdq D.toLDTParameters gLdt g'Ldt hneqLdt
