   112	/-! ## Coordinatewise low individual degree soundness -/
   113	
   114	/-- Quantum soundness of the low individual degree test (`thm:main-formal`,
   115	paper `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:180-202`) applied to one
   116	coordinate of a projective strategy for the direct low-degree game.
   117	
   118	The coordinate strategy passes the test with failure probability at most
   119	`3 ε`, and the theorem is instantiated at the auxiliary sampling parameter
   120	`directLdAuxParameter D`; both numerical side conditions of the theorem follow
   121	from the positivity of the dimension and of the degree.  Blueprint
   122	`lem:ld-soundness`, paper
   123	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`. -/
   124	theorem directCoordinateMainFormal
   125	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
   126	    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) (ε : Error)
   127	    (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) :
   128	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   129	    ∃ GA : ProjMeas (Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιA,
   130	      ∃ GB : ProjMeas (Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιB,
   131	        ConsRel (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).state
   132	            (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
   133	            (IdxProjMeas.toIdxSubMeas
   134	              (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementA)
   135	            (polynomialEvaluationFamily D.toLDTParameters GB.toSubMeas)
   136	            (Test.mainFormalError D.toLDTParameters
   137	              (directLdAuxParameter D) (3 * ε)) ∧
   138	          ConsRel (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).state
   139	            (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
   140	            (polynomialEvaluationFamily D.toLDTParameters GA.toSubMeas)
   141	            (IdxProjMeas.toIdxSubMeas
   142	              (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementB)
   143	            (Test.mainFormalError D.toLDTParameters
   144	              (directLdAuxParameter D) (3 * ε)) ∧
   145	          ConsRel (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).state
   146	            (uniformDistribution Unit)
   147	            (constSubMeasFamily GA.toSubMeas)
   148	            (constSubMeasFamily GB.toSubMeas)
   149	            (Test.mainFormalError D.toLDTParameters
   150	              (directLdAuxParameter D) (3 * ε)) := by
   151	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   152	  exact Test.mainFormal D.toLDTParameters
   153	    (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r) (3 * ε)
   154	    (directCoordinate_passes D S hS r ε hwin).soundnessHypothesis
   155	    (directLdAuxParameter D) (four_hundred_mul_le_directLdAuxParameter D)
   156	    (directLdAuxParameter_pos D)

   158	/-! ## One-coordinate tuples -/
   159	
   160	/-- Relabeling an outcome by a constant tuple over a one-element index set is
   161	selected by the value of the tuple at the unique index. -/
   162	private theorem const_tuple_eq_iff {iota beta : Type*} [Unique iota]
   163	    (v : iota → beta) (b : beta) :
   164	    v = (fun _ => b) ↔ v default = b :=
   165	  funext_iff.trans Unique.forall_iff
   166	
   167	/-- The effect of a tuple-relabeled measurement at a constant tuple over a
   168	one-element index set is the effect of the relabeling by the unique
   169	coordinate. -/
   170	private theorem postprocess_effect_const_tuple
   171	    {alpha beta iota d : Type*} [Fintype alpha] [DecidableEq alpha]
   172	    [Fintype beta] [DecidableEq beta] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   173	    [Unique iota] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   174	    (M : Quantum.Measurement alpha d) (f : alpha → iota → beta) (b : beta) :
   175	    (M.postprocess f).effect (fun _ => b) =
   176	      (M.postprocess (fun a => f a default)).effect b := by
   177	  simp only [Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
   178	  exact Finset.sum_congr
   179	    (Finset.filter_congr fun a _ => const_tuple_eq_iff (f a) b)
   180	    (fun _ _ => rfl)
   181	
   182	/-- Reading a measurement as a one-coordinate tuple measurement does not
   183	change its effects. -/
   184	private theorem postprocess_const_tuple_effect_self
   185	    {alpha iota d : Type*} [Fintype alpha] [DecidableEq alpha]
   186	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota] [Unique iota] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   187	    (M : Quantum.Measurement alpha d) (p : alpha) :
   188	    (M.postprocess (fun a (_ : iota) => a)).effect (fun _ => p) = M.effect p := by
   189	  rw [postprocess_effect_const_tuple]
   190	  simp only [Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect, Finset.filter_eq',
   191	    Finset.mem_univ, if_true, Finset.sum_singleton]
   192	
   193	/-- The polynomial-tuple conclusion of `lem:ld-soundness` for simultaneity
   194	parameter `1`: the coordinate conclusions of the low individual degree
   195	theorem, read as one-coordinate tuples.
   196	
   197	The three consistency defects carry the error of `thm:main-formal` at the
   198	auxiliary parameter `directLdAuxParameter D` and pass bound `3 ε`; its
   199	absorption into the error function `deltaLd` is
   200	`exists_directLdTransportConstants`.  For simultaneity parameter at least `2`
   201	the coordinate conclusions do not determine simultaneous polynomial
   202	measurements; see the module docstring and
   203	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-simultaneous-sandwich.tex`.  Blueprint
   204	`lem:ld-soundness`, paper
   205	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`. -/
   206	theorem exists_directSimultaneousPolynomialMeasurements_of_k_eq_one
   207	    (D : DirectLdParams) (hk : D.k = 1) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
   208	    (hS : S.IsProjective) (ε : Error) (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) :
   209	    ∃ GA : DirectPolyMeasTuple D S.ιA,
   210	      ∃ GB : DirectPolyMeasTuple D S.ιB,
   211	        consistencyDefect
   212	            (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   213	            (fun u outcome =>
   214	              heteroKron
   215	                (((S.A (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
   216	                  (directLdPointValuesOrZero D)).effect outcome) 1)
   217	            (fun u outcome =>
   218	              heteroKron 1
   219	                ((GB.postprocess (evalDirectPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome))
   220	            S.ψ ≤
   221	          Test.mainFormalError D.toLDTParameters (directLdAuxParameter D) (3 * ε) ∧
   222	        consistencyDefect
   223	            (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   224	            (fun u outcome =>
   225	              heteroKron
   226	                ((GA.postprocess (evalDirectPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome) 1)
   227	            (fun u outcome =>
   228	              heteroKron 1
   229	                (((S.B (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
   230	                  (directLdPointValuesOrZero D)).effect outcome))
   231	            S.ψ ≤
   232	          Test.mainFormalError D.toLDTParameters (directLdAuxParameter D) (3 * ε) ∧
   233	        consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
   234	            (fun _ g => heteroKron (GA.effect g) 1)
   235	            (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 (GB.effect g))
   236	            S.ψ ≤
   237	          Test.mainFormalError D.toLDTParameters (directLdAuxParameter D) (3 * ε) := by
   238	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   239	  haveI hU : Unique (Fin D.k) :=
   240	    { default := ⟨0, by omega⟩
   241	      uniq := fun i => Fin.ext (by have := i.isLt; omega) }
   242	  obtain ⟨GA₀, GB₀, h1, h2, h3⟩ :=
   243	    directCoordinateMainFormal D S hS default ε hwin
   244	  refine ⟨(directPolynomialMeasurement D GA₀).postprocess (fun g _ => g),
   245	    (directPolynomialMeasurement D GB₀).postprocess (fun g _ => g), ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   246	  · have h1' := directPointPolynomial_consistencyDefect_le D S hS default GB₀ _ h1
   247	    refine ((consistencyDefect_outcome_equiv _
   248	      (Equiv.funUnique (Fin D.k) (DirectScalarQ D)).symm _ _ S.ψ).symm.trans
   249	      (consistencyDefect_congr _ _ _ _ _ S.ψ ?_ ?_)).trans_le h1'
   250	    · intro u a
   251	      change heteroKron (((S.A (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
   252	        (directLdPointValuesOrZero D)).effect (fun _ => a)) 1 = _
   253	      rw [postprocess_effect_const_tuple]
   254	      rfl
   255	    · intro u a
   256	      change heteroKron 1 ((((directPolynomialMeasurement D GB₀).postprocess
   257	        (fun g _ => g)).postprocess (evalDirectPolyTupleAt u)).effect
   258	          (fun _ => a)) = _
   259	      rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_comp,
   260	        postprocess_effect_const_tuple]
   261	      rfl
   262	  · have h2' := directPolynomialPoint_consistencyDefect_le D S hS default GA₀ _ h2
   263	    refine ((consistencyDefect_outcome_equiv _
   264	      (Equiv.funUnique (Fin D.k) (DirectScalarQ D)).symm _ _ S.ψ).symm.trans
   265	      (consistencyDefect_congr _ _ _ _ _ S.ψ ?_ ?_)).trans_le h2'
   266	    · intro u a
   267	      change heteroKron ((((directPolynomialMeasurement D GA₀).postprocess
   268	        (fun g _ => g)).postprocess (evalDirectPolyTupleAt u)).effect
   269	          (fun _ => a)) 1 = _
   270	      rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_comp,
   271	        postprocess_effect_const_tuple]
   272	      rfl
   273	    · intro u a
   274	      change heteroKron 1 (((S.B (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
   275	        (directLdPointValuesOrZero D)).effect (fun _ => a)) = _
   276	      rw [postprocess_effect_const_tuple]
   277	      rfl
   278	  · have h3' := directPolynomialPolynomial_consistencyDefect_le D S GA₀ GB₀ _ h3
   279	    refine ((consistencyDefect_outcome_equiv _
   280	      (Equiv.funUnique (Fin D.k) (PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d)).symm _ _
   281	        S.ψ).symm.trans
   282	      (consistencyDefect_congr _ _ _ _ _ S.ψ ?_ ?_)).trans_le h3'
   283	    · intro _ p
   284	      change heteroKron (((directPolynomialMeasurement D GA₀).postprocess
   285	        (fun g _ => g)).effect (fun _ => p)) 1 = _
   286	      rw [postprocess_const_tuple_effect_self]
   287	    · intro _ p
   288	      change heteroKron 1 (((directPolynomialMeasurement D GB₀).postprocess
   289	        (fun g _ => g)).effect (fun _ => p)) = _
   290	      rw [postprocess_const_tuple_effect_self]
   291

     3	/-!
     4	# Question and answer transport for the directly indexed low-degree game
     5	
     6	This module reads low individual degree test questions as canonical direct
     7	questions and rebases direct answers to the LDT line parametrization.
     8	
     9	Points and lines are decoded with the coordinate order reversed
    10	(`directPointEquiv`), so that the suffix-zero direction restriction of the
    11	LDT diagonal test becomes the prefix-zero restriction of the direct game.
    12	An LDT diagonal line reveals no coordinate index, whereas a direct diagonal
    13	question carries one.  The transported question uses the *leading index* of
    14	the decoded direction, the least coordinate at which the direction is
    15	nonzero.  Under the direct sampler, this is the index attached to the sampled
    16	direction exactly when the direction is nonzero at the sampled index
    17	(`directDiagonalIndexOf_prefixProjection`), an event of conditional
    18	probability `1 - 1/q`; on the LDT side, the leading index of a decoded
    19	`j`-restricted direction is `Fin.rev j` exactly when its pivot coordinate is
    20	nonzero (`directDiagonalIndexOf_extendRestrictedDirection`).  Diagonal answers
    21	on zero-direction lines are read as the constant polynomial carrying their
    22	value at the base point, following `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
    23	
    24	## References
    25	
    26	- `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:230-272`
    27	- `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:49-65`
    28	- `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:120-121`
    29	- `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`
    30	-/
    31	
    32	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    33

    37	open MIPStarRE.Quantum

    41	/-! ## Canonical line rebasing of LDT lines -/
    42	
    43	/-- A chosen affine parameter expressing a point relative to its canonical
    44	line representative. -/
    45	noncomputable def directLineRepParameter
    46	    {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ} (v u : Fin m → K) : K :=
    47	  Classical.choose (mem_linePoints_lineRepMap v u)
    48	
    49	/-- The chosen canonical rebase parameter reconstructs the original point. -/
    50	theorem directLineRepParameter_spec
    51	    {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ} (v u : Fin m → K) :
    52	    u = lineRepMap v u + directLineRepParameter v u • v :=
    53	  Classical.choose_spec (mem_linePoints_lineRepMap v u)
    54	
    55	/-- Canonical line representatives are unchanged by translation along their
    56	direction. -/
    57	theorem lineRepMap_add_smul
    58	    {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    59	    (v u : Fin m → K) (t : K) :
    60	    lineRepMap v (u + t • v) = lineRepMap v u := by
    61	  let W : Submodule K (Fin m → K) := Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K))
    62	  have hv : v ∈ W := Submodule.subset_span (Set.mem_singleton v)
    63	  have hzero : lineRepMap v v = 0 := by
    64	    simp [lineRepMap, canonicalProjOfKernel, W, LinearMap.comp_apply,
    65	      Submodule.projectionOnto_apply_of_mem_right
    66	        (isCompl_registerSubmodule_canonicalComplement W).symm hv]
    67	  simp [map_add, map_smul, hzero]
    68	
    69	/-- For a nonzero direction, the canonical rebase parameter is unique. -/
    70	theorem directLineRepParameter_eq_of_nonzero
    71	    {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    72	    {v u : Fin m → K} (hv : v ≠ 0) {t : K}
    73	    (ht : u = lineRepMap v u + t • v) :
    74	    directLineRepParameter v u = t := by
    75	  have hfun : directLineRepParameter v u • v = t • v := by
    76	    apply add_left_cancel (a := lineRepMap v u)
    77	    exact (directLineRepParameter_spec v u).symm.trans ht
    78	  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ : ∃ i, v i ≠ 0 := by
    79	    by_contra h
    80	    apply hv
    81	    funext i
    82	    simpa using not_exists.mp h i
    83	  have hcoord := congrFun hfun i
    84	  simp only [Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul] at hcoord
    85	  exact mul_right_cancel₀ hi hcoord
    86	
    87	/-- Translating a point on a nonzero line adds the translation to its
    88	canonical rebase parameter. -/
    89	theorem directLineRepParameter_add_smul
    90	    {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    91	    {v u : Fin m → K} (hv : v ≠ 0) (t : K) :
    92	    directLineRepParameter v (u + t • v) =
    93	      directLineRepParameter v u + t := by
    94	  apply directLineRepParameter_eq_of_nonzero hv
    95	  rw [lineRepMap_add_smul]
    96	  calc
    97	    u + t • v =
    98	        (lineRepMap v u + directLineRepParameter v u • v) + t • v := by
    99	      rw [← directLineRepParameter_spec v u]
   100	    _ = lineRepMap v u + (directLineRepParameter v u + t) • v := by
   101	      module
   102	
   103	/-! ## The leading index of a direction -/
   104	
   105	/-- The coordinates at which a direct direction vector is nonzero. -/
   106	def directionSupport (D : DirectLdParams) (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
   107	    Finset (Fin D.m) :=
   108	  open Classical in
   109	  Finset.univ.filter fun j => v j ≠ 0
   110	
   111	theorem mem_directionSupport (D : DirectLdParams)
   112	    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (j : Fin D.m) :
   113	    j ∈ directionSupport D v ↔ v j ≠ 0 := by
   114	  simp [directionSupport]
   115	
   116	/-- The leading index of a direction: the least coordinate at which it is
   117	nonzero, or the last coordinate for the zero direction.  Every coordinate
   118	before the leading index vanishes, so a direction is the prefix projection of
   119	itself at its leading index, and the pair (leading index, direction) is a
   120	canonical direct diagonal sample.  It is the direct index of the sample
   121	whenever the sampled direction is nonzero at the sampled index. -/
   122	noncomputable def directDiagonalIndexOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   123	    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) : Fin D.m :=
   124	  open Classical in
   125	  if h : (directionSupport D v).Nonempty then (directionSupport D v).min' h
   126	  else Fin.rev D.firstIndex
   127	
   128	/-- Coordinates before the leading index vanish. -/
   129	theorem directDiagonalIndexOf_prefix_zero (D : DirectLdParams)
   130	    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
   131	    ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < (directDiagonalIndexOf D v).val → v j = 0 := by
   132	  classical
   133	  intro j hj
   134	  by_contra hne
   135	  have hmem : j ∈ directionSupport D v := (mem_directionSupport D v j).mpr hne
   136	  have hnonempty : (directionSupport D v).Nonempty := ⟨j, hmem⟩
   137	  have hle : directDiagonalIndexOf D v ≤ j := by
   138	    unfold directDiagonalIndexOf
   139	    rw [dif_pos hnonempty]
   140	    exact Finset.min'_le _ _ hmem
   141	  exact absurd (Fin.lt_def.mpr hj) (not_lt.mpr hle)
   142	
   143	/-- A direction vanishing before `i` and nonzero at `i` has leading index
   144	`i`. -/
   145	theorem directDiagonalIndexOf_eq (D : DirectLdParams)
   146	    {v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D} {i : Fin D.m}
   147	    (hzero : ∀ j : Fin D.m, j.val < i.val → v j = 0) (hi : v i ≠ 0) :
   148	    directDiagonalIndexOf D v = i := by
   149	  classical
   150	  have hmem : i ∈ directionSupport D v := (mem_directionSupport D v i).mpr hi
   151	  have hnonempty : (directionSupport D v).Nonempty := ⟨i, hmem⟩
   152	  unfold directDiagonalIndexOf
   153	  rw [dif_pos hnonempty]
   154	  apply le_antisymm
   155	  · exact Finset.min'_le _ _ hmem
   156	  · apply Finset.le_min'
   157	    intro j hj
   158	    by_contra hlt
   159	    exact (mem_directionSupport D v j).mp hj
   160	      (hzero j (Fin.lt_def.mp (not_le.mp hlt)))
   161	
   162	/-- The leading index of a prefix-projected direction is the projection index
   163	whenever the direction is nonzero there.  This is the generic direct
   164	diagonal sample: the sampled index is recovered from the projected direction
   165	alone. -/
   166	theorem directDiagonalIndexOf_prefixProjection (D : DirectLdParams)
   167	    (i : Fin D.m) (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (hi : v i ≠ 0) :
   168	    directDiagonalIndexOf D (directPrefixProjection i v) = i := by
   169	  apply directDiagonalIndexOf_eq
   170	  · intro j hj
   171	    simp [directPrefixProjection, hj]
   172	  · simpa [directPrefixProjection] using hi
   173	
   174	/-- Prefix projection at the leading index is the identity. -/
   175	theorem directPrefixProjection_directDiagonalIndexOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   176	    (v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
   177	    directPrefixProjection (directDiagonalIndexOf D v) v = v := by
   178	  funext j
   179	  unfold directPrefixProjection
   180	  split_ifs with hj
   181	  · exact (directDiagonalIndexOf_prefix_zero D v j hj).symm
   182	  · rfl

   184	/-! ## Decoding LDT points and lines -/
   185	
   186	/-- Decode an LDT point into the fixed direct scalar field, reversing the
   187	coordinate order. -/
   188	abbrev ldtPointToDirect (D : DirectLdParams) :
   189	    Point D.toLDTParameters → Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D :=
   190	  (directPointEquiv D).symm
   191	
   192	/-- The direct canonical axis question represented by an LDT axis line.
   193	The LDT coordinate index is reversed together with the point
   194	coordinates. -/
   195	noncomputable def directAxisQuestionOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   196	    (line : AxisParallelLine D.toLDTParameters) : DirectLdQuestion D :=
   197	  let u := ldtPointToDirect D line.base
   198	  let i : Fin D.m := Fin.rev line.direction
   199	  let v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D := coordinateDirection i
   200	  (.aline, ⟨lineRepMap v u, i, 0⟩)
   201	
   202	/-- The direct canonical diagonal question represented by an LDT diagonal
   203	line.  The decoded direction is kept and the direct index is its leading
   204	index, so the question is the canonical direct question of the direct sample
   205	formed by the decoded base, the leading index, and the decoded direction
   206	(`directDiagonalQuestionOf_eq_directLdMap`). -/
   207	noncomputable def directDiagonalQuestionOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   208	    (line : DiagonalLine D.toLDTParameters) : DirectLdQuestion D :=
   209	  let u := ldtPointToDirect D line.base
   210	  let v := ldtPointToDirect D line.direction
   211	  (.dline, ⟨lineRepMap v u, directDiagonalIndexOf D v, v⟩)
   212	
   213	/-- The direct point question represented by an LDT point. -/
   214	noncomputable def directPointQuestionOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   215	    (u : Point D.toLDTParameters) : DirectLdQuestion D :=
   216	  directLdPointQuestionOf D (ldtPointToDirect D u)
   217	
   218	/-- Every transported diagonal question is the canonical direct question of
   219	the direct sample carrying the leading index, hence lies in the support of
   220	the direct diagonal sampler. -/
   221	theorem directDiagonalQuestionOf_eq_directLdMap (D : DirectLdParams)
   222	    (line : DiagonalLine D.toLDTParameters) :
   223	    directDiagonalQuestionOf D line =
   224	      (.dline, directLdMap D .dline
   225	        ⟨ldtPointToDirect D line.base,
   226	          directDiagonalIndexOf D (ldtPointToDirect D line.direction),
   227	          ldtPointToDirect D line.direction⟩) := by
   228	  unfold directDiagonalQuestionOf directLdMap
   229	  simp only [directPrefixProjection_directDiagonalIndexOf]
   230	
   231	/-- The LDT diagonal line represented by a direct sample: the encoded
   232	point and the encoded direction. -/
   233	def ldtDiagonalLineOf (D : DirectLdParams) (sample : DirectLdSpace D) :
   234	    DiagonalLine D.toLDTParameters :=
   235	  { base := directPointEquiv D sample.point
   236	    direction := directPointEquiv D sample.direction }
   237	
   238	/-- Round trip on generic direct samples: when the sampled direction is
   239	nonzero at the sampled index, the LDT line of the canonical direct
   240	diagonal question transports back to that question, index included. -/
   241	theorem directDiagonalQuestionOf_ldtDiagonalLineOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   242	    (sample : DirectLdSpace D)
   243	    (hgeneric : sample.direction sample.index ≠ 0) :
   244	    directDiagonalQuestionOf D
   245	        (ldtDiagonalLineOf D (directLdMap D .dline sample)) =
   246	      (.dline, directLdMap D .dline sample) := by
   247	  cases sample with
   248	  | mk point index direction =>
   249	      unfold directDiagonalQuestionOf ldtDiagonalLineOf directLdMap
   250	      simp only [ldtPointToDirect, Equiv.symm_apply_apply, lineRepMap_apply_self,
   251	        directDiagonalIndexOf_prefixProjection D index direction hgeneric]
   252	
   253	/-- An LDT `j`-restricted diagonal direction decodes to a direct direction
   254	vanishing before index `Fin.rev j`: the suffix restriction of the low
   255	individual degree test is the prefix restriction of the direct game. -/
   256	theorem ldtPointToDirect_extendRestrictedDirection_prefix_zero
   257	    (D : DirectLdParams) (j : Fin D.m)
   258	    (free : Fin (j.val + 1) → Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   259	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   260	    ∀ c : Fin D.m, c.val < (Fin.rev j).val →
   261	      ldtPointToDirect D (extendRestrictedDirection j free) c = 0 := by
   262	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   263	  intro c hc
   264	  have hj := j.isLt
   265	  have hgt : ¬ (Fin.rev c).val ≤ j.val := by
   266	    rw [Fin.val_rev] at hc ⊢
   267	    omega
   268	  simp only [ldtPointToDirect, directPointEquiv_symm_apply,
   269	    extendRestrictedDirection, dif_neg hgt]
   270	  exact (FieldModel.equiv (q := D.q)).symm_apply_apply 0
   271	
   272	/-- The leading index of a decoded `j`-restricted direction is `Fin.rev j`
   273	exactly on the generic event that its pivot coordinate `j` is nonzero. -/
   274	theorem directDiagonalIndexOf_extendRestrictedDirection
   275	    (D : DirectLdParams) (j : Fin D.m)
   276	    (free : Fin (j.val + 1) → Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   277	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   278	    free ⟨j.val, Nat.lt_succ_self _⟩ ≠ zeroCoord →
   279	      directDiagonalIndexOf D
   280	          (ldtPointToDirect D (extendRestrictedDirection j free)) =
   281	        Fin.rev j := by
   282	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   283	  intro hpivot
   284	  apply directDiagonalIndexOf_eq
   285	  · exact ldtPointToDirect_extendRestrictedDirection_prefix_zero D j free
   286	  · simp only [ldtPointToDirect, directPointEquiv_symm_apply, Fin.rev_rev,
   287	      extendRestrictedDirection, dif_pos (le_refl j.val)]
   288	    intro h
   289	    apply hpivot
   290	    have hcoded := congrArg (directScalarEquiv D) h
   291	    rw [Equiv.apply_symm_apply] at hcoded
   292	    exact hcoded

   294	/-! ## Rebasing lines -/
   295	
   296	/-- Decoding an axis-line rebase is translation by the decoded scalar along
   297	the reversed direct coordinate direction. -/
   298	theorem ldtPointToDirect_axis_rebase (D : DirectLdParams)
   299	    (line : AxisParallelLine D.toLDTParameters)
   300	    (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   301	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   302	    ldtPointToDirect D (line.rebaseAt t).base =
   303	      ldtPointToDirect D line.base +
   304	        (directScalarEquiv D).symm t •
   305	          coordinateDirection (Fin.rev line.direction) := by
   306	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   307	  funext i
   308	  simp only [ldtPointToDirect, directPointEquiv_symm_apply,
   309	    AxisParallelLine.rebaseAt, AxisParallelLine.pointAt, Pi.add_apply,
   310	    Pi.smul_apply]
   311	  by_cases hi : i = Fin.rev line.direction
   312	  · subst hi
   313	    simp only [coordinateDirection, Fin.rev_rev, if_pos, smul_eq_mul]
   314	    rw [Pi.single_eq_same, mul_one]
   315	    exact (FieldModel.equiv (q := D.q)).symm_apply_apply _
   316	  · have hrev : Fin.rev i ≠ line.direction := by
   317	      intro h
   318	      apply hi
   319	      rw [← h, Fin.rev_rev]
   320	    simp [hi, hrev, coordinateDirection]
   321	
   322	/-- Decoding a diagonal-line rebase is translation by the decoded scalar
   323	along the decoded direct direction. -/
   324	theorem ldtPointToDirect_diagonal_rebase (D : DirectLdParams)
   325	    (line : DiagonalLine D.toLDTParameters)
   326	    (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   327	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   328	    ldtPointToDirect D (line.rebaseAt t).base =
   329	      ldtPointToDirect D line.base +
   330	        (directScalarEquiv D).symm t • ldtPointToDirect D line.direction := by
   331	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   332	  funext i
   333	  change decodeScalar
   334	      (addCoord (line.base (Fin.rev i))
   335	        (mulCoord t (line.direction (Fin.rev i)))) =
   336	    decodeScalar (line.base (Fin.rev i)) +
   337	      decodeScalar t * decodeScalar (line.direction (Fin.rev i))
   338	  simp [addCoord, mulCoord]
   339	
   340	/-- Canonical direct axis questions do not depend on the chosen base point of
   341	the LDT line. -/
   342	theorem directAxisQuestionOf_rebase (D : DirectLdParams)
   343	    (line : AxisParallelLine D.toLDTParameters)
   344	    (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   345	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   346	    directAxisQuestionOf D (line.rebaseAt t) = directAxisQuestionOf D line := by
   347	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   348	  simp only [directAxisQuestionOf, AxisParallelLine.rebaseAt_direction]
   349	  rw [ldtPointToDirect_axis_rebase, lineRepMap_add_smul]
   350	
   351	/-- Canonical direct diagonal questions do not depend on the chosen base point
   352	of the LDT line; the leading index depends only on the direction. -/
   353	theorem directDiagonalQuestionOf_rebase (D : DirectLdParams)
   354	    (line : DiagonalLine D.toLDTParameters)
   355	    (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   356	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   357	    directDiagonalQuestionOf D (line.rebaseAt t) =
   358	      directDiagonalQuestionOf D line := by
   359	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   360	  simp only [directDiagonalQuestionOf, DiagonalLine.rebaseAt]
   361	  have hrebase := ldtPointToDirect_diagonal_rebase D line t
   362	  change ldtPointToDirect D (line.pointAt t) =
   363	      ldtPointToDirect D line.base +
   364	        (directScalarEquiv D).symm t • ldtPointToDirect D line.direction at hrebase
   365	  rw [hrebase, lineRepMap_add_smul]
   366	
   367	/-- The fixed scalar coding transports field addition to LDT coordinate
   368	addition. -/
   369	theorem directScalarEquiv_add (D : DirectLdParams)
   370	    (x y : DirectScalarQ D) :
   371	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   372	    directScalarEquiv D (x + y) =
   373	      addCoord (directScalarEquiv D x) (directScalarEquiv D y) := by
   374	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   375	  change FieldModel.equiv (x + y) =
   376	    FieldModel.equiv
   377	      (FieldModel.equiv.symm (FieldModel.equiv x) +
   378	        FieldModel.equiv.symm (FieldModel.equiv y))
   379	  rw [FieldModel.equiv.symm_apply_apply, FieldModel.equiv.symm_apply_apply]
   380	
   381	private theorem coordinateDirection_ne_zero
   382	    {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ} (i : Fin m) :
   383	    (coordinateDirection i : Fin m → K) ≠ 0 := by
   384	  intro h
   385	  have hi := congrFun h i
   386	  simp [coordinateDirection] at hi
   387	
   388	/-- Canonical rebase parameter for an LDT axis-parallel line. -/
   389	noncomputable def directAxisRebaseParameter (D : DirectLdParams)
   390	    (line : AxisParallelLine D.toLDTParameters) : DirectScalarQ D :=
   391	  directLineRepParameter (coordinateDirection (Fin.rev line.direction))
   392	    (ldtPointToDirect D line.base)
   393	
   394	/-- Canonical rebase parameter for an LDT diagonal line. -/
   395	noncomputable def directDiagonalRebaseParameter (D : DirectLdParams)
   396	    (line : DiagonalLine D.toLDTParameters) : DirectScalarQ D :=
   397	  directLineRepParameter (ldtPointToDirect D line.direction)
   398	    (ldtPointToDirect D line.base)
   399	
   400	/-- Axis-line canonical parameters add under LDT line rebasing. -/
   401	theorem directAxisRebaseParameter_rebase (D : DirectLdParams)
   402	    (line : AxisParallelLine D.toLDTParameters)
   403	    (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters) :
   404	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   405	    directAxisRebaseParameter D (line.rebaseAt t) =
   406	      directAxisRebaseParameter D line + (directScalarEquiv D).symm t := by
   407	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   408	  unfold directAxisRebaseParameter
   409	  rw [ldtPointToDirect_axis_rebase]
   410	  exact directLineRepParameter_add_smul
   411	    (coordinateDirection_ne_zero (Fin.rev line.direction)) _
   412	
   413	/-- Nonzero diagonal-line canonical parameters add under LDT line rebasing. -/
   414	theorem directDiagonalRebaseParameter_rebase (D : DirectLdParams)
   415	    (line : DiagonalLine D.toLDTParameters)
   416	    (t : Fq D.toLDTParameters)
   417	    (hdir : ldtPointToDirect D line.direction ≠ 0) :
   418	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   419	    directDiagonalRebaseParameter D (line.rebaseAt t) =
   420	      directDiagonalRebaseParameter D line + (directScalarEquiv D).symm t := by

     7	/-!
     8	# Simultaneous polynomial measurements for the direct low-degree game
     9	
    10	This module applies the quantum soundness theorem of the low individual
    11	degree test to each coordinate of a projective strategy for the directly
    12	indexed low-degree game, transports the Schwartz--Zippel collision estimate
    13	to the direct polynomial representatives, and, for simultaneity parameter
    14	`1`, obtains the polynomial-tuple conclusion of `lem:ld-soundness` from the
    15	coordinate conclusions.
    16	
    17	## The simultaneity obstruction
    18	
    19	For simultaneity parameter `k ≥ 2` the coordinate conclusions alone do not
    20	determine simultaneous polynomial measurements, so no palindromic combination
    21	of the coordinate measurements can be consistent with a joint point
    22	measurement in general.  Let `q = 2^s`, let the degree be `1`, and let Bob
    23	measure the univariate polynomials `g = g₀ + g₁ x` once in the standard basis
    24	`|g⟩` and once in the Fourier basis attached to the symmetric pairing
    25	`⟨h, g⟩ = h₀ g₁ + h₁ g₀`.  In characteristic two every evaluation functional
    26	`h ↦ h(u)` is represented by an isotropic vector of this pairing, so at every
    27	point `u` the value-level coarse-grainings `Q^{1,u}_{[a]}` (Fourier basis) and
    28	`Q^{2,u}_{[b]}` (standard basis) commute, and on the maximally entangled state
    29	Alice may answer point questions with the joint projective measurement
    30	`P^u_{a,b} = (Q^{1,u}_{[a]} Q^{2,u}_{[b]})ᵀ`.  All coordinate consistencies of
    31	`lem:ld-soundness` then hold with defect `0` and distinct polynomials collide
    32	at a uniform point with probability `1 / q`, but the sandwiched POVM has
    33	`∑_{g₂(u) = b} |g₂⟩⟨g₂| Q^{1,u}_{[a]} |g₂⟩⟨g₂| = q⁻¹ Q^{2,u}_{[b]}`, whose
    34	consistency defect against `P^u` is `1 - 1/q`; more strongly, every
    35	polynomial-pair POVM on Bob's side has defect at least `1 - 2/q` against
    36	`P^u`.  No bound of the form `C k √(δ + m d / q)` holds for a universal `C`.
    37	The source obtains the general case not coordinatewise but by the combining
    38	reduction of Theorem 4.43 in the NEEXP paper, which applies the `k = 1`
    39	theorem once, in dimension `m + k`, to a combined strategy; that reduction is
    40	not formalized here.  The two-measurement pasting estimate (Fact 4.35 there)
    41	does not apply either, since it evaluates the two coordinates at
    42	independently sampled points while the low-degree game evaluates all
    43	coordinates at one point.  The counterexample and the resulting formal
    44	status are recorded in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-simultaneous-sandwich.tex`.
    45

    47

    49	* `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:465-501`

    54	* `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-simultaneous-sandwich.tex`
    55	-/

    67	/-! ## Direct polynomial collision estimate -/
    68	
    69	/-- Two distinct direct polynomial representatives agree at a uniformly

   324		of the field size are unchanged.  The degree is unchanged because the
   325		combining map of Definition~\ref{def:ld-combining-map} is linear in the
   326		fresh coordinates and therefore, in the individual-degree class of
   327		Definition~\ref{def:polyfunc}, raises no individual degree above $d$ as soon
   328		as $d \ge 1$.  The source works with total degree and passes from $d$ to
   329		$d+1$ at this step; that increment is an artifact of the total-degree
   330		formulation and does not occur here.

1	import MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.Polynomials
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# The combining map on tuples of low individual degree polynomials
     5	
     6	The extension of the quantum soundness of the low individual degree test from
     7	simultaneity parameter `1` to a general simultaneity parameter `k` is obtained
     8	in the source by a reduction, not coordinatewise: the `k` answer polynomials
     9	`g_0, …, g_{k-1}` in `m` variables are combined into the single polynomial
    10	
    11	`comb(g)(u, α) = ∑_{r < k} α_r g_r(u)`
    12	
    13	in `m + k` variables, the case `k = 1` is applied once in dimension `m + k`,
    14	and the `k` polynomials are recovered from the resulting outcome by exact
    15	linearity in the combining variables `α` together with the Schwartz--Zippel
    16	lemma.  This module develops the polynomial algebra of that combining map: the
    17	coordinate split of `Fin (m + k)`, the map itself, its evaluation identity, its
    18	individual-degree bound, and the substitution recovering the `r`-th component,
    19	which exhibits the map as injective.
    20	
    21	The combining map of `def:combine-map` (`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Defs.lean`)
    22	is the special case of two components used by the Chapter 15 combining
    23	argument, written there in the fixed coordinate layout of that chapter; the
    24	present map is the general `k`-component form required by the reduction, in the
    25	coordinate layout of the directly indexed low-degree game, where the `m` point
    26	coordinates precede the `k` combining coordinates.
    27	
    28	## Main definitions
    29	
    30	* `combinedPointVar`, `combinedCoefficientVar` — the two coordinate blocks of
    31	  the combined dimension `m + k`.
    32	* `combinePolyTuple` — the combining map on tuples of polynomials.
    33	* `splitCombinedPoly` — the substitution `α ↦ e_r` recovering the `r`-th
    34	  component of a combined polynomial.
    35	
    36	## References
    37	
    38	* `references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex:1409-1503`
    39	  (the derivation of Theorem 4.43 from Theorem 4.40)
    40	* `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`
    41	* `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:240-250`
    42	* `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-simultaneous-sandwich.tex`
    43	-/
    44	
    45	open scoped BigOperators
    46	
    47	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    48	
    49	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    50	
    51	noncomputable section
    52	
    53	/-! ## The coordinates of the combined dimension -/
    54	
    55	/-- The point coordinates of the combined dimension `m + k`.  The `m` point
    56	coordinates come first, so that zeroing a prefix of a direction of the combined
    57	space restricts to zeroing the corresponding prefix of its point part. -/
    58	def combinedPointVar (m k : ℕ) (j : Fin m) : Fin (m + k) :=
    59	  finSumFinEquiv (Sum.inl j)
    60	
    61	/-- The combining coordinates of the combined dimension `m + k`.  Coordinate
    62	`combinedCoefficientVar m k r` carries the scalar `α_r` multiplying the `r`-th
    63	component of a polynomial tuple. -/
    64	def combinedCoefficientVar (m k : ℕ) (r : Fin k) : Fin (m + k) :=
    65	  finSumFinEquiv (Sum.inr r)
    66	
    67	theorem combinedPointVar_injective (m k : ℕ) :
    68	    Function.Injective (combinedPointVar m k) := by
    69	  intro j j' h
    70	  simpa using finSumFinEquiv.injective h
    71	
    72	theorem combinedCoefficientVar_injective (m k : ℕ) :
    73	    Function.Injective (combinedCoefficientVar m k) := by
    74	  intro r r' h
    75	  simpa using finSumFinEquiv.injective h
    76	
    77	/-- The two coordinate blocks of the combined dimension are disjoint. -/
    78	theorem combinedCoefficientVar_ne_combinedPointVar (m k : ℕ) (r : Fin k) (j : Fin m) :
    79	    combinedCoefficientVar m k r ≠ combinedPointVar m k j := by
    80	  intro h
    81	  have := finSumFinEquiv.injective h
    82	  simp at this
    83	
    84	theorem combinedCoefficientVar_notMem_range (m k : ℕ) (r : Fin k) :
    85	    combinedCoefficientVar m k r ∉ Set.range (combinedPointVar m k) := by
    86	  rintro ⟨j, hj⟩
    87	  exact combinedCoefficientVar_ne_combinedPointVar m k r j hj.symm
    88	
    89	/-- The point part of a point of the combined space. -/
    90	def combinedPointPart {K : Type*} {m k : ℕ} (z : Fin (m + k) → K) : Fin m → K :=
    91	  fun j => z (combinedPointVar m k j)
    92	
    93	/-- The combining part of a point of the combined space. -/
    94	def combinedCoefficientPart {K : Type*} {m k : ℕ} (z : Fin (m + k) → K) : Fin k → K :=
    95	  fun r => z (combinedCoefficientVar m k r)
    96	
    97	/-- The point of the combined space with the given point and combining parts. -/
    98	def combinedPoint {K : Type*} {m k : ℕ} (u : Fin m → K) (α : Fin k → K) :
    99	    Fin (m + k) → K :=
   100	  fun i => Sum.elim u α (finSumFinEquiv.symm i)
   101	
   102	@[simp] theorem combinedPointPart_combinedPoint {K : Type*} {m k : ℕ}
   103	    (u : Fin m → K) (α : Fin k → K) :
   104	    combinedPointPart (combinedPoint u α) = u := by
   105	  funext j
   106	  simp [combinedPointPart, combinedPoint, combinedPointVar]
   107	
   108	@[simp] theorem combinedCoefficientPart_combinedPoint {K : Type*} {m k : ℕ}
   109	    (u : Fin m → K) (α : Fin k → K) :
   110	    combinedCoefficientPart (combinedPoint u α) = α := by
   111	  funext r
   112	  simp [combinedCoefficientPart, combinedPoint, combinedCoefficientVar]
   113	
   114	/-! ## The combining map -/
   115	
   116	/-- The combining map of the reduction: the tuple `g` is sent to the polynomial
   117	`(u, α) ↦ ∑_{r < k} α_r g_r(u)` in `m + k` variables.
   118	
   119	Source `references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex:1425-1435`. -/
   120	def combinePolyTuple {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m k : ℕ}
   121	    (g : Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) : MvPolynomial (Fin (m + k)) K :=
   122	  ∑ r : Fin k, MvPolynomial.X (combinedCoefficientVar m k r) *
   123	    MvPolynomial.rename (combinedPointVar m k) (g r)
   124	
   125	/-- Evaluation of a combined polynomial is the displayed combining formula. -/
   126	theorem combinePolyTuple_eval {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m k : ℕ}
   127	    (g : Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) (z : Fin (m + k) → K) :
   128	    MvPolynomial.eval z (combinePolyTuple g) =
   129	      ∑ r : Fin k, combinedCoefficientPart z r *
   130	        MvPolynomial.eval (combinedPointPart z) (g r) := by
   131	  simp only [combinePolyTuple, map_sum, map_mul, MvPolynomial.eval_X,
   132	    MvPolynomial.eval_rename, combinedCoefficientPart]
   133	  rfl
   134	
   135	/-- Evaluation of a combined polynomial at a point given by its two blocks. -/
   136	theorem combinePolyTuple_eval_combinedPoint {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m k : ℕ}
   137	    (g : Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) (u : Fin m → K) (α : Fin k → K) :
   138	    MvPolynomial.eval (combinedPoint u α) (combinePolyTuple g) =
   139	      ∑ r : Fin k, α r * MvPolynomial.eval u (g r) := by
   140	  rw [combinePolyTuple_eval, combinedPointPart_combinedPoint,
   141	    combinedCoefficientPart_combinedPoint]
   142	
   143	/-! ## Recovering the components -/
   144	
   145	/-- The substitution sending each point coordinate to its own variable and the
   146	combining coordinates to the `r`-th standard basis vector.  Applied to a
   147	combined polynomial it returns the `r`-th component of the tuple. -/
   148	def combinedSubstitution (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K] (m k : ℕ) (r : Fin k) :
   149	    Fin (m + k) → MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
   150	  fun i => Sum.elim (fun j : Fin m => MvPolynomial.X j)
   151	    (fun s : Fin k => if s = r then 1 else 0) (finSumFinEquiv.symm i)
   152	
   153	@[simp] theorem combinedSubstitution_point (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K] (m k : ℕ)
   154	    (r : Fin k) (j : Fin m) :
   155	    combinedSubstitution K m k r (combinedPointVar m k j) = MvPolynomial.X j := by
   156	  simp [combinedSubstitution, combinedPointVar]
   157	
   158	@[simp] theorem combinedSubstitution_coefficient (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K] (m k : ℕ)
   159	    (r s : Fin k) :
   160	    combinedSubstitution K m k r (combinedCoefficientVar m k s) =
   161	      if s = r then 1 else 0 := by
   162	  simp [combinedSubstitution, combinedCoefficientVar]
   163	
   164	/-- The `r`-th component of a polynomial in the combined variables: substitute
   165	the `r`-th standard basis vector for the combining variables. -/
   166	def splitCombinedPoly {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m k : ℕ}
   167	    (p : MvPolynomial (Fin (m + k)) K) (r : Fin k) : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
   168	  MvPolynomial.aeval (combinedSubstitution K m k r) p
   169	
   170	/-- The components of a combined polynomial are the polynomials it combines. -/
   171	theorem splitCombinedPoly_combinePolyTuple {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m k : ℕ}
   172	    (g : Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) (r : Fin k) :
   173	    splitCombinedPoly (combinePolyTuple g) r = g r := by
   174	  classical
   175	  have hcomp : (combinedSubstitution K m k r) ∘ (combinedPointVar m k) =
   176	      (MvPolynomial.X : Fin m → MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) := by
   177	    funext j
   178	    exact combinedSubstitution_point K m k r j
   179	  have hterm : ∀ s : Fin k,
   180	      MvPolynomial.aeval (combinedSubstitution K m k r)
   181	          (MvPolynomial.X (combinedCoefficientVar m k s) *
   182	            MvPolynomial.rename (combinedPointVar m k) (g s)) =
   183	        (if s = r then 1 else 0) * g s := by
   184	    intro s
   185	    rw [map_mul, MvPolynomial.aeval_X, combinedSubstitution_coefficient,
   186	      MvPolynomial.aeval_rename, hcomp, MvPolynomial.aeval_X_left_apply]
   187	  rw [splitCombinedPoly, combinePolyTuple, map_sum]
   188	  simp only [hterm, ite_mul, one_mul, zero_mul]
   189	  simp
   190	
   191	/-- The combining map is injective: the components of a combined polynomial are
   192	determined by it. -/
   193	theorem combinePolyTuple_injective {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m k : ℕ} :
   194	    Function.Injective (combinePolyTuple (K := K) (m := m) (k := k)) := by
   195	  intro g g' h
   196	  funext r
   197	  rw [← splitCombinedPoly_combinePolyTuple g r, h,
   198	    splitCombinedPoly_combinePolyTuple]
   199	
   200	/-! ## The individual-degree bound -/
   201	
   202	/-- Membership in the low individual degree class from a bound on every
   203	individual degree.  This is the converse direction of
   204	`degreeOf_le_of_mem_polyFunc`. -/
   205	theorem mem_polyFunc_of_degreeOf_le {m d : ℕ} {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K]
   206	    {p : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K} (h : ∀ i, p.degreeOf i ≤ d) :
   207	    p ∈ polyFunc m K d := by
   208	  rw [MvPolynomial.mem_restrictDegree]
   209	  exact fun s hs i => MvPolynomial.degreeOf_le_iff.mp (h i) s hs
   210	
   211	private theorem degreeOf_X_le_one {τ K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] (c i : τ) :
   212	    (MvPolynomial.X c : MvPolynomial τ K).degreeOf i ≤ 1 := by
   213	  rw [MvPolynomial.degreeOf_le_iff]
   214	  intro s hs
   215	  have hs' : s ∈ ({Finsupp.single c 1} : Finset (τ →₀ ℕ)) :=
   216	    MvPolynomial.support_monomial_subset hs
   217	  rw [Finset.mem_singleton] at hs'
   218	  subst hs'
   219	  by_cases h : c = i
   220	  · simp [h]
   221	  · simp [h]
   222	
   223	private theorem degreeOf_X_eq_zero_of_ne {τ K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {c i : τ}
   224	    (h : i ≠ c) : (MvPolynomial.X c : MvPolynomial τ K).degreeOf i = 0 := by
   225	  rw [← Nat.le_zero, MvPolynomial.degreeOf_le_iff]
   226	  intro s hs
   227	  have hs' : s ∈ ({Finsupp.single c 1} : Finset (τ →₀ ℕ)) :=
   228	    MvPolynomial.support_monomial_subset hs
   229	  rw [Finset.mem_singleton] at hs'
   230	  subst hs'
   231	  simp [Ne.symm h]
   232	
   233	private theorem degreeOf_rename_le {σ τ K : Type*} [CommSemiring K]
   234	    {f : σ → τ} (hf : Function.Injective f) {p : MvPolynomial σ K} {d : ℕ}
   235	    (hp : ∀ j : σ, p.degreeOf j ≤ d) (i : τ) :
   236	    (MvPolynomial.rename f p).degreeOf i ≤ d := by
   237	  classical
   238	  rw [MvPolynomial.degreeOf_le_iff]
   239	  intro s hs
   240	  rw [MvPolynomial.support_rename_of_injective hf] at hs
   241	  obtain ⟨t, ht, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hs
   242	  by_cases hi : ∃ j, f j = i
   243	  · obtain ⟨j, rfl⟩ := hi
   244	    rw [Finsupp.mapDomain_apply hf]
   245	    exact le_trans (MvPolynomial.le_degreeOf_of_mem_support j ht) (hp j)
   246	  · rw [Finsupp.mapDomain_notin_range t i (by simpa using hi)]
   247	    exact Nat.zero_le d
   248	
   249	private theorem degreeOf_rename_eq_zero_of_notMem_range {σ τ K : Type*} [CommSemiring K]
   250	    {f : σ → τ} (hf : Function.Injective f) (p : MvPolynomial σ K)
   251	    {i : τ} (hi : i ∉ Set.range f) :
   252	    (MvPolynomial.rename f p).degreeOf i = 0 := by
   253	  classical
   254	  rw [← Nat.le_zero, MvPolynomial.degreeOf_le_iff]
   255	  intro s hs
   256	  rw [MvPolynomial.support_rename_of_injective hf] at hs
   257	  obtain ⟨t, _, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hs
   258	  exact le_of_eq (Finsupp.mapDomain_notin_range t i hi)
   259	
   260	/-- The combining map preserves the individual-degree bound.  The two coordinate
   261	blocks are disjoint: a component polynomial depends only on the point
   262	coordinates, so multiplying it by a combining variable leaves its individual
   263	degrees in the point block unchanged and produces individual degree one in the
   264	fresh combining coordinate.  The hypothesis `1 ≤ d` supplies exactly the bound
   265	needed on that fresh coordinate; no bound `d + 1` is introduced.  This is the
   266	individual-degree counterpart of the degree-`d + 1` bound used for total degree
   267	in `references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex:1435-1440`. -/
   268	theorem combinePolyTuple_mem_polyFunc {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m k d : ℕ}
   269	    (hd : 1 ≤ d) (g : Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin m) K)
   270	    (hg : ∀ r, g r ∈ polyFunc m K d) :
   271	    combinePolyTuple g ∈ polyFunc (m + k) K d := by
   272	  classical
   273	  refine Submodule.sum_mem _ fun r _ => mem_polyFunc_of_degreeOf_le fun i => ?_
   274	  refine le_trans (MvPolynomial.degreeOf_mul_le i _ _) ?_
   275	  by_cases hi : i ∈ Set.range (combinedPointVar m k)
   276	  · have hne : i ≠ combinedCoefficientVar m k r := by
   277	      rintro rfl
   278	      exact combinedCoefficientVar_notMem_range m k r hi
   279	    rw [degreeOf_X_eq_zero_of_ne hne, zero_add]
   280	    exact degreeOf_rename_le (combinedPointVar_injective m k)
   281	      (fun j => degreeOf_le_of_mem_polyFunc (hg r) j) i
   282	  · rw [degreeOf_rename_eq_zero_of_notMem_range (combinedPointVar_injective m k) _ hi,
   283	      add_zero]
   284	    exact le_trans (degreeOf_X_le_one _ _) hd
   285	
   286	end

     5	/-!
     6	# The combined strategy of the simultaneity reduction
     7	
     8	`def:ld-combined-strategy` turns a projective strategy for the directly indexed
     9	low-degree game at parameters `D` into a projective strategy for the same game
    10	at the combined parameters `D.combined` of `def:ld-combining-parameters`, on
    11	the same state and the same two Hilbert spaces.  Each question of the combined
    12	game is answered by measuring one question of the original strategy and
    13	relabelling its outcome; the question measured and the relabelling are fixed by
    14	the type of the combined question and by whether its stored coordinate index is
    15	a point coordinate or a combining coordinate.
    16	
    17	Writing a point of the combined space as `(u, α)` with `u` its point part and
    18	`α` its combining part, the five cases are:
    19	
    20	1. a point question at `(u, α)` measures the point question at `u` and answers
    21	   the combined value `∑ r, α r * b r`;
    22	2. an axis-parallel line question whose stored index is the point coordinate
    23	   `j` measures the canonical axis-parallel line question of the original game
    24	   at `u` with index `j`, and answers the combination `∑ r, α r * f r` of the
    25	   measured line answers;
    26	3. an axis-parallel line question whose stored index is a combining coordinate
    27	   measures the point question at `u`: the line lies in the fiber of the
    28	   projection to the point coordinates through `u`, so the combined polynomial
    29	   restricted to it is the affine function of the parameter determined by the
    30	   `k` values at `u`;
    31	4. a diagonal line question whose stored index is the point coordinate `j`
    32	   measures the canonical diagonal line question of the original game at `u`
    33	   with index `j` and the point part of the direction, and answers
    34	   `t ↦ ∑ r, (α r + t * w r) * f r (t + s)`;
    35	5. a diagonal line question whose stored index is a combining coordinate
    36	   measures the point question at `u`, its direction having vanishing point
    37	   part, and answers as in case 3.
    38	
    39	The affine shift `s` of cases 2 and 4 is `directCombinedRebaseParameter`, the
    40	change of parameter between the presentation of the image line by the point
    41	part of the combined canonical base and its presentation by its own canonical
    42	base; the two need not agree, since the canonical base of a line of the
    43	combined space need not project to the canonical base of its image.
    44	
    45	Each case measures a single measurement of the original strategy and relabels
    46	its outcome, so the combined strategy is again projective; this is
    47	`directCombinedStrategy_isProjective`.
    48	
    49	## Main definitions
    50	
    51	* `directCombinedMeasuredQuestion` — the question of the original game measured
    52	  on a question of the combined game.
    53	* `directCombinedAnswerMap` — the relabelling of the measured outcome.
    54	* `directCombinedStrategy` — `def:ld-combined-strategy`.
    55	
    56	## References
    57	
    58	* `references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex:1409-1503`
    59	* `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`
    60	* `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:420-472`
    61	-/

    73	/-! ## Coordinates of a combined question -/
    74	
    75	/-- The point part of a point of the combined space, at the combined
    76	parameters of `def:ld-combining-parameters`. -/
    77	def directCombinedPointPart (D : DirectLdParams)
    78	    (z : Fin D.combined.m → DirectScalarQ D) : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D :=
    79	  combinedPointPart (m := D.m) (k := D.k) z
    80	
    81	/-- The combining part of a point of the combined space. -/
    82	def directCombinedCoefficientPart (D : DirectLdParams)
    83	    (z : Fin D.combined.m → DirectScalarQ D) : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D :=
    84	  combinedCoefficientPart (m := D.m) (k := D.k) z
    85	
    86	@[simp] theorem directCombinedPointPart_combinedPoint (D : DirectLdParams)
    87	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (α : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) :
    88	    directCombinedPointPart D (combinedPoint u α) = u :=
    89	  combinedPointPart_combinedPoint u α
    90	
    91	@[simp] theorem directCombinedCoefficientPart_combinedPoint (D : DirectLdParams)
    92	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (α : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) :
    93	    directCombinedCoefficientPart D (combinedPoint u α) = α :=
    94	  combinedCoefficientPart_combinedPoint u α
    95	
    96	/-- A coordinate of the combined dimension is either a point coordinate or a
    97	combining coordinate. -/
    98	def directCombinedIndexSplit (D : DirectLdParams) (i : Fin D.combined.m) :
    99	    Fin D.m ⊕ Fin D.k :=
   100	  finSumFinEquiv.symm i
   101	
   102	@[simp] theorem directCombinedIndexSplit_combinedPointVar (D : DirectLdParams)
   103	    (j : Fin D.m) :
   104	    directCombinedIndexSplit D (combinedPointVar D.m D.k j) = Sum.inl j := by
   105	  simp [directCombinedIndexSplit, combinedPointVar]
   106	
   107	@[simp] theorem directCombinedIndexSplit_combinedCoefficientVar
   108	    (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k) :
   109	    directCombinedIndexSplit D (combinedCoefficientVar D.m D.k r) = Sum.inr r := by
   110	  simp [directCombinedIndexSplit, combinedCoefficientVar]
   111	
   112	/-- The geometric direction of the line carried by a question of the combined
   113	game; the zero direction on point questions. -/
   114	def directCombinedQuestionDirection (D : DirectLdParams)
   115	    (q : DirectLdQuestion D.combined) : Fin D.combined.m → DirectScalarQ D :=
   116	  match q.1 with
   117	  | .point => 0
   118	  | .aline => coordinateDirection q.2.index
   119	  | .dline => q.2.direction
   120	
   121	/-! ## The measured question -/
   122	
   123	/-- The direction of the line of the original game measured on a question of
   124	the combined game.  It is the coordinate direction of the stored point
   125	coordinate for an axis-parallel question, and the prefix projection of the
   126	point part of the combined direction for a diagonal question; on the three
   127	cases measuring a point question it is the zero direction. -/
   128	def directCombinedMeasuredDirection (D : DirectLdParams)
   129	    (q : DirectLdQuestion D.combined) : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D :=
   130	  match q.1, directCombinedIndexSplit D q.2.index with
   131	  | .aline, .inl j => coordinateDirection j
   132	  | .dline, .inl j =>
   133	      directPrefixProjection j (directCombinedPointPart D q.2.direction)
   134	  | _, _ => 0
   135	
   136	/-- The change of parameter between the presentation of the measured line by
   137	the point part of the canonical base of the combined line and its presentation
   138	by its own canonical base.  It is the canonical parameter of that line for the
   139	measured direction; it is needed because the canonical base of a line of the
   140	combined space need not project to the canonical base of its image line. -/
   141	def directCombinedRebaseParameter (D : DirectLdParams)
   142	    (q : DirectLdQuestion D.combined) : DirectScalarQ D :=
   143	  directLineRepParameter (directCombinedMeasuredDirection D q)
   144	    (directCombinedPointPart D q.2.point)
   145	
   146	/-- The question of the original game measured by the combined strategy on a
   147	question of the combined game.  This is the case distinction of
   148	`def:ld-combined-strategy`: cases 1, 3 and 5 measure a point question, case 2
   149	an axis-parallel line question, and case 4 a diagonal line question. -/
   150	def directCombinedMeasuredQuestion (D : DirectLdParams)
   151	    (q : DirectLdQuestion D.combined) : DirectLdQuestion D :=
   152	  match q.1, directCombinedIndexSplit D q.2.index with
   153	  | .aline, .inl j =>
   154	      (.aline, directLdMap D .aline
   155	        ⟨directCombinedPointPart D q.2.point, j, 0⟩)
   156	  | .dline, .inl j =>
   157	      (.dline, directLdMap D .dline
   158	        ⟨directCombinedPointPart D q.2.point, j,
   159	          directCombinedPointPart D q.2.direction⟩)
   160	  | _, _ => directLdPointQuestionOf D (directCombinedPointPart D q.2.point)
   161	
   162	/-! ## The relabelling of the measured outcome -/
   163	
   164	/-- The relabelling by which the combined strategy answers a question of the
   165	combined game from the outcome of the measured question of the original game.
   166	An outcome whose constructor does not match the measured question type is sent
   167	to the zero answer of the constructor required by the combined question type,
   168	which the combined win predicate treats exactly as the original win predicate
   169	treats the mismatched outcome. -/
   170	def directCombinedAnswerMap (D : DirectLdParams)
   171	    (q : DirectLdQuestion D.combined) (a : DirectLdAnswer D) :
   172	    DirectLdAnswer D.combined :=
   173	  let α := directCombinedCoefficientPart D q.2.point
   174	  let w := directCombinedCoefficientPart D (directCombinedQuestionDirection D q)
   175	  let s := directCombinedRebaseParameter D q
   176	  match q.1, directCombinedIndexSplit D q.2.index with
   177	  | .point, _ =>
   178	      .pointVals fun _ =>
   179	        match a with
   180	        | .pointVals b => ∑ r : Fin D.k, α r * b r
   181	        | .alinePolys _ => 0
   182	        | .dlinePolys _ => 0
   183	  | .aline, .inl _ =>
   184	      .alinePolys fun _ =>
   185	        match a with
   186	        | .alinePolys f =>
   187	            coefficientsOfPolynomial D.combined.d (combinedAxisPolynomial α s f)
   188	        | .pointVals _ => 0
   189	        | .dlinePolys _ => 0
   190	  | .aline, .inr _ =>
   191	      .alinePolys fun _ =>
   192	        match a with
   193	        | .pointVals b =>
   194	            coefficientsOfPolynomial D.combined.d (fiberLinePolynomial α w b)
   195	        | .alinePolys _ => 0
   196	        | .dlinePolys _ => 0
   197	  | .dline, .inl _ =>
   198	      .dlinePolys fun _ =>
   199	        match a with
   200	        | .dlinePolys f =>
   201	            coefficientsOfPolynomial (D.combined.m * D.combined.d)
   202	              (combinedDiagonalPolynomial α w s f)
   203	        | .pointVals _ => 0
   204	        | .alinePolys _ => 0
   205	  | .dline, .inr _ =>
   206	      .dlinePolys fun _ =>
   207	        match a with
   208	        | .pointVals b =>
   209	            coefficientsOfPolynomial (D.combined.m * D.combined.d)
   210	              (fiberLinePolynomial α w b)
   211	        | .alinePolys _ => 0
   212	        | .dlinePolys _ => 0
   213	
   214	/-! ## The combined strategy -/
   215	
   216	/-- The combined strategy of `def:ld-combined-strategy`: the same state and the
   217	same two Hilbert spaces, each question of the combined game answered by
   218	measuring `directCombinedMeasuredQuestion` and relabelling its outcome by
   219	`directCombinedAnswerMap`. -/
   220	def directCombinedStrategy (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) :
   221	    Strategy (directLdGame D.combined) where
   222	  ιA := S.ιA
   223	  ιB := S.ιB
   224	  ψ := S.ψ
   225	  ψ_norm := S.ψ_norm
   226	  A := fun q =>
   227	    (S.A (directCombinedMeasuredQuestion D q)).postprocess
   228	      (directCombinedAnswerMap D q)
   229	  B := fun q =>
   230	    (S.B (directCombinedMeasuredQuestion D q)).postprocess
   231	      (directCombinedAnswerMap D q)
   232	
   233	@[simp] theorem directCombinedStrategy_state (D : DirectLdParams)
   234	    (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) : (directCombinedStrategy D S).ψ = S.ψ := rfl
   235	
   236	@[simp] theorem directCombinedStrategy_A (D : DirectLdParams)
   237	    (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) (q : DirectLdQuestion D.combined) :
   238	    (directCombinedStrategy D S).A q =
   239	      (S.A (directCombinedMeasuredQuestion D q)).postprocess
   240	        (directCombinedAnswerMap D q) := rfl
   241	
   242	@[simp] theorem directCombinedStrategy_B (D : DirectLdParams)
   243	    (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) (q : DirectLdQuestion D.combined) :
   244	    (directCombinedStrategy D S).B q =
   245	      (S.B (directCombinedMeasuredQuestion D q)).postprocess
   246	        (directCombinedAnswerMap D q) := rfl
   247	
   248	/-- Projectivity transfer for `def:ld-combined-strategy`: each measurement of
   249	the combined strategy is a coarse-graining of a measurement of the original
   250	strategy, and coarse-graining preserves projectivity. -/
   251	theorem directCombinedStrategy_isProjective (D : DirectLdParams)
   252	    (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) (hS : S.IsProjective) :
   253	    (directCombinedStrategy D S).IsProjective := by
   254	  refine ⟨fun q => ?_, fun q => ?_⟩
   255	  · exact MIPStarRE.QPBT.SandwichProduct.postprocess_isProjective _ (hS.1 _) _
   256	  · exact MIPStarRE.QPBT.SandwichProduct.postprocess_isProjective _ (hS.2 _) _
   257	
   258	end
   259	
   260	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

45	noncomputable def directEvalOpt {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ}
    46	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    47	    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) : Option (DirectScalarQ D) := by
    48	  classical
    49	  exact if h : ∃ a : DirectScalarQ D, DirectEvaluatesTo line f u a then
    50	    some (Classical.choose h)
    51	  else none
    52	
    53	/-- The typed question alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/
    54	abbrev DirectLdQuestion (D : DirectLdParams) := LdType × DirectLdSpace D
    55	
    56	/-- Canonicalize a common direct sample for one question type.  Irrelevant
    57	coordinates are fixed, so point questions reveal no sampled line index and
    58	axis-line questions reveal no diagonal direction. -/
    59	noncomputable def directLdMap (D : DirectLdParams) :
    60	    LdType → DirectLdSpace D → DirectLdSpace D
    61	  | .point, sample => ⟨sample.point, D.firstIndex, 0⟩
    62	  | .aline, sample =>
    63	      let direction := coordinateDirection sample.index
    64	      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, 0⟩
    65	  | .dline, sample =>
    66	      let direction := directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction
    67	      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, direction⟩
    68	
    69	/-- The directly indexed question distribution.  It has the same uniform
    70	ordered type-pair branches as `ldQuestionDistribution`, but its common sample
    71	contains an actual coordinate index rather than a field seed. -/
    72	noncomputable def directLdQuestionDistribution (D : DirectLdParams) :
    73	    Distribution (DirectLdQuestion D × DirectLdQuestion D) :=
    74	  (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>
    75	    ((sample.1.1, directLdMap D sample.1.1 sample.2),
    76	      (sample.1.2, directLdMap D sample.1.2 sample.2))
    77	
    78	/-- The directly indexed question law is probabilistic. -/
    79	theorem directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :
    80	    (directLdQuestionDistribution D).IsProbability := by
    81	  exact (uniformDistribution_isProbability
    82	    ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map _
    83	
    84	/-- The answer alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/
    85	inductive DirectLdAnswer (D : DirectLdParams) where
    86	  | pointVals (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D)
    87	  | alinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
    88	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
    89	  deriving DecidableEq
    90	
    91	/-- A finite code for the directly indexed answer alphabet. -/
    92	abbrev DirectLdAnswerCode (D : DirectLdParams) :=
    93	  (Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
    94	    ((Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
    95	      (Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D))
    96	
    97	/-- The canonical code equivalence for `DirectLdAnswer`, sending point,
    98	axis-line, and diagonal-line answers to the three summands. -/
    99	noncomputable def directLdAnswerEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   100	    DirectLdAnswer D ≃ DirectLdAnswerCode D where
   101	  toFun
   102	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   103	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   104	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   105	  invFun
   106	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   107	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   108	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   109	  left_inv := by intro answer; cases answer <;> rfl
   110	  right_inv := by
   111	    intro answer
   112	    rcases answer with a | a
   113	    · rfl
   114	    · rcases a with a | a <;> rfl
   115	
   116	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Inhabited (DirectLdAnswer D) :=
   117	  ⟨.pointVals 0⟩
   118	
   119	noncomputable instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Fintype (DirectLdAnswer D) :=
   120	  Fintype.ofEquiv (DirectLdAnswerCode D) (directLdAnswerEquiv D).symm
   121	
   122	/-- Check that a direct-game answer has the constructor required by its
   123	question type. -/
   124	def validDirectLdAnswer {D : DirectLdParams} (t : LdType)
   125	    (answer : DirectLdAnswer D) : Bool :=
   126	  match t, answer with
   127	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   128	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   129	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   130	  | _, _ => false
   131	
   132	/-- The directly indexed axis-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
   133	def directAlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)
   134	    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)
   135	    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
   136	    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
   137	  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,
   138	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection line.index →
   139	      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   140	
   141	/-- The directly indexed diagonal-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
   142	def directDlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)
   143	    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)
   144	    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
   145	    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
   146	  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,
   147	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   148	      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   149	
   150	/-- The directly indexed low-degree win predicate.  It differs from
   151	`ldWinPredicate` only by reading the coordinate index directly from each line
   152	question. -/
   153	noncomputable def directLdWinPredicate (D : DirectLdParams) :
   154	    DirectLdQuestion D → DirectLdQuestion D →
   155	      DirectLdAnswer D → DirectLdAnswer D → Bool :=
   156	  open Classical in
   157	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   158	    if validDirectLdAnswer tA a && validDirectLdAnswer tB b then
   159	      match tA, tB, a, b with
   160	      | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   161	      | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   162	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   163	      | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   164	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   165	      | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   166	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   167	      | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   168	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   169	      | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   170	      | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   171	      | _, _, _, _ => true
   172	    else false
   173	
   174	/-- The directly indexed low-degree game at an arbitrary positive dimension.
   175	It is an internal analysis game, not the conditionally linear verifier game
   176	`ldGame`. -/
   177	noncomputable def directLdGame (D : DirectLdParams) : Game where
   178	  QuestionA := DirectLdQuestion D
   179	  QuestionB := DirectLdQuestion D
   180	  AnswerA := DirectLdAnswer D
   181	  AnswerB := DirectLdAnswer D
   182	  μ := directLdQuestionDistribution D
   183	  μ_prob := directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability D
   184	  decide := directLdWinPredicate D
   185	
   186	/-- The canonical point question associated with a geometric point. -/
   187	def directLdPointQuestionOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   188	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) : DirectLdQuestion D :=
   189	  (.point, ⟨u, D.firstIndex, 0⟩)
   190	
   191	/-- Total point-answer relabeling used in the direct soundness conclusion.
   192	Wrong-form answers are folded into the zero tuple, exactly as for
   193	`ldPointValuesOrZero`. -/
   194	def directLdPointValuesOrZero (D : DirectLdParams) :
   195	    DirectLdAnswer D → Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D
   196	  | .pointVals values => values
   197	  | .alinePolys _ => 0
   198	  | .dlinePolys _ => 0
   199	
   200	/-- A simultaneous tuple of bounded polynomials for the directly indexed
   201	game. -/
   202	noncomputable abbrev DirectPolyTuple (D : DirectLdParams) :=
   203	  Fin D.k → PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d
   204	
   205	/-- A polynomial-tuple POVM for the directly indexed game. -/
   206	noncomputable abbrev DirectPolyMeasTuple (D : DirectLdParams) (ι : Type*)
   207	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   208	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectPolyTuple D) ι
   209	
   210	/-- Evaluate every component of a direct polynomial tuple at a point. -/
   211	def evalDirectPolyTupleAt {D : DirectLdParams}
   212	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (g : DirectPolyTuple D) :
   213	    Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D :=
   214	  fun j => MvPolynomial.eval u (g j).1
   215	
   216	end
   217	
   218	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.DirectLowDegree.Transport.Combining.Strategy

     3	/-!
     4	# The questions measured by the combined strategy
     5	
     6	`lem:ld-combined-question-law` identifies the pair of questions measured by the
     7	combined strategy of `def:ld-combined-strategy` on a sample of the combined
     8	game.  The coordinate index of the common sample is uniform on the `m + k`
     9	coordinates of the combined dimension, and the identification splits according
    10	to whether that index is a point coordinate or a combining coordinate.
    11	
    12	On a point coordinate `j`, all three question types measure the canonical
    13	question of the same type of the original game attached to the *projected*
    14	sample `directCombinedSampleProjection`: the point part of the sampled point,
    15	the index `j`, and the point part of the sampled direction.  This uses the
    16	coordinate order of `def:ld-combining-map`: the point coordinates precede the
    17	combining coordinates, so the coordinate direction of a point coordinate has
    18	point part the corresponding coordinate direction, and the prefix projection at
    19	a point coordinate restricts to the prefix projection at that coordinate of the
    20	point part.
    21	
    22	On a combining coordinate, every direction produced by the question
    23	distribution has vanishing point part, so all three question types measure the
    24	point question at the point part of the sampled point.
    25	
    26	The projected sample is read from the *canonical* base of the combined line,
    27	which need not project to the canonical base of the image line; the two agree
    28	after rebasing along the image direction, which is
    29	`lineRepMap_directCombinedPointPart_lineRepMap`.
    30	
    31	## References
    32	
    33	* `references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex:1409-1503`
    34	* `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`
    35	* `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:473-508`
    36	-/
    37	
    38	open scoped BigOperators
    39	
    40	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    41	
    42	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    43	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    44	
    45	noncomputable section
    46	
    47	/-! ## Coordinates of the combined dimension -/
    48	
    49	@[simp] theorem combinedPointVar_val (m k : ℕ) (j : Fin m) :
    50	    (combinedPointVar m k j).val = j.val := by
    51	  simp [combinedPointVar]
    52	
    53	@[simp] theorem combinedCoefficientVar_val (m k : ℕ) (r : Fin k) :
    54	    (combinedCoefficientVar m k r).val = m + r.val := by
    55	  simp [combinedCoefficientVar]
    56	
    57	/-- The coordinate direction of a point coordinate of the combined dimension
    58	has point part the corresponding coordinate direction. -/
    59	@[simp] theorem directCombinedPointPart_coordinateDirection_pointVar
    60	    (D : DirectLdParams) (j : Fin D.m) :
    61	    directCombinedPointPart D (coordinateDirection (combinedPointVar D.m D.k j)) =
    62	      coordinateDirection j := by
    63	  funext j'
    64	  show (coordinateDirection (combinedPointVar D.m D.k j) :
    65	      Fin (D.m + D.k) → DirectScalarQ D) (combinedPointVar D.m D.k j') =
    66	    coordinateDirection j j'
    67	  by_cases h : j' = j
    68	  · subst h
    69	    rw [coordinateDirection, coordinateDirection, Pi.single_eq_same,
    70	      Pi.single_eq_same]
    71	  · rw [coordinateDirection, coordinateDirection,
    72	      Pi.single_eq_of_ne fun hc => h (combinedPointVar_injective D.m D.k hc),
    73	      Pi.single_eq_of_ne h]
    74	
    75	/-- The coordinate direction of a combining coordinate of the combined
    76	dimension has vanishing point part. -/
    77	@[simp] theorem directCombinedPointPart_coordinateDirection_coefficientVar
    78	    (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k) :
    79	    directCombinedPointPart D
    80	        (coordinateDirection (combinedCoefficientVar D.m D.k r)) = 0 := by
    81	  funext j
    82	  show (coordinateDirection (combinedCoefficientVar D.m D.k r) :
    83	      Fin (D.m + D.k) → DirectScalarQ D) (combinedPointVar D.m D.k j) = 0
    84	  rw [coordinateDirection,
    85	    Pi.single_eq_of_ne (combinedCoefficientVar_ne_combinedPointVar D.m D.k r j).symm]
    86	
    87	/-- Prefix projection at a point coordinate restricts to prefix projection at
    88	that coordinate of the point part.  This is the coordinate order of
    89	`def:ld-combining-map`: the point coordinates precede the combining ones. -/
    90	@[simp] theorem directCombinedPointPart_directPrefixProjection_pointVar
    91	    (D : DirectLdParams) (j : Fin D.m)
    92	    (w : Fin D.combined.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
    93	    directCombinedPointPart D
    94	        (directPrefixProjection (combinedPointVar D.m D.k j) w) =
    95	      directPrefixProjection j (directCombinedPointPart D w) := by
    96	  funext j'
    97	  show (if (combinedPointVar D.m D.k j').val < (combinedPointVar D.m D.k j).val
    98	      then 0 else w (combinedPointVar D.m D.k j')) =
    99	    if j'.val < j.val then 0 else directCombinedPointPart D w j'
   100	  rw [combinedPointVar_val, combinedPointVar_val]
   101	  rfl
   102	
   103	/-- Prefix projection at a combining coordinate annihilates the point part:
   104	every point coordinate precedes every combining coordinate. -/
   105	@[simp] theorem directCombinedPointPart_directPrefixProjection_coefficientVar
   106	    (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k)
   107	    (w : Fin D.combined.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
   108	    directCombinedPointPart D
   109	        (directPrefixProjection (combinedCoefficientVar D.m D.k r) w) = 0 := by
   110	  funext j'
   111	  show (if (combinedPointVar D.m D.k j').val <
   112	      (combinedCoefficientVar D.m D.k r).val
   113	      then 0 else w (combinedPointVar D.m D.k j')) = 0
   114	  rw [combinedPointVar_val, combinedCoefficientVar_val, if_pos]
   115	  omega

   117	/-! ## Canonical bases -/
   118	
   119	private theorem directCombinedPointPart_sub_smul (D : DirectLdParams)
   120	    (z V : Fin D.combined.m → DirectScalarQ D) (c : DirectScalarQ D) :
   121	    directCombinedPointPart D (z - c • V) =
   122	      directCombinedPointPart D z - c • directCombinedPointPart D V :=
   123	  rfl
   124	
   125	/-- A line of the combined space whose direction has vanishing point part lies
   126	in a fiber of the projection to the point coordinates, so its canonical base
   127	projects to the point part of every one of its points. -/
   128	theorem directCombinedPointPart_lineRepMap_of_pointPart_eq_zero
   129	    (D : DirectLdParams) (V z : Fin D.combined.m → DirectScalarQ D)
   130	    (hV : directCombinedPointPart D V = 0) :
   131	    directCombinedPointPart D (lineRepMap V z) = directCombinedPointPart D z := by
   132	  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := Submodule.mem_span_singleton.mp (sub_lineRepMap_mem_span V z)
   133	  have hz : lineRepMap V z = z - c • V := by rw [hc]; abel
   134	  rw [hz, directCombinedPointPart_sub_smul, hV, smul_zero, sub_zero]
   135	
   136	/-- The canonical base of a line of the combined space projects to a point of
   137	the image line, so rebasing its projection along the image direction returns
   138	the canonical base of the image line.  The canonical base of a line of the
   139	combined space need not itself project to the canonical base of its image; this
   140	is why the answer relabellings of `def:ld-combined-strategy` carry the affine
   141	shift `directCombinedRebaseParameter`. -/
   142	theorem lineRepMap_directCombinedPointPart_lineRepMap (D : DirectLdParams)
   143	    (V z : Fin D.combined.m → DirectScalarQ D) :

   154	/-- The sample of the original game to which a sample of the combined game

   162	/-- First half of `lem:ld-combined-question-law`: on a sample whose coordinate

   166	theorem directCombined_measuredQuestion_of_pointVar (D : DirectLdParams)

   172	  | point => rfl
   173	  | aline =>
   174	      have hbase := lineRepMap_directCombinedPointPart_lineRepMap D
   175	        (coordinateDirection (combinedPointVar D.m D.k j)) sample.point

   187	      simp only [directLdMap, directCombinedMeasuredQuestion, hindex,
   188	        directCombinedIndexSplit_combinedPointVar,
   189	        directCombinedSampleProjection,
   190	        directCombinedPointPart_directPrefixProjection_pointVar,

   192	      exact congrArg (fun x : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D =>
