     6	/-!
     7	# The low-degree game
     8	
     9	The low-degree component of the Pauli basis test has finite question and answer
    10	alphabets.  Its question maps act explicitly on the point, coordinate, and
    11	direction registers of the ambient coefficient space and have recursive
    12	conditionally linear representations of levels one, two, and three.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The source-facing nodes are `def:ld-game`, `def:ld-question-distribution`, and
    17	`def:ld-win-predicate` in
    18	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-194`; their paper origin is
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    20	The exact decomposition of a scalar seed into its coordinate index and its
    21	residue records the balance assertion for the map `chi` in the same source
    22	definition.
    23	-/
    24	
    25	open scoped BigOperators
    26	
    27	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    28	
    29	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    30	
    31	noncomputable section
    32	
    33	/-- Numerical parameters for the low-degree game.  The ambient coefficient
    34	space uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq`, rather than a
    35	model supplied by each parameter record.  This is the Lean carrier for
    36	`def:ld-game` in
    37	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-34`, with paper origin
    38	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    39	-/
    40	structure LdParams where
    41	  q : ℕ
    42	  m : ℕ
    43	  d : ℕ
    44	  k : ℕ
    45	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    46	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    47	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    48	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    49	  hdvd : m ∣ q
    50	
    51	/-- The positive dimension in `LdParams` supplies the finite coordinate type
    52	used by the uniform axis and prefix-index marginals. -/
    53	instance (L : LdParams) : Nonempty (Fin L.m) :=
    54	  ⟨⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one L.hm⟩⟩
    55	
    56	/-- The fixed scalar model of a low-degree parameter tuple.  It is a
    57	compatibility view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an
    58	independently quantified field representation.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-34`; paper origin
    59	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    60	-/
    61	noncomputable def LdParams.model (P : LdParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=
    62	  fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq
    63	
    64	/-- The scalar carrier selected by an `LdParams` record; this is the fixed
    65	field carrier in `def:ld-game`, selected globally by `LdParams.model`.
    66	Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-34`, paper origin
    67	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    68	-/
    69	abbrev ScalarQ (P : LdParams) := (P.model).K
    70	
    71	/-- The three low-degree question types of `def:ld-game`, blueprint
    72	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-34`, paper origin
    73	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    74	-/
    75	inductive LdType where
    76	  | point
    77	  | aline
    78	  | dline
    79	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    80	
    81	/-- The register index used by the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    82	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-34`; paper origin
    83	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    84	-/
    85	abbrev LdIndex (P : LdParams) := (Fin P.m ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m
    86	
    87	/-- The full ambient low-degree coefficient space (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    88	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-34`; paper origin
    89	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    90	-/
    91	abbrev LdSpace (P : LdParams) := LdIndex P → ScalarQ P
    92	
    93	/-- The point coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    94	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    95	-/
    96	def LdSpace.point {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    97	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))
    98	
    99	/-- The shared scalar coordinate of an ambient low-degree vector in
   100	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   101	-/
   102	def LdSpace.seed {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=
   103	  z (.inl (.inr ()) )
   104	
   105	/-- The direction coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   107	-/
   108	def LdSpace.direction {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   109	  fun i => z (.inr i)
   110	
   111	/-- The zero-based coordinate index corresponding to the paper's map `χ`:
   112	`chiIndex P s` represents `χ(s) - 1` in the fixed field representation.  This
   113	is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   114	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:36-61`, paper origin
   115	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   116	-/
   117	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
   118	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
   119	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   120	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   121	
   122	/-! ### Formalization-only coordinate-index fibers
   123	
   124	The following decomposition supplies the equal-fiber calculation used in the
   125	uniform coordinate-index law.
   126	-/
   127	
   128	/-- The common residue set in a fiber of `chiIndex` is nonempty.  This is part
   129	of the exact seed decomposition supporting the balance assertion in
   130	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `lem:chi-seed-fibers`, paper
   131	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:215-221`.
   132	-/
   133	theorem LdParams.seedFiberCard_pos (L : LdParams) : 0 < L.q / L.m := by
   134	  exact Nat.div_pos (Nat.le_of_dvd (by
   135	    obtain ⟨n, hn, hq⟩ := L.hq
   136	    rw [hq]
   137	    exact Nat.pow_pos (by decide)) L.hdvd) L.hm
   138	
   139	/-- Divisibility identifies the scalar cardinality with the product of the
   140	coordinate-index cardinality and the common fiber cardinality.  This supports
   141	`lem:chi-seed-fibers` in blueprint chapter 13. -/
   142	theorem LdParams.seedFiberProduct_eq (L : LdParams) :
   143	    L.q = L.m * (L.q / L.m) :=
   144	  (Nat.mul_div_cancel' L.hdvd).symm
   145	
   146	/-- Casting between equal finite cardinalities preserves the underlying
   147	natural-number representative. -/
   148	@[simp] private theorem equivCastFin_val {m n : ℕ} (h : m = n) (i : Fin m) :
   149	    (Equiv.cast (congrArg Fin h) i).val = i.val := by
   150	  subst n
   151	  rfl
   152	
   153	/-- A scalar seed is uniquely a coordinate index and a residue in its
   154	`chiIndex` fiber.  This is the exact decomposition underlying
   155	`lem:chi-seed-fibers` in blueprint chapter 13. -/
   156	noncomputable def seedFiberEquiv (L : LdParams) :
   157	    ScalarQ L ≃ Fin L.m × Fin (L.q / L.m) :=
   158	  (binaryRepresentation L.model).trans <|
   159	    (Equiv.cast <| congrArg Fin L.seedFiberProduct_eq).trans
   160	      finProdFinEquiv.symm
   161	
   162	/-- The coordinate component of the exact seed decomposition is `chiIndex`. -/
   163	@[simp] theorem seedFiberEquiv_fst (L : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ L) :
   164	    (seedFiberEquiv L s).1 = chiIndex L s := by
   165	  letI : NeZero L.m := ⟨Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one L.hm)⟩
   166	  have hquot : (binaryRepresentation L.model s).val / (L.q / L.m) < L.m := by
   167	    apply (Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul L.seedFiberCard_pos).mpr
   168	    rw [Nat.mul_div_cancel' L.hdvd]
   169	    exact (binaryRepresentation L.model s).isLt
   170	  simp only [seedFiberEquiv, Equiv.trans_apply]
   171	  apply Fin.ext
   172	  change
   173	    (Equiv.cast (congrArg Fin L.seedFiberProduct_eq)
   174	      (binaryRepresentation L.model s)).val / (L.q / L.m) =
   175	      (Fin.ofNat L.m ((binaryRepresentation L.model s).val / (L.q / L.m))).val
   176	  rw [equivCastFin_val]
   177	  · exact (Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hquot).symm
   178	  · exact L.seedFiberProduct_eq
   179	
   180	/-- Reconstruct the scalar seed belonging to a coordinate and its fiber
   181	residue. -/
   182	noncomputable def seedOfIndexResidue (L : LdParams)
   183	    (i : Fin L.m) (r : Fin (L.q / L.m)) : ScalarQ L :=
   184	  (seedFiberEquiv L).symm (i, r)
   185	
   186	/-- Decomposing a reconstructed seed recovers its coordinate and residue. -/
   187	@[simp] theorem seedFiberEquiv_seedOfIndexResidue (L : LdParams)
   188	    (i : Fin L.m) (r : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   189	    seedFiberEquiv L (seedOfIndexResidue L i r) = (i, r) :=
   190	  (seedFiberEquiv L).apply_symm_apply (i, r)
   191	
   192	/-- A reconstructed seed belongs to the prescribed `chiIndex` fiber. -/
   193	@[simp] theorem chiIndex_seedOfIndexResidue (L : LdParams)
   194	    (i : Fin L.m) (r : Fin (L.q / L.m)) :
   195	    chiIndex L (seedOfIndexResidue L i r) = i := by
   196	  rw [← seedFiberEquiv_fst]
   197	  simp
   198	
   199	/-- The projection used in the diagonal-line map zeroes coordinates before the
   200	chosen index and retains the suffix of the direction vector.  This is the
   201	prefix restriction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   202	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:36-61`, paper origin
   203	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   204	-/
   205	def prefixProjection {P : LdParams} (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   206	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   207	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   208	
   209	/-- Zeroing the coordinates preceding a fixed index is idempotent.  This is a
   210	formalization-only consequence of the prefix restriction in
   211	`def:ld-question-distribution`, recorded as `lem:prefix-projection-idempotent`
   212	in blueprint chapter 13. -/
   213	theorem prefixProjection_idempotent {P : LdParams} (i : Fin P.m)
   214	    (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   215	    prefixProjection i (prefixProjection i v) = prefixProjection i v := by
   216	  funext j
   217	  by_cases h : j.val < i.val
   218	  · simp only [prefixProjection, if_pos h]
   219	  · simp only [prefixProjection, if_neg h]
   220	
   221	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
   222	blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   223	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:36-61`, paper origin
   224	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   225	-/
   226	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   227	  fun i => match i with
   228	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   229	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   230	  | .inr _ => 0
   231	
   232	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   233	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   234	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:36-61`; paper
   235	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   236	-/
   237	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   238	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   239	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   240	  fun i => match i with
   241	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   242	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   243	  | .inr _ => 0
   244	
   245	/-- The diagonal-line CL map applies the canonical line representative map to
   246	the point block and stores the prefix-projected direction in the direction
   247	block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
   248	`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
   249	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:36-61`; paper origin
   250	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   251	-/
   252	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   253	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   254	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
   255	  let rep := lineRepMap direction
   256	  fun i => match i with
   257	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   258	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   259	  | .inr j => direction j

     3	/-!
     4	# Restricting a polynomial in the combined variables to a point
     5	
     6	The recovery step of the combining reduction reads a polynomial `p` in the
     7	`m + k` combined variables as a polynomial in the `k` combining variables whose
     8	coefficients are polynomials in the `m` point variables, and asks whether the
     9	restriction `p(u, ·)` obtained by substituting a point `u` for the point
    10	variables is a linear form in the combining variables.  This module introduces
    11	that restriction and records its elementary properties: it computes the
    12	combined polynomial of a tuple to the linear form of the tuple of values of the
    13	tuple at the point, and, when it is a linear form, its coefficients are forced
    14	to be the values at the point of the components recovered by the substitution
    15	of `lem:ld-combining-split`.  Consequently a restriction which is a linear form
    16	agrees with the restriction of the combined polynomial of those components,
    17	which is the first half of `lem:ld-combining-exact-linearity`.
    18	
    19	## Main statements
    20	
    21	* `eval_combinedRestrict` — evaluating `p(u, ·)` at `α` evaluates `p` at the
    22	  combined point with parts `u` and `α`.
    23	* `combinedRestrict_combinePolyTuple` — the restriction of a combined
    24	  polynomial is the linear form of the tuple of values of its components.
    25	* `combinedRestrict_eq_of_eq_combiningLinearForm` — a restriction which is a
    26	  linear form agrees with the restriction of the combined polynomial of the
    27	  components of `p`.
    28	
    29	## References
    30	
    31	* `references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex:1440-1470`
    32	* `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`
    33	* `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:575-600`
    34	-/

     4	/-!
     5	# The combined parameters of the simultaneity reduction
     6	
     7	The extension of the quantum soundness of the low individual degree test from
     8	simultaneity parameter `1` to a general simultaneity parameter `k` applies the
     9	case `k = 1` once, to a directly indexed low-degree game whose dimension is
    10	`m + k` and whose simultaneity parameter is `1`.  This module records that
    11	parameter map, the polynomial-tuple outcomes it carries, and the two maps
    12	relating outcomes of the two games: the combining map, which sends a tuple of
    13	`k` polynomials in `m` variables to the one-component tuple consisting of the
    14	combined polynomial in `m + k` variables, and its total left inverse, which
    15	returns the components of a combined polynomial and an arbitrary tuple
    16	otherwise.
    17	
    18	The field, the degree, and the admissibility of the field size are inherited
    19	unchanged; only the dimension and the simultaneity parameter change.  The
    20	degree is inherited because the combining map is linear in the fresh
    21	coordinates, so it raises no individual degree above `d` when `1 ≤ d`; this is
    22	where the individual-degree formulation differs from the total-degree
    23	formulation of the source, which passes from degree `d` to degree `d + 1`.
    24	
    25	## References
    26	
    27	* `references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex:1409-1503`
    28	* `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`
    29	* `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:240-250`
    30	* `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-simultaneous-sandwich.tex`
    31	-/
    32

    46	simultaneity parameter becomes `1`, while the field size, the degree, and the
    47	admissibility hypothesis are unchanged. -/

   126	    (r : Fin D.combined.k) :

   131	/-- A polynomial in the variables of the combined parameters is combined when it
   132	is the combined polynomial of a tuple.  This is the source's exact linearity in
   133	the combining variables, together with the individual-degree bound on the
   134	components.  Source
   135	`references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex:1462-1477`. -/
   136	def IsDirectCombined (D : DirectLdParams)
   137	    (p : PolyIndex D.combined.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d) : Prop :=

   141	    (g : DirectPolyTuple D) : IsDirectCombined D (directCombinedPolynomial D g) :=

   145	combined parameters: its components when it is combined, and the zero tuple
   146	otherwise.  The source leaves the value on non-combined outcomes arbitrary; the
   147	zero tuple is one admissible choice, and the estimates use only the value on

   149	`references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex:1477-1483`. -/
   150	def directTupleOfCombined (D : DirectLdParams)
   151	    (p : PolyIndex D.combined.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d) : DirectPolyTuple D := by
   152	  classical
   153	  exact if h : IsDirectCombined D p then h.choose else fun _ => 0
   154	
   155	/-- The components of a combined polynomial are the tuple it combines. -/
   156	@[simp] theorem directTupleOfCombined_directCombinedPolynomial (D : DirectLdParams)
   157	    (g : DirectPolyTuple D) :

   167	    (p : DirectPolyTuple D.combined) : DirectPolyTuple D :=

294	\subsection{The combining reduction to simultaneity parameter one}
   295	\label{sec:ld-combining-reduction}
   296	
   297	The extension from $k = 1$ to general $k$ cited in the proof of
   298	Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness} is recorded here in the form in which it is
   299	formalized.  The nodes below are formalization-support nodes: the source states
   300	none of them separately, and together they constitute its derivation of
   301	Theorem~4.43 from Theorem~4.40 in~\cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}.  The game in
   302	question is the directly indexed low-degree game of
   303	\cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}, which samples the coordinate index of
   304	a line directly instead of through a fiber of $\chi$; its point questions, line
   305	questions, answer formats and win predicate are those of
   306	Definition~\ref{def:ld-game}, and it is used here because the reduction applies
   307	the case $k = 1$ at dimension $m + k$, where the divisibility condition of
   308	Definition~\ref{def:ld-game} is not available.
   309	% A node of this subsection is marked as formalized only when the Lean
   310	% declarations it names are complete and carry no unproved placeholder.
   311	
   312	\begin{definition}[Combined parameters of the reduction]
   313		\label{def:ld-combining-parameters}
   314		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.DirectLdParams.combined}
   315		\leanok
   316		\uses{def:ld-game}
   317		For a parameter tuple $\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,m,d,k)$ as in
   318		Definition~\ref{def:ld-game}, the \emph{combined parameter tuple} is
   319		\[
   320			\mathsf{ldparams}^{\mathrm c} = (q,\; m+k,\; d,\; 1)\;:
   321		\]
   322		the dimension grows by the simultaneity parameter, the simultaneity
   323		parameter becomes $1$, and the field size, the degree and the admissibility
   324		of the field size are unchanged.  The degree is unchanged because the
   325		combining map of Definition~\ref{def:ld-combining-map} is linear in the
   326		fresh coordinates and therefore, in the individual-degree class of
   327		Definition~\ref{def:polyfunc}, raises no individual degree above $d$ as soon
   328		as $d \ge 1$.  The source works with total degree and passes from $d$ to
   329		$d+1$ at this step; that increment is an artifact of the total-degree
   330		formulation and does not occur here.
   331	\end{definition}
   332	
   333	\begin{definition}[The combining map on polynomial tuples]
   334		\label{def:ld-combining-map}
   335		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.combinePolyTuple, MIPStarRE.QPBT.combinePolyTuple_eval}
   336		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.combinePolyTuple_mem_polyFunc}
   337		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.directCombinedPolynomial}
   338		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.directCombinedPolynomial_eval}
   339		\leanok
   340		\uses{def:polyfunc, def:ld-meas, def:ld-combining-parameters}
   341		Coordinates of $\F_q^{m+k}$ are written $(u,\alpha)$, with $u \in \F_q^m$
   342		occupying the first $m$ coordinates and $\alpha \in \F_q^k$ the last $k$;
   343		the coordinates carrying $\alpha$ are called the \emph{combining
   344		coordinates}.  For a tuple $g = (g_0,\ldots,g_{k-1})$ of polynomials
   345		$g_r \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$, the \emph{combined polynomial} is
   346		\[
   347			\mathrm{comb}_g(u,\alpha) \;=\; \sum_{r=0}^{k-1} \alpha_r\, g_r(u)\;.
   348		\]
   349		It lies in $\polyfunc{m+k}{q}{d}$ whenever $d \ge 1$: a component $g_r$
   350		involves no combining coordinate, so multiplying it by $\alpha_r$ leaves its
   351		individual degrees in the first $m$ coordinates unchanged and produces
   352		individual degree $1$ in the coordinate carrying $\alpha_r$.
   353	
   354		The order of the two coordinate blocks is part of the construction.  The
   355		point coordinates precede the combining coordinates, so that zeroing a
   356		prefix of a direction of $\F_q^{m+k}$, as the diagonal-line branch of
   357		Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution} does, restricts on the first
   358		$m$ coordinates to zeroing the corresponding prefix of the point part of
   359		that direction; this is what makes the diagonal-line questions of the
   360		combined game project to diagonal-line questions of the original game in
   361		Definition~\ref{def:ld-combined-strategy}.  Definition~\ref{def:combine-map}
   362		is a variant of the same construction with two components in \emph{disjoint}
   363		blocks of point coordinates; the map above keeps one common block of point
   364		coordinates, as the reduction requires.
   365	\end{definition}
   366	
   367	\begin{lemma}[Recovery of the components of a combined polynomial]
   368		\label{lem:ld-combining-split}
   369		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.splitCombinedPoly}
   370		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.splitCombinedPoly_combinePolyTuple}
   371		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.combinePolyTuple_injective}
   372		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsDirectCombined, MIPStarRE.QPBT.directTupleOfCombined}
   373		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.directTupleOfCombined_directCombinedPolynomial}
   374		\leanok
   375		\uses{def:ld-combining-map}
   376		Let $\mathrm{split}_r$ denote the substitution of the $r$-th standard basis
   377		vector of $\F_q^k$ for the combining coordinates, a ring homomorphism
   378		$\F_q[u,\alpha] \to \F_q[u]$ fixing the point coordinates.  Then
   379		$\mathrm{split}_r(\mathrm{comb}_g) = g_r$ for every tuple $g$ and every
   380		$r$.  Consequently $g \mapsto \mathrm{comb}_g$ is injective, and the map
   381		sending $p \in \polyfunc{m+k}{q}{d}$ to the unique tuple $g$ with
   382		$\mathrm{comb}_g = p$ when $p$ is of that form, and to the zero tuple
   383		otherwise, is a well-defined total map $\mathrm{split}$ with
   384		$\mathrm{split}(\mathrm{comb}_g) = g$.
   385	\end{lemma}
   386	\begin{proof}
   387		\leanok
   388		\uses{def:ld-combining-map}
   389		Applying the homomorphism $\mathrm{split}_r$ to the sum defining
   390		$\mathrm{comb}_g$ sends the summand of index $s$ to $g_s$ when $s = r$ and to
   391		$0$ otherwise, since the combining coordinate carrying $\alpha_s$ is sent to
   392		$1$ for $s = r$ and to $0$ otherwise, while $g_s$, which involves no
   393		combining coordinate, is fixed; the sum is therefore $g_r$.
   394		Injectivity follows, and it makes the case distinction defining
   395		$\mathrm{split}$ unambiguous.  The value on polynomials that are not
   396		combined is immaterial: the source leaves it arbitrary, and the estimates
   397		below use only the value on combined polynomials.
   398	\end{proof}
   399	
   400	\begin{lemma}[Collision of two linear forms in the combining variables]
   401		\label{lem:ld-combining-collision}
   402		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.combiningLinearForm}
   403		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.combiningLinearForm_injective}
   404		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.combiningLinearForm_agreementProbability_le}
   405		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.directCombiningCollision_avg_le}
   406		\leanok
   407		\uses{lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree}
   408		Let $c, b \in \F_q^k$ with $c \neq b$.  Then
   409		\[
   410			\Pr_{\alpha \in \F_q^k}\Bigl[\; \sum_{r} c_r \alpha_r
   411				= \sum_{r} b_r \alpha_r \;\Bigr] \;\le\; \frac1q\;,
   412		\]
   413		the probability being over a uniformly random $\alpha$.
   414	\end{lemma}
   415	\begin{proof}
   416		\leanok
   417		\uses{lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree}
   418		The two sides are the evaluations at $\alpha$ of the linear forms
   419		$\sum_r c_r X_r$ and $\sum_r b_r X_r$ in $k$ variables.  The coefficient of
   420		$X_r$ in such a form is $c_r$, so the two forms are distinct polynomials,
   421		and each has total degree at most $1$.  Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree}
   422		bounds the probability that two distinct polynomials of total degree at most
   423		$1$ agree at a uniformly random point of $\F_q^k$ by $1/q$.
   424	\end{proof}

   426	\begin{definition}[The combined strategy]
   427		\label{def:ld-combined-strategy}
   428		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.directCombinedMeasuredQuestion}
   429		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.directCombinedMeasuredDirection}
   430		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.directCombinedRebaseParameter}
   431		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.directCombinedAnswerMap}
   432		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.directCombinedStrategy}
   433		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.directCombinedStrategy_isProjective}
   434		\leanok
   435		\uses{def:ld-game, def:ld-question-distribution, def:ld-win-predicate,
   436			def:projective-strategy-general, def:ld-combining-parameters,
   437			def:ld-combining-map}
   438		Let $\mathcal S = (\psi, A, B)$ be a projective strategy for the directly
   439		indexed low-degree game with parameters $\mathsf{ldparams}$.  The
   440		\emph{combined strategy} $\mathcal S^{\mathrm c}$ for the directly indexed
   441		low-degree game with parameters $\mathsf{ldparams}^{\mathrm c}$ has the same
   442		state and the same two Hilbert spaces, and answers each question of the
   443		combined game by measuring one question of $\mathcal S$ and post-processing
   444		its outcome.  Writing questions of the combined game in the coordinates of
   445		Definition~\ref{def:ld-combining-map}, the five cases are the following.
   446		\begin{enumerate}
   447			\item On the point question $(u,\alpha) \in \F_q^{m+k}$: measure the
   448			point question $u$, obtaining $b \in \F_q^k$, and answer
   449			$\sum_r \alpha_r b_r$.
   450			\item On the axis-parallel line question with stored index $i < m$ and
   451			canonical base $(u_0,\alpha_0)$: measure the axis-parallel line question
   452			with index $i$ and base $u_0$, obtaining univariate polynomials
   453			$f_0,\ldots,f_{k-1}$ of degree at most $d$, and answer
   454			$\sum_r (\alpha_0)_r f_r$, again of degree at most $d$.
   455			\item On the axis-parallel line question with stored index $m + r$ and
   456			canonical base $(u_0,\alpha_0)$, a line along which $u$ is constant and
   457			only the coordinate $\alpha_r$ varies: measure the point question $u_0$,
   458			obtaining $b$, and answer the degree-one polynomial
   459			$t \mapsto \sum_s (\alpha_0)_s b_s + t\, b_r$.
   460			\item On the diagonal line question with stored index $i < m$, canonical
   461			base $(u_0,\alpha_0)$ and direction $(v,w)$: measure the diagonal line
   462			question with index $i$, direction $v$ and the canonical base of the
   463			line $\ell(u_0, v)$, rebase the answer along the affine change of
   464			parameter relating the two presentations of that line, obtaining
   465			univariate polynomials $f_0,\ldots,f_{k-1}$ of degree at most $md$ in the
   466			parameter of the combined line, and answer
   467			$t \mapsto \sum_r \bigl((\alpha_0)_r + t\, w_r\bigr) f_r(t)$, of degree
   468			at most $md+1 \le (m+k)d$.
   469			\item On the diagonal line question with stored index $i \ge m$,
   470			canonical base $(u_0,\alpha_0)$ and direction $(0,w)$, a line along which
   471			$u$ is constant: measure the point question $u_0$, obtaining $b$, and
   472			answer $t \mapsto \sum_r (\alpha_0)_r b_r + t \sum_r w_r b_r$.
   473		\end{enumerate}
   474		Each case measures a single measurement of $\mathcal S$ and relabels its
   475		outcome, so $\mathcal S^{\mathrm c}$ is again a projective strategy, on the
   476		same state.  Cases~3 and~5 use that a line of $\F_q^{m+k}$ whose direction
   477		has vanishing point part is contained in a fiber of the projection to
   478		$\F_q^m$, so that the combined polynomial restricted to it is determined by
   479		the $k$ values of the tuple at the single point $u_0$; the rebasing in
   480		case~4 is the affine change of parameter of the previous paragraph, needed
   481		because the
   482		canonical base of a line of $\F_q^{m+k}$ need not project to the canonical
   483		base of its image line in $\F_q^m$.
   484	\end{definition}

+\begin{definition}[The combining map on polynomial tuples]
+	\label{def:ld-combining-map}
+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.combinePolyTuple, MIPStarRE.QPBT.combinePolyTuple_eval}

+	Coordinates of $\F_q^{m+k}$ are written $(u,\alpha)$, with $u \in \F_q^m$
+	occupying the first $m$ coordinates and $\alpha \in \F_q^k$ the last $k$;
+	the coordinates carrying $\alpha$ are called the \emph{combining
+	coordinates}.  For a tuple $g = (g_0,\ldots,g_{k-1})$ of polynomials
+	$g_r \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$, the \emph{combined polynomial} is
+	\[
+		\mathrm{comb}_g(u,\alpha) \;=\; \sum_{r=0}^{k-1} \alpha_r\, g_r(u)\;.
+	\]
+	It lies in $\polyfunc{m+k}{q}{d}$ whenever $d \ge 1$: a component $g_r$
+	involves no combining coordinate, so multiplying it by $\alpha_r$ leaves its

+	individual degree $1$ in the coordinate carrying $\alpha_r$.

 \section{The Magic Square game}
 % Paper label sec:ms kept for cross-reference fidelity.
 \label{sec:ms}
 
 We recall the Magic Square game of Mermin and Peres. It is a simple self-test for two EPR pairs, and it allows one to test that a pair of binary observables \emph{anticommutes}; both properties are used in the Pauli basis test. Here it is presented as a binary constraint satisfaction game. Throughout this section and the next, $\sigma^X$ and $\sigma^Z$ denote the single-qubit Pauli observables, with associated two-outcome projective measurements $\{\sigma^W_b\}_{b \in \F_2}$ for $W \in \{X,Z\}$.
 
 \begin{definition}[The Magic Square game]\label{def:ms-game}
 	\uses{def:game, def:graph-distribution}
 	The Magic Square game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{MS}}$ is the following two-player game. There are $9$ variables $x_1,\ldots,x_9$ taking values in $\F_2$, arranged in a $3 \times 3$ grid: the cell in row $r$ and column $c$ contains the variable $x_{3(r-1)+c}$. There are $6$ linear equations over these variables: for each of the three rows and each of the first two columns, the sum of the three variables in it equals $0$; for the third column, the sum of the three variables in it equals $1$.
 
 	The question types are
 	\begin{align*}
 		\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}} &= \{\mathsf{Constraint}_i : i = 1,2,\ldots,6\}\;,\\
 		\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mv}} &= \{\mathsf{Variable}_j : j = 1,2,\ldots,9\}\;,\\
 		\mathcal T^{\mathrm{ms}} &= \mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}} \cup \mathcal T^{\mathrm{mv}}\;,
 	\end{align*}
 	where $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ for $i \in \{1,2,3\}$ denotes the constraint of row $i$ (with variables $x_{3(i-1)+1}, x_{3(i-1)+2}, x_{3(i-1)+3}$), $\mathsf{Constraint}_4$ and $\mathsf{Constraint}_5$ denote the constraints of the first two columns, and $\mathsf{Constraint}_6$ denotes the constraint of the third column (with variables $x_{i-3}, x_{i}, x_{i+3}$ for $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$, $i \in \{4,5,6\}$).
 
 	The question distribution is as follows: the verifier samples $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ uniformly from $\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}}$, then samples $\mathsf{Variable}_j$ uniformly among the three variables appearing in the row or column of $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$; one player, chosen uniformly at random, receives $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ and the other receives $\mathsf{Variable}_j$. Equivalently, the verifier samples a uniformly random edge of the bipartite \emph{type graph} $G^{\mathrm{ms}}$ on vertex sets $\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}}$ and $\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mv}}$, whose edges are $\mathsf{Constraint}_i \,\text{---}\, \mathsf{Variable}_{3(i-1)+j}$ for $i,j \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $\mathsf{Constraint}_i \,\text{---}\, \mathsf{Variable}_{(i-3)+3(j-1)}$ for $i \in \{4,5,6\}$, $j \in \{1,2,3\}$ ($18$ edges in total, and no self-loops), and sends one endpoint to a uniformly random player and the other endpoint to the other player.
 
 	The $\mathsf{Constraint}$ player answers with three bits $(\beta_{v_1}, \beta_{v_2}, \beta_{v_3}) \in \F_2^3$, where $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ are the indices of the three variables of $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$; the $\mathsf{Variable}$ player answers with a single bit $\gamma \in \F_2$. The players win if and only if the $\mathsf{Constraint}$ player's answer satisfies the equation associated with $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ and $\gamma = \beta_j$.
 \end{definition}
 
 The following theorem records the self-testing (rigidity) properties of the Magic Square game. It is used in the soundness analysis of the Pauli basis test to enforce anticommutation relations between certain pairs of observables.
 With zero-based labels, the paper's variables $1$ and $5$ have labels $0$ and
 $4$, respectively.

   769	\section{The Magic Square game}
   770	% Paper label sec:ms kept for cross-reference fidelity.
   771	\label{sec:ms}
   772	
   773	We recall the Magic Square game of Mermin and Peres. It is a simple self-test for two EPR pairs, and it allows one to test that a pair of binary observables \emph{anticommutes}; both properties are used in the Pauli basis test. Here it is presented as a binary constraint satisfaction game. Throughout this section and the next, $\sigma^X$ and $\sigma^Z$ denote the single-qubit Pauli observables, with associated two-outcome projective measurements $\{\sigma^W_b\}_{b \in \F_2}$ for $W \in \{X,Z\}$.
   774	
   775	\begin{definition}[The Magic Square game]\label{def:ms-game}
   776		\uses{def:game, def:graph-distribution}
   777		The Magic Square game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{MS}}$ is the following two-player game. There are $9$ variables $x_1,\ldots,x_9$ taking values in $\F_2$, arranged in a $3 \times 3$ grid: the cell in row $r$ and column $c$ contains the variable $x_{3(r-1)+c}$. There are $6$ linear equations over these variables: for each of the three rows and each of the first two columns, the sum of the three variables in it equals $0$; for the third column, the sum of the three variables in it equals $1$.
   778	
   779		The question types are
   780		\begin{align*}
   781			\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}} &= \{\mathsf{Constraint}_i : i = 1,2,\ldots,6\}\;,\\
   782			\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mv}} &= \{\mathsf{Variable}_j : j = 1,2,\ldots,9\}\;,\\
   783			\mathcal T^{\mathrm{ms}} &= \mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}} \cup \mathcal T^{\mathrm{mv}}\;,
   784		\end{align*}
   785		where $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ for $i \in \{1,2,3\}$ denotes the constraint of row $i$ (with variables $x_{3(i-1)+1}, x_{3(i-1)+2}, x_{3(i-1)+3}$), $\mathsf{Constraint}_4$ and $\mathsf{Constraint}_5$ denote the constraints of the first two columns, and $\mathsf{Constraint}_6$ denotes the constraint of the third column (with variables $x_{i-3}, x_{i}, x_{i+3}$ for $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$, $i \in \{4,5,6\}$).

     7	/-!
     8	# Simultaneous polynomial measurements for the direct low-degree game
     9	
    10	This module applies the quantum soundness theorem of the low individual
    11	degree test to each coordinate of a projective strategy for the directly
    12	indexed low-degree game, transports the Schwartz--Zippel collision estimate
    13	to the direct polynomial representatives, and, for simultaneity parameter
    14	`1`, obtains the polynomial-tuple conclusion of `lem:ld-soundness` from the
    15	coordinate conclusions.
    16	
    17	## The simultaneity obstruction
    18	
    19	For simultaneity parameter `k ≥ 2` the coordinate conclusions alone do not
    20	determine simultaneous polynomial measurements, so no palindromic combination
    21	of the coordinate measurements can be consistent with a joint point
    22	measurement in general.  Let `q = 2^s`, let the degree be `1`, and let Bob
    23	measure the univariate polynomials `g = g₀ + g₁ x` once in the standard basis
    24	`|g⟩` and once in the Fourier basis attached to the symmetric pairing
    25	`⟨h, g⟩ = h₀ g₁ + h₁ g₀`.  In characteristic two every evaluation functional
    26	`h ↦ h(u)` is represented by an isotropic vector of this pairing, so at every
    27	point `u` the value-level coarse-grainings `Q^{1,u}_{[a]}` (Fourier basis) and
    28	`Q^{2,u}_{[b]}` (standard basis) commute, and on the maximally entangled state
    29	Alice may answer point questions with the joint projective measurement
    30	`P^u_{a,b} = (Q^{1,u}_{[a]} Q^{2,u}_{[b]})ᵀ`.  All coordinate consistencies of
    31	`lem:ld-soundness` then hold with defect `0` and distinct polynomials collide
    32	at a uniform point with probability `1 / q`, but the sandwiched POVM has
    33	`∑_{g₂(u) = b} |g₂⟩⟨g₂| Q^{1,u}_{[a]} |g₂⟩⟨g₂| = q⁻¹ Q^{2,u}_{[b]}`, whose
    34	consistency defect against `P^u` is `1 - 1/q`; more strongly, every
    35	polynomial-pair POVM on Bob's side has defect at least `1 - 2/q` against
    36	`P^u`.  No bound of the form `C k √(δ + m d / q)` holds for a universal `C`.
    37	The source obtains the general case not coordinatewise but by the combining
    38	reduction of Theorem 4.43 in the NEEXP paper, which applies the `k = 1`
    39	theorem once, in dimension `m + k`, to a combined strategy; that reduction is
    40	not formalized here.  The two-measurement pasting estimate (Fact 4.35 there)
    41	does not apply either, since it evaluates the two coordinates at
    42	independently sampled points while the low-degree game evaluates all
    43	coordinates at one point.  The counterexample and the resulting formal
    44	status are recorded in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-simultaneous-sandwich.tex`.
    45	
    46	## References
    47	
    48	* `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`
    49	* `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:465-501`
    50	* `references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex:912-1060` and `:1409-1503`
    51	* `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:180-202`
    52	* `lem:ld-soundness` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex`
    53	* `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`
    54	* `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-simultaneous-sandwich.tex`
    55	-/

    67	/-! ## Direct polynomial collision estimate -/
    68	
    69	/-- Two distinct direct polynomial representatives agree at a uniformly
    70	sampled direct point with probability at most `m d / q`.
    71	
    72	This is the Schwartz--Zippel estimate `polynomialAgreement_avg_le_mdq` of the
    73	low individual degree test, read through the polynomial and point
    74	identifications of the direct low-degree game; it is the collision
    75	hypothesis of `lem:ld-sandwich` (blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:454-480`,
    76	paper `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:465-501`). -/
    77	theorem directPolynomialAgreement_avg_le_mdq (D : DirectLdParams)
    78	    (g g' : PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d) (hneq : g ≠ g') :
    79	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
    80	        (fun u => if MvPolynomial.eval u g.1 = MvPolynomial.eval u g'.1 then
    81	          (1 : Error) else 0) ≤
    82	      (D.m * D.d : Error) / D.q := by
    83	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    84	  let gLdt := directPolyEquivPolynomial D g
    85	  let g'Ldt := directPolyEquivPolynomial D g'
    86	  have hneqLdt : gLdt ≠ g'Ldt := by
    87	    intro heq
    88	    exact hneq ((directPolyEquivPolynomial D).injective heq)
    89	  calc
    90	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
    91	        (fun u => if MvPolynomial.eval u g.1 = MvPolynomial.eval u g'.1 then
    92	          (1 : Error) else 0) =
    93	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
    94	        (fun u => if gLdt (directPointEquiv D u) =
    95	          g'Ldt (directPointEquiv D u) then (1 : Error) else 0) := by
    96	            apply avgOver_congr
    97	            intro u
    98	            simp only [gLdt, g'Ldt, directPolyEquivPolynomial_apply]
    99	            exact if_congr
   100	              ((directScalarEquiv D).injective.eq_iff.symm) rfl rfl
   101	    _ = avgOver (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
   102	        (fun u : Point D.toLDTParameters =>
   103	          if gLdt u = g'Ldt u then (1 : Error) else 0) := by
   104	      simpa using
   105	        (avgOver_uniform_equiv (directPointEquiv D)
   106	          (fun u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D =>
   107	            if gLdt (directPointEquiv D u) =
   108	              g'Ldt (directPointEquiv D u) then (1 : Error) else 0))
   109	    _ ≤ (D.m * D.d : Error) / D.q :=
   110	      polynomialAgreement_avg_le_mdq D.toLDTParameters gLdt g'Ldt hneqLdt

   112	/-! ## Coordinatewise low individual degree soundness -/
   113	
   114	/-- Quantum soundness of the low individual degree test (`thm:main-formal`,
   115	paper `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:180-202`) applied to one
   116	coordinate of a projective strategy for the direct low-degree game.
   117	
   118	The coordinate strategy passes the test with failure probability at most
   119	`3 ε`, and the theorem is instantiated at the auxiliary sampling parameter
   120	`directLdAuxParameter D`; both numerical side conditions of the theorem follow
   121	from the positivity of the dimension and of the degree.  Blueprint
   122	`lem:ld-soundness`, paper
   123	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`. -/

   125	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
   126	    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k) (ε : Error)
   127	    (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) :
   128	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   129	    ∃ GA : ProjMeas (Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιA,
   130	      ∃ GB : ProjMeas (Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) S.ιB,
   131	        ConsRel (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).state
   132	            (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
   133	            (IdxProjMeas.toIdxSubMeas
   134	              (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementA)

   138	          ConsRel (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).state
   139	            (uniformDistribution (Point D.toLDTParameters))
   140	            (polynomialEvaluationFamily D.toLDTParameters GA.toSubMeas)
   141	            (IdxProjMeas.toIdxSubMeas
   142	              (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementB)
   143	            (Test.mainFormalError D.toLDTParameters
   144	              (directLdAuxParameter D) (3 * ε)) ∧
   145	          ConsRel (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).state
   146	            (uniformDistribution Unit)
   147	            (constSubMeasFamily GA.toSubMeas)
   148	            (constSubMeasFamily GB.toSubMeas)
   149	            (Test.mainFormalError D.toLDTParameters
   150	              (directLdAuxParameter D) (3 * ε)) := by
   151	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   152	  exact Test.mainFormal D.toLDTParameters
   153	    (directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r) (3 * ε)

     3	/-!
     4	# The joint recovery estimate in the point and combining variables
     5	
     6	`lem:ld-combining-recovery` compares the tuple of values at a point of the
     7	components recovered from an outcome of the combined game with the tuple of
     8	answers of the point measurement of the original game.  The comparison rests on
     9	a joint estimate over the sampled point `u` and the sampled combining vector
    10	`α`: for every outcome `p` of the combined game and every tuple `b` of scalars,
    11	the event that the recovered tuple of values at `u` differs from `b` while the
    12	value of `p` at the combined point agrees with the combination `∑_r α_r b_r`
    13	has probability at most `(m + k) d / q`.
    14	
    15	Two cases occur.  If `p` is the combined polynomial of a tuple `g`, its value at
    16	the combined point is the combination `∑_r α_r g_r(u)`, and two combinations
    17	with distinct coefficient tuples agree at a uniformly sampled `α` with
    18	probability at most `1 / q`.  If `p` is not combined, then by
    19	`lem:ld-combining-exact-linearity` its restriction `p(u, ·)` fails to be a
    20	linear form except with probability `m d / q` over `u`, and off that event the
    21	restriction and the linear form of `b` are distinct polynomials of total degree
    22	at most `k d`, so they agree at a uniformly sampled `α` with probability at
    23	most `k d / q`.
    24	
    25	The estimate is recorded in two stages, because the consistency calculus
    26	averages it against Born weights which depend on the sampled point but not on
    27	the sampled combining vector: a bound at a fixed point which does not depend on
    28	the tuple `b`, and the average of that bound over the point.
    29	
    30	## Main statements
    31	
    32	* `directCombinedRecoveryLocalBound` — the bound at a fixed point.
    33	* `directCombinedRecoveryEvent_avg_le` — the estimate at a fixed point.
    34	* `directCombinedRecoveryLocalBound_avg_le` — the average of the bound at a
    35	  fixed point over a uniformly sampled point.
    36	* `directCombinedRecoveryBadEvent_avg_le` — the joint estimate of
    37	  `lem:ld-combining-recovery`.
    38	
    39	## References
    40	
    41	* `references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex:1440-1503`
    42	* `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`
    43	* `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:617-680`
    44	-/

    66	  Finset.sum_congr rfl fun _ _ => mul_comm _ _

    72	      ((n : ℕ) : Error) / D.q := by

    19	\section{At a glance}
    20	
    21	\begin{itemize}
    22	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Easy for simultaneity parameter $k = 1$, hard
    23	  for general $k$.  The coordinatewise route planned for the formalization
    24	  applies the single-polynomial soundness theorem to each coordinate and
    25	  combines the resulting measurements by the sandwich of the source's
    26	  Lemma~\texttt{lem:ld-sandwich}; an explicit pair of measurements refutes
    27	  every bound this route could produce.  The source instead cites a
    28	  reduction of the $k$-tuple test to the single-polynomial test in $m + k$
    29	  variables at degree $d + 1$; that reduction is now carried out in the
    30	  formalization, in the individual-degree formulation, where the degree stays
    31	  $d$.
    32	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} The case $k = 1$ is closed by relabeling
    33	  the coordinate conclusions (about 150 lines).  The combining reduction is
    34	  complete: a combined strategy for the directly indexed game in dimension
    35	  $m + k$ at degree $d$, a transfer of the success probability with the
    36	  constant $10$, and the extraction of $k$ polynomials from one polynomial by
    37	  linearity, in about a dozen new definitions and 6000 lines of formal proof.
    38	  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} The counterexample is finite Fourier
    39	  analysis over $\F_{2^s}$ and a Gram-matrix estimate.  The reduction itself
    40	  is almost entirely project-local (game constructions and the consistency
    41	  calculus), with the Schwartz--Zippel lemma and multivariate polynomial
    42	  algebra taken from Mathlib.
    43	  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} Additive characters of $\F_q^2$
    44	  and isotropic vectors of a symmetric pairing in characteristic two; the
    45	  eigenvalue bound for nearly orthogonal unit vectors; the reduction proving
    46	  Theorem~4.43 from Theorem~4.40 in \cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}.  Tracked in
    47	  \ghissue{134}.
    48	\end{itemize}
    49	
    50	\section{Key theorem forms}
    51	
    52	The source theorem (\texttt{lem:ld-soundness}) states that for every
    53	projective strategy passing the low individual degree game with parameters
    54	$(q,m,d,k)$ with probability at least $1 - \eps$ there are polynomial-tuple
    55	measurements $G^{\mathrm A}$ and $G^{\mathrm B}$, with outcomes
    56	$(g_1,\dots,g_k)$ of individual degree at most $d$, such that on average over
    57	a uniform point $u \in \F_q^m$
    58	\[
    59	  A^{\mathsf{Point},u}_{a} \ot I \simeq_{\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}}
    60	    I \ot G^{\mathrm B}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = a]},
    61	  \qquad
    62	  G^{\mathrm A}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = a]} \ot I \simeq_{\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}}
    63	    I \ot B^{\mathsf{Point},u}_{a},
    64	  \qquad
    65	  G^{\mathrm A}_{g} \ot I \simeq_{\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}} I \ot G^{\mathrm B}_{g},
    66	  \tag{source form}
    67	\]
    68	where $a = (a_1,\dots,a_k)$ and
    69	$\mathrm{eval}_u(g_1,\dots,g_k) = (g_1(u),\dots,g_k(u))$.
    70	
    71	The formalization planned to derive this from the case $k = 1$ as follows.
    72	Reading the $i$-th coordinate of every answer yields $k$ strategies for the
    73	game with $k = 1$, each passing with probability at least $1 - 3\eps$; the
    74	single-polynomial theorem gives projective measurements $G^{w,i}$ with
    75	\[
    76	  A^{\mathsf{Point},u}_{[a_i]} \ot I \simeq_{\delta}
    77	    I \ot G^{\mathrm B,i}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = a_i]},
    78	  \qquad
    79	  G^{\mathrm A,i}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = a_i]} \ot I \simeq_{\delta}
    80	    I \ot B^{\mathsf{Point},u}_{[a_i]},
    81	  \qquad
    82	  G^{\mathrm A,i}_{g} \ot I \simeq_{\delta} I \ot G^{\mathrm B,i}_{g},
    83	  \tag{coordinate form}
    84	\]
    85	where $A^{\mathsf{Point},u}_{[a_i]}$ is the $i$-th marginal of the joint
    86	point measurement; and the planned combination was the sandwich
    87	\[
    88	  C^{w}_{g_1,\dots,g_k}
    89	    = G^{w,k}_{g_k} \cdots G^{w,2}_{g_2}\, G^{w,1}_{g_1}\,
    90	      G^{w,2}_{g_2} \cdots G^{w,k}_{g_k},
    91	  \qquad
    92	  A^{\mathsf{Point},u}_{a} \ot I \simeq_{C k (\delta + md/q)^{1/2}}
    93	    I \ot C^{\mathrm B}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot) = a]},
    94	  \tag{planned form}
    95	\]
    96	with a universal constant $C$, and likewise on the other side and for the
    97	global relation.  We show that no statement of the planned form holds: the
    98	coordinate form, even with $\delta = 0$ and even with both point
    99	measurements and all $2k$ polynomial measurements available, does not
   100	determine any polynomial-tuple measurement consistent with the joint point
   101	measurement.
   102	
   103	The formalization proves the source form for every $k$, for the directly
   104	indexed low-degree game of \cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility} and by the
   105	source reduction rather than by the refuted route.  From a projective strategy for the
   106	directly indexed low-degree game with parameters $(q,m,d,k)$ succeeding with
   107	probability at least $1 - \eps$ it produces polynomial-tuple measurements
   108	satisfying the three relations of the source form with the error of the low
   109	individual degree theorem at the combined parameters $(q, m+k, d, 1)$, at the
   110	auxiliary parameter $2560000\,(m+k)^{3}d$ and pass bound $30\eps$, increased by
   111	the recovery loss $(m+k)d/q$ on the two point/polynomial relations;%
   112	\footnote{The declaration is
   113	\leanid{exists\_directSimultaneousPolynomialMeasurements\_combinedError} in
   114	\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/Combining/SimultaneousGeneral.lean}.}
   115	and, absorbing that error, the same three relations with the error function
   116	$\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}(\eps,q,m,d,k)$ of the source statement at the universal
   117	constants $a = 10^{23}$ and $b = 1/80000$.%
   118	\footnote{The declaration is \leanid{exists\_direct\_ld\_soundness} in
   119	\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Soundness.lean}.  The case
   120	$k = 1$, the only one instantiated by the Pauli basis test analysis, remains
   121	available separately as
   122	\leanid{exists\_directSimultaneousPolynomialMeasurements\_of\_k\_eq\_one}
   123	in \doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/Simultaneous.lean};
   124	the instantiation with $k = 1$ at dimension $2m+2$ is in the proof of
   125	\texttt{lem:qld-4-7}, \path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex}.}
   126	
   127	The route is the source's: the combined strategy answers each question of the
   128	game at the combined parameters by measuring one question of the original
   129	strategy and relabeling its outcome, its success probability is at least
   130	$1 - 10\eps$, the case $k = 1$ is applied once to it, and the $k$ polynomials
   131	are recovered from the single outcome polynomial by exact linearity in the
   132	fresh coordinates.  Two quantitative points differ from the account of the
   133	source assertion below, and both are forced by the individual-degree
   134	formulation of the game.  The degree does not rise to $d + 1$: the combined
   135	polynomial $(u,\alpha) \mapsto \sum_r \alpha_r g_r(u)$ has individual degree
   136	at most $d$ in each of the $m + k$ variables, so the theorem is applied at
   137	degree $d$ and its error function is evaluated there.  Correspondingly the
   138	recovery cost is not $(d+1)/q$ taken twice but $(m+k)d/q$: the exact-linearity
   139	test on the point space contributes $md/q$, and the collision of two distinct
   140	tuples at the sampled point contributes $kd/q$.  A reader comparing the two
   141	accounts should read the displayed recovery term of the source assertion as
   142	$(m+k)d/q$ throughout.
   143	
   144	\section{The source assertion}
   145	
   146	The proof of \texttt{lem:ld-soundness} in
   147	\cite[lines~413--458]{Ji2020MIPStar} treats $k = 1$ by an identification
   148	with the tensor-code test of \cite{Ji2021Quantum} (the identification is
   149	examined in \path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex}) and
   150	then extends to general $k$ by reference to the derivation of Theorem~4.43
   151	from Theorem~4.40 in \cite[lines~1409--1503]{Natarajan2018NEEXP}.  That
   152	derivation is not coordinatewise.  It builds two combined provers who play
   153	the single-polynomial test in $m + k$ variables at degree $d + 1$: on a
   154	point $(\alpha, u)$ the combined prover asks the original prover for the $k$
   155	values $(b_1,\dots,b_k)$ at $u$ and returns $\sum_i \alpha_i b_i$, and on a
   156	line it returns the corresponding combination of the $k$ answer polynomials.
   157	The degree rises by one because the combination
   158	$(\alpha, u) \mapsto \sum_i \alpha_i g_i(u)$ is linear in $\alpha$ and of
   159	degree $d$ in $u$, so its restriction to a queried subspace has degree
   160	$d + 1$; the single-polynomial theorem is therefore applied at degree $d + 1$
   161	and its error function is evaluated there.  That theorem then yields one
   162	measurement with outcomes $g(\alpha,u)$, and the $k$ polynomials are
   163	recovered from $g$ because $g$ is exactly linear in $\alpha$ with high
   164	probability, by the Schwartz--Zippel lemma; applied at degree $d + 1$, that
   165	lemma contributes the term $(d+1)/q$ twice in the recovery.  The
   166	simultaneity of the $k$ outputs is thus inherited from the joint answers of
   167	the original provers through a single application of the $k = 1$ theorem.
   168	
   169	\section{The counterexample}
   170	
   171	Let $q = 2^s$, let $d = 1$, and let $\Gamma$ be the set of univariate
   172	polynomials $g = g_0 + g_1 x$ over $\F_q$, so $|\Gamma| = N = q^2$.  Two
   173	distinct elements of $\Gamma$ agree at a uniformly random point of $\F_q$
   174	with probability at most $1/q$.  Bob's Hilbert space is $\C^{\Gamma}$ with
   175	standard basis $\{\ket{g}\}$; Alice's is a second copy, and the state is
   250	$p$ a probability distribution and $\rho$ density matrices.  Its
   251	consistency with the joint point measurement is
   252	\[
   253	  \E_{u} \sum_{g_1,g_2} p_{g_1,g_2}\,
   254	    \bra{\xi^u_{g_1(u),g_2(u)}}\, \rho_{g_1,g_2}\, \ket{\xi^u_{g_1(u),g_2(u)}}
   255	  \le \max_{g_1,g_2}\,
   256	    \lambda_{\max}\Bigl(\E_{u}\, \ket{\xi^u_{g_1(u),g_2(u)}}\!\bra{\xi^u_{g_1(u),g_2(u)}}\Bigr).
   257	\]
   258	For $u \ne u'$ the supports $\{g : g(u) = g_2(u)\}$ and
   259	$\{g : g(u') = g_2(u')\}$ meet exactly in $\{g_2\}$, so the $q$ unit vectors
   260	$\xi^u_{g_1(u),g_2(u)}$ have pairwise inner products of modulus $1/q$, and
   261	the largest eigenvalue of their Gram matrix is at most $1 + (q-1)/q < 2$.
   262	Hence the consistency of every polynomial-pair POVM with the joint point
   263	measurement is below $2/q$, on either side.  Consequently no argument that
   264	uses only the coordinate form --- with any error, any number of applications
   265	of the pasting or sandwich facts, and either player as reference --- can
   266	produce the source form for $k \ge 2$.
   267	
   268	Two remarks.  First, the pair $(\ket{\psi}, \Pi, G^1, G^2)$ is not a
   269	strategy for the low-degree game passing with high probability: by the same
   270	Gram-matrix bound no line measurement with polynomial-pair outcomes is
   271	consistent with the point measurements, so the source theorem is not
   272	contradicted; what fails is the coordinatewise route.  Second, the pasting
   273	fact (Fact~4.35 of \cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}, imported as
   274	\texttt{lem:pasting}) does not repair the route: it requires the two
   275	coordinates to be evaluated at points $y_1, y_2$ whose conditional
   276	distribution supports a collision bound $\eta < 1$, whereas the low-degree
   277	game evaluates all coordinates at the same point, for which the conditional
   278	collision probability of any two polynomials agreeing there is $1$.
   279	
   280	\section{Comparison with the blueprint and formalization}
   281	
   282	The blueprint proof of \texttt{lem:ld-soundness} records the source route,
   283	including the extension from $k = 1$ to general $k$ by the derivation of
   284	Theorem~4.43 in \cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}, and lists the game
   285	correspondence and the parameter bound as open obligations.  The present
   286	note added a third: the extension is the combining reduction and must be
   287	formalized as such.  That third obligation is now met.  The blueprint records
   288	the reduction in \texttt{prop:ld-simultaneous-general-k} and the nodes
   289	preceding it, and the directly indexed game and its transport prove the source
   290	form from the low individual degree theorem for every $k$.  The game
   291	correspondence and the parameter bound of the import remain as they were.  The
   292	combination of the coordinate measurements by the sandwich is defined and is a
   293	POVM, but it carries no consistency estimate, and by the computation above it
   294	cannot; nothing depends on it.
   295	
   296	\section{Conclusion}
   297	
   298	The source statement is not contradicted.  Its proof for general $k$ is a
   299	reduction to a single application of the $k = 1$ theorem in $m + k$
   300	variables, and the formalization follows that reduction; a
   301	coordinatewise application of the $k = 1$ theorem followed by any
   302	combination of the coordinate measurements provably cannot yield the
   303	theorem.  The application in the analysis of the Pauli basis test uses
   304	$k = 1$ only, for which the source form is proved from the low individual
   305	degree theorem directly; for general $k$ it is proved by the reduction, for
   306	the directly indexed game.

    15	branch of the original game; on each of the two events the relabelling of
    16	`def:ld-combined-strategy` carries acceptance to acceptance, which is
    17	`directCombinedWinTransport_all`.  Each branch of the combined game is therefore
    18	rejected with probability at most the sum of two branch rejection probabilities
    19	of the original game, and summing over the nine branches multiplies the
    20	rejection probability by at most ten.

    39	/-- The rejected mass of the original strategy at the pair of questions
    40	measured by the combined strategy, as a function of the coordinate index and of
    41	the two point parts of the sample of the combined game.  By
    42	`lem:ld-combined-question-law` those three data determine the measured pair. -/
    43	def directCombinedMeasuredRejectedMass (D : DirectLdParams)
    44	    (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) (types : LdType × LdType)
    45	    (i : Fin D.combined.m)
    46	    (pd : (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)) : ℝ :=
    47	  match directCombinedIndexSplit D i with
    48	  | .inl j =>
    49	      directRejectedMass D S
    50	        (types.1, directLdMap D types.1 ⟨pd.1, j, pd.2⟩)
    51	        (types.2, directLdMap D types.2 ⟨pd.1, j, pd.2⟩)
    52	  | .inr _ =>
    53	      directRejectedMass D S (directLdPointQuestionOf D pd.1)

    56	/-- Branch-wise rejected-mass comparison at a fixed sample of the combined
    57	game: the acceptance transport of `directCombinedWinTransport_all` bounds the

    59	strategy at the measured questions, which `lem:ld-combined-question-law`
    60	identifies. -/
    61	theorem directRejectedMass_directCombinedStrategy_le_measured (D : DirectLdParams)
    62	    (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) (types : LdType × LdType)
    63	    (sample : DirectLdSpace D.combined) :
    64	    directRejectedMass D.combined (directCombinedStrategy D S)
    65	        (types.1, directLdMap D.combined types.1 sample)
    66	        (types.2, directLdMap D.combined types.2 sample) ≤
    67	      directCombinedMeasuredRejectedMass D S types sample.index
    68	        (directCombinedPointPart D sample.point,
    69	          directCombinedPointPart D sample.direction) := by
    70	  refine le_trans (directRejectedMass_directCombinedStrategy_le D S _ _
    71	    (directCombinedWinTransport_all D types.1 types.2 sample)) (le_of_eq ?_)
    72	  rcases hsplit : directCombinedIndexSplit D sample.index with j | r
    73	  · have hindex : sample.index = combinedPointVar D.m D.k j :=
    74	      eq_combinedPointVar_of_indexSplit D hsplit
    75	    rw [directCombined_measuredQuestion_of_pointVar D types.1 j sample hindex,
    76	      directCombined_measuredQuestion_of_pointVar D types.2 j sample hindex]
    77	    simp only [directCombinedMeasuredRejectedMass, hsplit,
    78	      directCombinedSampleProjection]

    80	      eq_combinedCoefficientVar_of_indexSplit D hsplit

    82	      directCombined_measuredQuestion_of_coefficientVar D types.2 r sample hindex]

   133	/-- Branch-wise half of `lem:ld-combined-value`: every branch of the combined
   134	game is rejected with probability at most the sum of the branch of the original
   135	game at the same ordered type pair and its point-versus-point branch. -/
   136	theorem directLdBranchRejectionProbability_directCombinedStrategy_le
   137	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
   138	    (types : LdType × LdType) :
   139	    directLdBranchRejectionProbability D.combined (directCombinedStrategy D S)
   140	        types ≤
   141	      directLdBranchRejectionProbability D S types +
   142	        directLdBranchRejectionProbability D S (.point, .point) := by
   143	  classical
   144	  have hstep : directLdBranchRejectionProbability D.combined
   145	      (directCombinedStrategy D S) types ≤
   146	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.combined.m ×
   147	        ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))))
   148	        (fun x => directCombinedMeasuredRejectedMass D S types x.1 x.2) := by
   149	    rw [directLdBranchRejectionProbability_eq_avgOver,
   150	      ← directCombinedSample_indexPointParts_uniform D, Distribution.avgOver_map]
   151	    exact avgOver_mono _ _ _ fun sample =>
   152	      directRejectedMass_directCombinedStrategy_le_measured D S types sample
   153	  refine le_trans hstep ?_
   154	  rw [avgOver_uniform_prod (f := fun i pd =>
   155	      directCombinedMeasuredRejectedMass D S types i pd),
   156	    avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum, Fintype.card_fin]
   157	  have hmkNat : D.combined.m = D.m + D.k := rfl
   158	  have hmpos : 0 < D.m := Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one D.hm
   159	  have hkpos : 0 < D.k := Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one D.hk
   160	  have hcard : (D.m : ℝ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr hmpos.ne'
   161	  have hmk : ((D.combined.m : ℕ) : ℝ) = (D.m : ℝ) + (D.k : ℝ) := by
   162	    rw [hmkNat]
   163	    push_cast
   164	    ring
   165	  have hsum : ∑ i : Fin D.combined.m,
   166	      avgOver (uniformDistribution
   167	          ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)))
   168	        (fun pd => directCombinedMeasuredRejectedMass D S types i pd) =
   169	      (∑ j : Fin D.m, directLdIndexedBranchRejectionProbability D S types j) +
   170	        (D.k : ℝ) * directLdBranchRejectionProbability D S (.point, .point) := by
   171	    show ∑ i : Fin (D.m + D.k),
   172	        avgOver (uniformDistribution
   173	            ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)))
   174	          (fun pd => directCombinedMeasuredRejectedMass D S types i pd) = _
   175	    rw [Fin.sum_univ_add]
   176	    congr 1
   177	    · refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => ?_
   178	      exact avgOver_directCombinedMeasuredRejectedMass_pointVar D S types j
   179	    · have hconst : ∀ r : Fin D.k,
   180	          avgOver (uniformDistribution
   181	              ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)))
   182	            (fun pd => directCombinedMeasuredRejectedMass D S types
   183	              (Fin.natAdd D.m r) pd) =
   184	            directLdBranchRejectionProbability D S (.point, .point) := fun r =>
   185	        avgOver_directCombinedMeasuredRejectedMass_coefficientVar D S types r
   186	      simp [hconst, Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]
   187	  have hbranch : ∑ j : Fin D.m,
   188	      directLdIndexedBranchRejectionProbability D S types j =
   189	      (D.m : ℝ) * directLdBranchRejectionProbability D S types := by
   190	    rw [directLdBranchRejectionProbability_eq_avgOver_index,
   191	      avgOver_uniform_eq_inv_card_mul_sum, Fintype.card_fin]
   192	    field_simp
   193	  rw [hsum, hbranch, hmk]
   194	  have hB : 0 ≤ directLdBranchRejectionProbability D S types :=
   195	    directLdBranchRejectionProbability_nonneg D S types
   196	  have hP : 0 ≤ directLdBranchRejectionProbability D S (.point, .point) :=
   197	    directLdBranchRejectionProbability_nonneg D S (.point, .point)
   198	  have hm : (0 : ℝ) < D.m := by exact_mod_cast hmpos
   199	  have hk : (0 : ℝ) < D.k := by exact_mod_cast hkpos
   200	  rw [inv_mul_eq_div, div_le_iff₀ (by linarith)]
   201	  nlinarith [mul_nonneg hm.le hP, mul_nonneg hk.le hB]

   203	/-- `lem:ld-combined-value`, rejection form.  Both the directly indexed
   204	low-degree game with the original parameters and the one with the combined
   205	parameters weight their nine ordered type pairs uniformly, so averaging the
   206	branch-wise bound over the nine pairs bounds the rejection probability of the
   207	combined strategy by the rejection probability of the original strategy plus
   208	its point-versus-point branch; that branch is in turn at most nine times the
   209	rejection probability of the original strategy.  The universal constant of the
   210	source statement is therefore `10`. -/
   211	theorem directLdRejectionProbability_directCombinedStrategy_le
   212	    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) :
   213	    directLdRejectionProbability D.combined (directCombinedStrategy D S) ≤
   214	      10 * directLdRejectionProbability D S := by
   215	  have hle := directLdBranchRejectionProbability_directCombinedStrategy_le D S
   216	  have hnn := directLdBranchRejectionProbability_nonneg D S
   217	  rw [directLdRejectionProbability, directLdRejectionProbability,
   218	    avgOver_ldType_pair, avgOver_ldType_pair]
   219	  linarith [hle (.point, .point), hle (.point, .aline), hle (.point, .dline),
   220	    hle (.aline, .point), hle (.aline, .aline), hle (.aline, .dline),
   221	    hle (.dline, .point), hle (.dline, .aline), hle (.dline, .dline),
   222	    hnn (.point, .point), hnn (.point, .aline), hnn (.point, .dline),
   223	    hnn (.aline, .point), hnn (.aline, .aline), hnn (.aline, .dline),
   224	    hnn (.dline, .point), hnn (.dline, .aline), hnn (.dline, .dline)]
   225

   229	with probability at least `1 - 10 ε` in the directly indexed low-degree game

   233	    (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) (ε : ℝ) (hvalue : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) :
   234	    1 - 10 * ε ≤ (directCombinedStrategy D S).value := by
   235	  have hcomb := directLdRejectionProbability_directCombinedStrategy_le D S
   236	  rw [directLdRejectionProbability_eq_one_sub_value,
   237	    directLdRejectionProbability_eq_one_sub_value] at hcomb
   238	  linarith

     5	/-!
     6	# The recovery of the polynomial-tuple measurements
     7	
     8	`lem:ld-combining-recovery` turns the three conclusions of `lem:ld-soundness`
     9	for the combined strategy at the combined parameters into the three conclusions
    10	for the original strategy at the original parameters, by post-processing the
    11	measurements of the combined game with the recovery map of
    12	`def:ld-combining-map`.
    13	
    14	The two point relations are wired by the abstract transport of
    15	`Transport.Combining.RecoveryDefect`.  At a point `(u, α)` of the combined
    16	space the point measurement of the combined strategy is the point measurement
    17	of the original strategy at `u` post-processed by the combination with
    18	coefficients `α`, and the polynomial measurement of the combined game read at
    19	that point is the same measurement read through the recovery map and then
    20	combined with the same coefficients; the two families therefore differ only on
    21	the discrepancy event of `Recovery`, whose average is `(m + k) d / q`.  The
    22	uniform law on the combined space is the product of the uniform laws on the
    23	point part and on the combining part, which is the reindexing along
    24	`directCombinedPointEquiv`.
    25	
    26	The polynomial relation is data processing: the recovered measurements are
    27	post-processings of the measurements of the combined game.
    28	
    29	## Main statements
    30	
    31	* `directCombinedPointEquiv` — the point of the combined space with given
    32	  point and combining parts, as an identification.
    33	* `directCombinedRecovery_relation_one` — the first conclusion.
    34	* `directCombinedRecovery_relation_two` — the second conclusion.
    35	* `directCombinedRecovery_relation_three` — the third conclusion.
    36	
    37	## References
    38	
    39	* `references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex:1440-1503`
    40	* `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`
    41	* `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:617-680`
    42	-/

    57	/-- The identification of a point of the combined space with the pair formed by
    58	its point part and its combining part. -/
    59	def directCombinedPointEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
    60	    ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) × (Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D)) ≃
    61	      (Fin D.combined.m → DirectScalarQ D) where
    62	  toFun z := combinedPoint z.1 z.2
    63	  invFun z := (directCombinedPointPart D z, directCombinedCoefficientPart D z)
    64	  left_inv z := by
    65	    have h1 : directCombinedPointPart D (combinedPoint z.1 z.2) = z.1 :=
    66	      directCombinedPointPart_combinedPoint D z.1 z.2
    67	    have h2 : directCombinedCoefficientPart D (combinedPoint z.1 z.2) = z.2 :=
    68	      directCombinedCoefficientPart_combinedPoint D z.1 z.2
    69	    show (directCombinedPointPart D (combinedPoint z.1 z.2),
    70	      directCombinedCoefficientPart D (combinedPoint z.1 z.2)) = z
    71	    rw [h1, h2]
    72	  right_inv z := by
    73	    funext i
    74	    show Sum.elim (fun j => z (finSumFinEquiv (Sum.inl j)))
    75	      (fun r => z (finSumFinEquiv (Sum.inr r))) (finSumFinEquiv.symm i) = z i
    76	    rcases hi : finSumFinEquiv.symm i with j | r
    77	    · simp only [Sum.elim_inl]
    78	      rw [← hi, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
    79	    · simp only [Sum.elim_inr]
    80	      rw [← hi, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]

    82	@[simp] theorem directCombinedPointEquiv_apply (D : DirectLdParams)
    83	    (z : (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) × (Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D)) :
    84	    directCombinedPointEquiv D z = combinedPoint z.1 z.2 := rfl

    88	/-- On a point question of the combined game the combined strategy measures the
    89	point question of the original game at the point part. -/
    90	private theorem directCombinedMeasuredQuestion_point (D : DirectLdParams)
    91	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (α : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) :
    92	    directCombinedMeasuredQuestion D
    93	        (directLdPointQuestionOf D.combined (combinedPoint u α)) =
    94	      directLdPointQuestionOf D u := by
    95	  show directLdPointQuestionOf D
    96	    (directCombinedPointPart D (combinedPoint u α)) = _
    97	  rw [directCombinedPointPart_combinedPoint]

    99	/-- On a point question of the combined game the combined answer, read as a
   100	one-component tuple of scalars, is the combination of the measured point answer
   101	with the combining part of the sampled point. -/
   102	private theorem directCombinedPointAnswerMap_comp (D : DirectLdParams)
   103	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (α : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) :
   104	    (fun a : DirectLdAnswer D => directLdPointValuesOrZero D.combined
   105	        (directCombinedAnswerMap D
   106	          (directLdPointQuestionOf D.combined (combinedPoint u α)) a)) =
   107	      fun a : DirectLdAnswer D => (fun _ : Fin D.combined.k =>
   108	        ∑ r : Fin D.k, α r * directLdPointValuesOrZero D a r) := by
   109	  funext a
   110	  cases a with
   111	  | pointVals b =>
   112	      funext j
   113	      show (∑ r : Fin D.k,
   114	        directCombinedCoefficientPart D (combinedPoint u α) r * b r) = _
   115	      rw [directCombinedCoefficientPart_combinedPoint]
   116	      rfl
   117	  | alinePolys g =>
   118	      funext j
   119	      show (0 : DirectScalarQ D) =
   120	        ∑ r : Fin D.k, α r * (0 : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) r
   121	      simp
   122	  | dlinePolys g =>
   123	      funext j
   124	      show (0 : DirectScalarQ D) =
   125	        ∑ r : Fin D.k, α r * (0 : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) r
   126	      simp

   129	
   130	/-- A constant function on a one-element index set equals a function exactly
   131	when the value of the function at the unique index is the constant. -/
   132	private theorem const_eq_fun_iff {ι K : Type*} [Unique ι] (c : K) (h : ι → K) :
   133	    ((fun _ : ι => c) = h) ↔ h default = c := by
   134	  constructor
   135	  · intro hh
   136	    rw [← hh]
   137	  · intro hh
   138	    funext i
   139	    rw [Unique.eq_default i, hh]

   141	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
   142	/-- The discrepancy estimate of `Recovery` in the shape required by the
   143	transport: for a fixed point, a fixed point answer and a fixed outcome of the
   144	combined game, the probability over the combining vector that the recovered
   145	tuple of values differs from the point answer while the outcome read at the
   146	combined point agrees with the combination is at most the local bound. -/
   147	private theorem directCombinedRecoveryEvent_transport (D : DirectLdParams)
   148	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (b : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D)
   149	    (p : DirectPolyTuple D.combined) :
   150	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D)) (fun α =>
   151	        if evalDirectPolyTupleAt u (directTupleOfCombinedTuple D p) ≠ b ∧
   152	            (fun _ : Fin D.combined.k => ∑ r : Fin D.k, α r * b r) =
   153	              evalDirectPolyTupleAt (D := D.combined) (combinedPoint u α) p then
   154	          (1 : ℝ) else 0) ≤
   155	      directCombinedRecoveryLocalBound D (p default) u := by
   156	  classical
   157	  refine le_trans (le_of_eq (avgOver_congr _ _ _ fun α => ?_))
   158	    (directCombinedRecoveryEvent_avg_le D (p default) u b)
   159	  exact if_congr (and_congr Iff.rfl (const_eq_fun_iff _
   160	    (evalDirectPolyTupleAt (D := D.combined) (combinedPoint u α) p))) rfl rfl
   161	
   162	/-! ## The two point relations -/
   163	
   164	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
   165	/-- First conclusion of `lem:ld-combining-recovery`: the point measurement of
   166	the original strategy is consistent with the recovered polynomial tuple
   167	evaluated at the sampled point, up to the defect of the first conclusion for
   168	the combined strategy plus `(m + k) d / q`. -/
   169	theorem directCombinedRecovery_relation_one (D : DirectLdParams)
   170	    (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
   171	    (GB : DirectPolyMeasTuple D.combined S.ιB) :
   172	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   173	        (fun u outcome => heteroKron
   174	          (((S.A (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
   175	            (directLdPointValuesOrZero D)).effect outcome) 1)
   176	        (fun u outcome => heteroKron 1
   177	          (((GB.postprocess (directTupleOfCombinedTuple D)).postprocess
   178	            (evalDirectPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome))
   179	        S.ψ ≤
   180	      consistencyDefect
   181	          (uniformDistribution (Fin D.combined.m → DirectScalarQ D))
   182	          (fun z outcome => heteroKron
   183	            ((((directCombinedStrategy D S).A
   184	              (directLdPointQuestionOf D.combined z)).postprocess
   185	                (directLdPointValuesOrZero D.combined)).effect outcome) 1)
   186	          (fun z outcome => heteroKron 1
   187	            ((GB.postprocess (evalDirectPolyTupleAt (D := D.combined) z)).effect
   188	              outcome))
   189	          S.ψ +
   190	        ((D.combined.m * D.d : ℕ) : ℝ) / D.q := by
   191	  classical
